places.notes: [Wagashi · Kenninji, a temple supplier in a back lane] A tiny wagashi shop on a quiet lane by Kenninji, supplier to Kenninji and Kodaiji: the small dorayaki called Mikasa (¥180), a monaka filled after you order so the shell stays crisp (¥180), and seasonal fresh sweets from ¥300. Phone ahead — booked orders come first, and fresh sweets need a day's notice; walk-ins often find things sold out. Tabelog says it is under renovation and taking phone orders. Cash only.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed in the sources) · Per the operator’s Tabelog text: founded in 1932; a favourite of Kenninji since its founding and, by reputation, also a supplier to Kodaiji; trusted by Gion teahouses. A March 2026 reviewer gives 2026 as its 94th year; a November 2026 reviewer gives the founding as 1927. Tabelog Japanese-sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 and 2026, Sweets WEST 2018–2020 and 2022, Sweets 2017. · Mikasa; monaka; seasonal jō-namagashi.
places.gfd: Ask. Mochi and bean-paste sweets such as botamochi and warabi mochi may suit, but the Mikasa is a small dorayaki (a baked batter cake) and the monaka has a wafer shell; no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Bean-paste and mochi sweets such as botamochi, warabi mochi and monaka may suit, but the Mikasa batter and the other sweets have no published ingredient list (2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Craft beer & Italian · Nishiki, Ichijoji Brewery's pub] Ichijoji Brewery's taproom just north of Nishiki Market, renovated in 2026 with an Italian menu: beers from Belgian wheat to a yuzu weiss and an English-style IPA, then Kyoto yuba potato salad, spare ribs stewed in the brewery's own beer, octopus in red wine, wagyu tagliata. A three-beer, three-dish tasting set (¥2,500) is the easy way in. Reviewers like the beer and the panna cotta; two found the high chairs uncomfortable, and some found the prices on the high side. English menu. Open from noon at weekends; closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Pub of Ichijoji Brewery (Kyoto); no person is named · Tabelog lists the former name BEER PUB ICHI-YA; a March 2026 regular found it renovated, the menu much more food-led and the Red Ale gone. Reviewers describe it as the pub of Kyoto’s Ichijoji Brewery (December 2025; May 2026), and a November 2025 reviewer refers to a second location. Opened 8 August 2016 (Tabelog). · Ichijoji Brewery craft beer; beer-stewed spare ribs; tasting set.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free in practice: a craft-beer pub (beer is barley or wheat) whose food includes zeppole (fried bread), croquettes, pizza and ravioli; no gluten information is published (Tabelog menu, October 2026; 2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, and olives, smoked nuts, sauerkraut, green salad, grilled black-soybean edamame and fries are on the menu, but nothing is marked vegan (Tabelog menu, October 2026).

places.cu: Chicken and quail at a 10-seat counter, grilled over charcoal and served off the skewer, cut into bite-size pieces on a plate (2026 reviews) · chicken sashimi platter: breast, gizzard, white liver, heart, kombu-cured breast; white liver sashimi with sesame oil; chicken-thigh tataki with yuzu pepper and ponzu (July–October 2026) · grills: grilled quail thigh, neck, thigh, tsukune with ginger, gizz…
places.notes: [Chicken · Shijo Kawabata, a 10-seat chicken counter by the Kamo River] A narrow ten-seat counter on Kawabata-dori just north of Shijo, where the master grills chicken and quail over charcoal and serves it off the skewer in bite-size pieces. Start with the chicken sashimi — white liver with sesame oil, heart, kombu-cured breast — or the rare thigh tataki; then quail thigh, gizzard, red liver and grilled vegetables such as Kamo eggplant; finish with an oyakodon soaked in dashi. Good sake, including Aramasa. Almost always full: book, or ask for an hour's slot. Bills ran about ¥6,000–15,000 a head in 2026. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Master (主) at the grill, with young staff (August 2026); not named · Per an August 2026 Japanese review: the master holds the grill at the far end of the long counter and young staff work briskly under the master’s direction; the cooking is not on skewers, and the heat is well managed; the staff came to call the reviewer, who had arrived early and was waiting by the Kamo River. A regular of ten years (January 2024) and others describe it as always booked. Tabelog Chicken "Tabelog 100" 2025. · Chicken sashimi (white liver); thigh tataki; oyakodon.
places.gfd: Ask. Chicken sashimi comes with sesame oil, ponzu or yuzu pepper, and the grills and oyakodon use sauces and dashi; no gluten information is published (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a chicken and quail house; grilled vegetables are on the menu, but the soup is chicken and the oyakodon uses dashi (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 17:30–22:00; Thursday 18:00–22:00; closed Wednesday; hours may change (Tabelog). places.cu: Kyoto shop of Ginza’s Star Bar, a bar built around ice: hand-cut clear ice and its own craft ice 洛氷 made from Kyoto spring waters under an ice-making licence (official site) · cocktails with Japanese flavours, e.g. Japanese Martini Matcha ¥2,300, Sakura Fubuki ¥2,300, Matcha Hopper, Yuzu Mule; cocktails about ¥2,000–3,000 (2026 reviews) · kakigori of 洛氷 shaved with a SWAN cygne machine, with matc…
places.notes: [Bar & kakigori · Kiyamachi, Ginza's Star Bar in a Kyoto alley] The Kyoto branch of Ginza's Star Bar, down an alley between Kiyamachi and Pontocho: a dim, Japanese-styled room with a tea set at its centre, where the kimono-clad master works alone. Everything turns on ice — hand-cut clear ice for highballs, and the bar's own 洛氷 from Kyoto spring water, shaved into kakigori (¥2,500) with matcha whisked at the counter or yuzu syrup. Come before 19:00 to skip the ¥2,200 table charge. Cocktails run ¥2,000–3,000. Cards only. One May 2026 visitor found the charge poor value and the staff absorbed in a computer.
places.chef: 松田 高雅 · Owner (the invoice holder); a May 2026 review describes the master, in a kimono, managing everything solo · Per Tabelog: a directly managed shop of STAR BAR GINZA in Ginza 1-chome, Tokyo. Per the official site: four STAR BAR shops (Ginza, Namiki, Kyoto, Hibiya Midtown); Star Bar made ice the star of the bar, uses three kinds of ice frozen in different ways, and the Kyoto shop makes craft ice (洛氷) from Kyoto spring waters under the only ice-making licence in Kyoto city; by day in summer the Kyoto shop is a kakigori shop. The invoice register lists an individual, 松田 高雅, for the Kyoto shop’s invoice number. Tabelog Bar "Tabelog 100" 2022. Opened 11 July 2016. · Per the official site: hand-cut ice is pursued for function as well as beauty, down to water quality and the theory of freezing. · Kakigori of 洛氷; matcha cocktails; hand-cut ice.
places.gfd: Ask. A cocktail bar: drinks, kakigori with matcha, yuzu or fermented-milk syrups, smoked nuts and dried fruit; no gluten information is published (Tabelog menu, April 2026).

places.notes: [Donuts & café · Shinkyogoku, organic donuts under bamboo baskets] A large donut factory-café a minute from Kawaramachi Station, under a dome of 572 traditional hexagon-weave bamboo baskets designed by Kengo Kuma's office. The koe brand fries its donuts in rice oil from organic and natural ingredients: try the plain koe donut (¥260) or the wasanbon cruller to take away, or sit down for a 'donut melt' eaten with knife and fork (from ¥1,100). Seasonal dango donuts change with the season. From 8:00 there's a French-toast morning plate, or a ¥500 coffee-and-donut set. Spacious, with Wi-Fi and outlets. Daily 8:00–20:00.
places.chef: koe brand café; Tabelog gives Stripe International’s PR department as the press contact; no person is named · Per the official site: an experiential donut factory serving freshly made donuts with knife and fork; ingredients chosen by three keywords, organic, natural origin and local production, made by hand in the shop as far as possible. The interior by Kengo Kuma & Associates covers a dome with 572 traditional hexagon-weave (六ツ目編み) bamboo baskets using Arashiyama bamboo; artist Yu Nagaba designed the goods, with Shun Kawakami as brand and art director. Opened 21 March 2019 (Tabelog). places.notes: [Fruit parlour · Shijo-Omiya, the fruit sandwich] The parlour of Yaoiso, a Shijo-Omiya fruit shop founded in 1869, which added a fruit parlour in 1972 and moved it into this room next door in 2013: soft cream (lightly sweet to some reviewers, quite sweet to one) and generous seasonal fruit in soft bread (a set with mixed juice about ¥900–1,000), parfaits, and set plates of peaches or mangoes in season. Sweets WEST Tabelog 100 2026. One September 2026 diner found the fruit cut too small and the staff unfriendly. Daily 9:30–17:00; sandwiches also to take away.
places.chef: Parlour of the fruit shop Yaoiso (no owner named) · Per the official site: a fruit specialist founded in Meiji 2 (1869), selling gift fruit and household fruit, known for Okayama white peaches in the summer gift season and Saga Sagahonoka strawberries in winter; a fruit parlour was added in Showa 47 (1972), and its signature fruit sandwich is widely loved; a certified fruit-adviser shop, with a governor’s award as an old Kyoto business. A second shop with a parlour stands on Karasuma-dori north of Imadegawa, next to Doshisha University (official site). Tabelog gives the opening day of this parlour as 23 May 2013; a September 2026 review says it began on the second floor of the main shop in 1972 and moved here in 2013. Tabelog Sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2022, 2023 and 2026. · Fruit sandwich; seasonal fruit parfaits.

places.notes: [Standing bar · Kamigyo, a lumber yard at night] By day a family lumber yard, by night a standing bar: the fourth-generation 井倉康博 turned a three-tatami office into a counter and the car park into tables (Serai 2017). Salt-seared bonito flamed outside (¥1,500), tuna and myoga rolls, grilled hamo, a ¥90 potato salad, and sake recommended out loud. A queue forms before 17:00, and the giant crab of November–December draws longer ones; popular dishes sell out. Tachinomi Tabelog 100 2025. Cash only, no bookings; Mon–Sat 17:00–22:00.
places.chef: 井倉康博 · Owner (fourth generation of the family lumber business), per Serai 2017 · Serai (5 October 2017): as the name says, the family has long made its living in the lumber trade; the fourth generation, 井倉康博 (then 40), could not give up a dream of running a restaurant, and five years earlier had opened a night-only standing bar while carrying on the family business, turning a three-tatami office into the counter and the car park into the shop; seven or eight people fit inside, and drinking outside in the autumn wind is part of the fun. Serai then listed house oil sardines (made only when large sardines come in), crab-miso ruibe ¥800, sake from ¥600 a gō, and closing on Sundays and holidays. A September 2026 diner heard that the lumber business, once run by the owner’s father, is no longer very active and the bar is now the main focus. Tabelog tachinomi "Tabelog 100" 2025. · Salt-seared bonito tataki; grilled hamo; winter crab.

The bar is known for "Nise Denki Bran", the fake brandy drink from Tomihiko Morimi's Kyoto novels; there are original cocktails with a house tea liqueur, the classics, whisky and cigars. Cocktails about ¥1,600. Open nightly 17:00–2:00, which makes it a late stop when Pontocho closes. Smoking allowed. A March 2025 visitor found the bartender fluent in English.

Regular curries run ¥1,300–1,500, with a monthly special such as a salmon rare-katsu curry (¥1,980 large) or a dashi curry katsu don; finish with a craft cola or a lemongrass sour. Most reviewers find the spicing aromatic rather than hot (the bone-in mutton curry has more kick). Listed on the same website as the biryani shop INDIA GATE. Open every day; Thursday until 15:00.

places.notes: [Obanzai izakaya · Kiyamachi, Kyoto home cooking late] A small counter izakaya just off Kiyamachi, open until midnight, where an open kitchen turns out Kyoto obanzai — eggplant ohitashi, potato salad — and seasonal plates: hamo sashimi in summer, scallop potato salad, mentaiko chicken wings, Saikyo-miso spring rolls, and an egg rice to finish. Local sake, with a deep list of Tamagawa. Reviewers single out friendly, attentive staff who explain the dishes and suggest sake off the list. Courses ¥4,400–5,500 for groups; book ahead. Smoking allowed.

places.notes: [Chinese · Kawaramachi Nijo, Chef Wei's townhouse by the canal] Creative Chinese cooking in a century-old townhouse facing the old Ichinofunairi boat landing on the Takase River, with private rooms: Chef Wei blends the eight Chinese cuisines with Japanese and Western techniques and Kyoto produce, on the principle that food is medicine. The braised shark fin is the signature; light, ungreasy courses run from appetiser platters to fried rice and a huge mango shaved ice. Lunch around ¥6,000–8,000; dinner courses ¥11,000–14,850, plus 10%. Book a course; closed Sunday. Tabelog Chinese WEST 100 2021, 2024.

places.notes: [Sushi izakaya · Kiyamachi, a hidden alley counter] A 20-seat sushi izakaya tucked into a narrow alley between Kiyamachi and Pontocho, run by a couple, with nostalgic anime stickers on one wall. Sushi on red-and-white-vinegar rice comes by the piece or as six- and ten-piece sets, alongside small dishes such as oyster namero and kimchi lotus root, meat dishes, and sake from around Japan; ingredients change daily, so book early and ask for favourites in advance. Service can be slow when busy. Smoking allowed; ¥500 charge each; cash only. Late on Friday and Saturday; closed Wednesday.

places.cu: Old wagashi shop with essentially one sweet, 味噌松風 (miso matsukaze): a castella-like sheet of wheat flour, sugar and white Saikyo miso, sprinkled with sesame, moist and chewy, with a sweet-savoury miso top (2026 reviews) · small ¥1,000, large ¥1,200 (Tabelog); cut ends for home use ¥300 (June and September 2026)
places.notes: [Wagashi · Imperial Palace, one sweet for centuries] A noren-hung shop south of the Imperial Palace's Sakaimachi gate that sells one thing: miso matsukaze, a moist, castella-like cake of flour, sugar, white Saikyo miso and sesame — one of Kyoto's three famous matsukaze, per a reviewer. Reviewers in 2026 were greeted by an elderly lady in the small tatami-floored shop. Book a day ahead (large ¥1,200; small ¥1,000, a few sold on the day), or ask for the ¥300 bag of cut ends. Eat within about three days. Daily 9:30–15:00, cash only.
places.chef: Family shop; no one is named in the sources · An April 2026 reviewer calls it a historic wagashi shop established in the Shoo era and favoured by the Imperial Palace and Daitoku-ji; a July 2026 reviewer says it has been in business for 360 years. Reviewers describe an elderly woman, apparently the head of the shop, with a young male staff member in the small tatami-floored shop. A July 2026 reviewer calls it one of Kyoto’s three famous matsukaze shops. Tabelog Japanese sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023, 2026. · Miso matsukaze.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: miso matsukaze is made from wheat flour, sugar, white miso and sesame (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Reviewers list only wheat flour, sugar, white (Saikyo) miso and sesame, and one notes it is egg-free; the shop publishes no ingredient list (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 9:30–15:00 daily; hours may change (Tabelog). Takeaway only (Tabelog). places.notes: [Wagashi · Teramachi Oike, Oike senbei] A long-established wagashi house on the corner of Teramachi and Oike, opposite Honnoji, best known for Oike senbei — pale, sugar-glazed wafers that dissolve like snow (¥1,350 for a tin of 22, per MAPPLE). The shelves also hold Tsuki, modelled on the door pulls of Katsura Imperial Villa, 小倉山 yokan and seasonal sweets, such as Daimonji-themed ones in August. One reviewer found the senbei has grown pricey. Takeaway only. 8:00–18:00; Tabelog says closed Wednesday and Sunday, but a reviewer found it open on a Sunday in November 2026.
places.chef: Long-established wagashi house; no one is named in the sources · MAPPLE gives the founding as 1832 (天保3); an August 2026 reviewer says it has been around since 1803. MAPPLE lists Oike senbei, Tsuki (after the door pulls of Katsura Imperial Villa) and 小倉山 yokan. A July 2026 reviewer who has loved the senbei since childhood found it has become quite pricey and that a favourite seasonal sweet, Toki no Nagare, is no longer made. Tabelog Japanese sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023, 2026. · Oike senbei; Tsuki.
places.gfd: Ask. Oike senbei tastes of egg and wheat (August 2026); bean-paste sweets, yokan and kudzu sweets may be wheat-free, but no ingredient lists are published (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Yokan and bean-paste sweets are plant-based in principle, but the Oike senbei contains egg and Honohono is a baked sweet; no ingredient lists are published (2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Wagyu & Kyoto courses · Pontocho, on the Kamo River] A restaurant at the back of a Pontocho building that looks over the Kamo River toward Higashiyama and the Minamiza theatre, with a riverside kawadoko terrace from May to September. Courses pair Kyoto starters — yuba, yudofu, hamo shabu — with lobster, abalone and black wagyu grilled on Fuji lava stones (about ¥9,500); in winter, wagyu sukiyaki (¥7,000 set). Reviews range from delighted to disappointed. 17:00–23:00, closed Monday.

places.notes: [Udon izakaya · Kiyamachi, open until 7 am] A small, worn, friendly late-night spot in the lane between Kiyamachi and Pontocho, open from 19:00 to 7:00 every night — the last stop after drinks. The curry udon (thin, firm noodles in a mild, dashi-rich curry) is what most people order; there are also egg-drop udon, katsudon, ramen and teppan snacks. Orders by QR code. Cash only; smoking allowed.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed in the sources) · Per an April 2023 review: a long-running shop famous for its curry udon, which had recently opened another place on Marutamachi in front of the prefectural office. Two seatings (18:00 and 20:00), booked on TableCheck; expect about ¥10,000–15,000 with drinks. Cash only; closed Monday.

The staple is the back-fat soy sauce ramen (¥960 in October 2026) — lighter than it looks, with thin straight noodles — alongside a lemon salt ramen and curry mazesoba. Reviews are mixed: some praise the kara-age bowl and the value, while a November 2025 visitor, who knew the Kokura shop, found the fried rice cold and the ramen bland on a busy night. Cash only. Hours are not published.

places.notes: [Yakitori · Shijo Kawaramachi, Kyo Akajidori over binchotan] A retro-modern yakitori izakaya down a narrow "eel's bed" building a couple of minutes from Kawaramachi Stn, using only female Kyo Akajidori chickens grilled over binchotan and salted with Guérande salt. Start with the aburi-yaki (thigh ¥1,320), then skewers from ¥253 — the tsukune with Ranno egg yolk and the white liver (when it hasn't sold out) are favourites — and finish with the oyakodon, which one regular calls the best anywhere. Courses with all-you-can-drink from ¥4,000. Open to midnight, to 1:00 on Friday and Saturday; ¥330 service charge.
places.chef: Kitchen unnamed; the official menu says the beef-tendon doteyaki has been made since training days in Osaka · Per the official site: the restaurant uses only female Kyo Akajidori, grills over binchotan for a crisp outside and juicy inside, and settled on French Guérande salt after a long search; yakitori is served with salt by default; the chicken is grilled before it goes into the oyakodon, made with Ranno eggs. Tabelog gives the opening as 25 February 2015. · Kyo Akajidori aburi-yaki and yakitori; oyakodon.

places.notes: [Steak · Gion, a 1962 steakhouse in a former teahouse] A Gion steakhouse in a remodelled ochaya south of Shijo, entered under a noren and red lantern, with a vermilion counter that faces the griddle and a small garden. The house steak is the heart of the black wagyu fillet, cut thick and steamed slowly over garlic so it is soft enough to barely need chewing; it comes with garlic rice and a triangle of pudding. The lunch course (¥8,800, 80 g fillet) is the way in; dinner courses start at ¥32,000. Upstairs there is a zashiki with a stage for parties with geiko and maiko. Reservation only; closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Italian yoshoku · Nijo, a menchi-katsu worth the trip] A renovated machiya a short walk from JR Nijo Stn where chef Noro — trained in Italy, then at Hotel Granvia Kyoto's La Risata and at Yoshoku Ogata — cooks Italian-based yoshoku with Japanese touches. The signature is a juicy menchi-katsu of Ozaki beef and Kofuku pork under demi-glace and balsamic; the menchi-katsu lunch set (¥3,300) comes with a soup and a vegetable plate that reviewers rave about. Dinner is a ¥10,000 course or à la carte with handmade pasta, risotto and the day's fish. Lunch fills up — book. Closed Monday.

places.notes: [French bistro · Gokomachi-Ayanokoji, a little rabbit] A 15-seat bistro behind a red fence south of Fuji Daimaru, open since July 2009, whose site likens its guests to a hungry little rabbit: French regional home cooking with French wines — lunch courses at ¥3,000 and ¥4,000, a ¥5,500 dinner menu and about 70 à la carte dishes from escargots and boudin noir to Hino venison crépinette with foie gras, and tarte Tatin. Reviewers in 2026 praise the owner-chef's warm service. Closed Wednesday; café hours 14:30–17:30.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed), per 2026 reviews · The official site describes a shop where people who love to eat gather, always smiling like a rabbit that never stops munching, and serves house "a little rye" bread. Tabelog gives the opening day as 5 July 2009 and describes traditional French cooking in bistro style, with vegetables, meat and fish from Miyama. The official information page names the current venison supplier, ジビエ堂 in Hino, Shiga, and sells party hors d’oeuvres and rice from Keihoku farmers. A May 2026 diner found the owner-chef attentive and was photographed by the owner on leaving; another the same month found the owner kind. · Per the official site: a shop where food-lovers gather, never without a smile, like a hungry little rabbit. · Venison crépinette with foie gras; tarte Tatin; regional French dishes.

Praised by food writers and on local TV, so it is often full; book. No prices on the wall menu; most pay ¥6,000–7,000. Cash only; closed Wednesday and Sunday.

Regulars chat at the counter; solo diners are welcome. Seen on Kazuhiko Ota's TV show. Cash only; smoking at the counter only. Hours are not published; call ahead.

Founder 田口 茂雄 was honoured as a Contemporary Master Craftsman (2017) and received the Medal with Yellow Ribbon (2020); after the founder's death in 2021, 田口 弥生 has run the shop with a son. places.notes: [Kaiseki · Kiyamachi, a 1928 ryotei famous for suppon] A sukiya-style ryotei between the Takase River and the Kamo, founded in 1928 by 栗栖 熊三郎 at a five-seat counter and now run by the family's fourth generation, Junichi Kurisu (from September 2026), a sommelier who travelled some 80 countries. The kaiseki is 'monmo' — ingredients served as they are — and its signature is suppon, in the 丸吸 soup or the 丸鍋 hot pot. It was among the first Kyoto ryotei with halal certification (2014) and serves kosher and vegan kaiseki on request. Courses from ¥22,000 plus 15% service; riverside kawadoko in summer. Booking required; closed Sunday.
places.chef: Junichi Kurisu (栗栖 純一) · 4th-generation executive chef and owner from September 2026 (official site), Sommelier: A.S.I. Sommelier Diploma, WSET Level 3 Wines and Sake, J.S.A. Two Michelin stars in the Kyoto/Osaka 2010 guide; one star in the 2024 guide. Lunch ¥10,000, dinner ¥20,000 (+10%). There is a sister shop in Tokyo Midtown. Closed Monday.

Steak, grilled shabu-shabu and teppan sukiyaki come together in the ¥30,000 three-way course; the lunch steak starts at ¥5,000 for 100 g. places.chef: 三嶋太郎 · Fifth-generation head (五代目主人), per the official site · Per the official site: the founder 三嶌兼吉, who served a court-noble’s samurai, learned gyunabe in Nagasaki together with the founder’s wife てい and opened Mishima Tei here on Teramachi-Sanjo in Meiji 6 (1873); the sukiya interior — garden, railings, ceilings, lattices — is mostly as it was at the founding; the house selects black wagyu from across Japan regardless of origin and ages it in its own way, cooking the sukiyaki on electric heaters that act like charcoal. The fifth generation, 三嶋太郎, refined the secret warishita, began training in Japanese cuisine, tea and ikebana eight years before the page was written, and devised the kaiseki-style Hana course with appetisers, sweets and usucha. A sister restaurant, 翁樹庵, is introduced on the site. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2019; Hot Pot "Tabelog 100" 2024 and 2026. · Per the official site: keeping the good things of old Kyoto, which is now harder than making new ones; the fifth generation aims to keep evolving while carrying on the tradition. · Sukiyaki of black wagyu with the house warishita.

places.notes: [Issen yoshoku · Shijo-Nawate, Gion's late-night snack] The 100-seat Gion shop that revived issen yoshoku, the pre-war flour snack seen as okonomiyaki's ancestor: a thin dashi batter folded over Kujo leek, egg, konnyaku, chikuwa and wagyu, sauced sweet, normal or spicy — the only dish, ¥950. Inside, tongue-in-cheek risqué ema, figures and kimono-clad mannequins at the tables play on the old pleasure quarter. Open daily from 11:00 to 1:00 (3:00 on Saturdays and days before holidays); a counter in Takashimaya and mail order too.
places.chef: 株式会社壹錢洋食 (founding president 木下辰雄, per the official site) · Per the official site: issen yoshoku faded in the late Showa era as modern okonomiyaki took over; the company’s first president, 木下辰雄, set out to revive it and make it better, choosing Kujo leek, egg and domestic wagyu, working on the seasoned konnyaku, dashi and sauce, and using shredded nori so that it would not cling to the teeth. It was first sold in a small shop by the Shirakawa in Gion, popular with maiko, geiko and entertainers, then moved to the larger shop at Shijo-Nawate, where the playful decor — saucy ema and figures satirising love in the pleasure quarter — became a sight in itself; mail order on Rakuten from April 2011. The site lists two shops today, the Gion honten and Takashimaya Kyoto, and sales at Mitsui Outlet Park Shiga Ryuo. Okonomiyaki "Tabelog 100" 2018. · Per the official site: "that nostalgic taste once more — and even better." · Issen Yoshoku (one dish only).

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Nishijin, a 300-year-old ryotei of court cuisine] A ryotei on Inokuma-dori in Nishijin that began in 1722 as a sake brewery, 萬屋, and later became the restaurant 萬亀楼; it formally carries on the Imperial Court's Ikama-ryu ceremonial knife school and yusoku-ryori, and the present head is the tenth generation. Meals are served in private tatami rooms over a garden: seasonal courses with hamo and live-grilled ayu in summer, crab and karasumi in winter, and a kago bento at lunch. Courses run about ¥30,000–40,000 a head with about 20% added; at events there may be shikibocho and maiko. Book ahead.

places.notes: [French · Kawaramachi-Takatsuji, a seafood French in the attic] A twelve-seat attic restaurant west of Kawaramachi-Takatsuji, decorated after the sea of the south of France and of the owner-chef's home, where Shingo Giki cooks French food built on Japanese seafood. places.notes: [Yakitori & oyakodon · Gion Shirakawa, a Meiji chicken family's casual shop] The casual counter of 鳥新, a Gion chicken house whose family traces itself to the mid-Meiji era and whose earlier shops appear in Ryōma ga Yuku and Tanizaki. At lunch it serves only oyakodon — the old geisha-delivery recipe, egg set round a raw yolk with Kujo onion on Tsuruga rice, with house pickles and miso soup; at night, a ¥2,200 skewer omakase with chicken soup. Cash only; smoking allowed; closed Thursday.
places.chef: Owner, fourth generation by the family’s count (official site); unnamed · Per the official site of 鳥新: founded about 120 years ago in the mid-Meiji era, with the present owner "said to be the fourth generation" though without firm proof; related 鳥新 shops once stood by Shijo Kobashi, on Kawaramachi, Teramachi and Shinkyogoku, and the family traces bird dealing back to Oda Nobunaga’s time; the Shijo Kobashi shop is thought to be the one in the last scene of Shiba Ryōtarō’s "Ryōma ga Yuku"; Tanizaki Jun’ichirō wrote of the Teramachi shop (Bungei Shunjū, 1924) and ate at Nawate; mizutaki came to dominate over sukiyaki from about Showa 40. The oyakodon was made for delivery to geiko, maiko and Gion households from the late Meiji, delivery ended around 1955, and the dish was revived for lunch at とり新 after some fifty years (official site). An August 2025 reviewer found the owner a person of few words who wore very tall geta; an April 2026 reviewer calls the house Meiji-era. · Per the official site: "町の普通の店" — an ordinary neighbourhood shop, a secret little space in Kyoto. · Oyakodon; yakitori omakase.

places.notes: [Ryokan kaiseki · Fuyacho, one of Kyoto's grand old inns] A historic inn near Oike, in the inn trade since 1861 (the house since 1818), whose holly crest is on everything and whose guests have included Kawabata Yasunari: seasonal Kyoto kaiseki in your room or a dining room, with fine old tableware. You can come just to eat — dinner for two or more, lunch for groups of ten — by booking ahead; allergies and vegetarian requests need three days' notice. Expect ¥20,000–50,000 a head. A 2026 Michelin Key hotel and Relais & Châteaux member.

places.notes: [French · Marutamachi, Chef Alexey Moko's townhouse] A modern French restaurant in a renovated Kyoto townhouse with a central counter, a courtyard and a storehouse, where Chef Alexey Moko — trained at Taillevent and in London hotels — cooks Japanese ingredients aged and fermented in-house: week-aged fish with koji or sourdough-miso sauces, game, and a sourdough loaf with butter people ask for again and again. Lunch ¥9,000, dinner ¥22,000, with natural-wine pairings. Families welcome, with a kids' menu. Michelin one star, per reviewers. Closed Sunday and Monday.

The eight-dish omakase (¥8,800 in November 2025) moves through the seasons: a 20-ingredient salad, vegetables with a heshiko sauce, hamo and matsutake in autumn, cod milt in winter, with sake from Kyoto and Toyama. Tabelog records eight straight years of a Bib Gourmand. Book ahead; dinner Tuesday–Sunday, lunch at weekends.

House rules are firm: book ahead, arrive on time, one drink each, keep your voice down, and no wheat, dairy or vegetarian adjustments. 8% service.

places.cu: Confectioner to Hongan-ji, founded by tradition in 1421 (official site) · 松風 (matsukaze): a fermented dough of wheat flour, sugar, malt syrup and white miso baked in a 45.5 cm pan, scattered with poppy seeds and cut into strips — said to have begun as rations during the 石山合戦 siege; 8 pieces ¥700 (August–October 2026), cut-end value bags; 西六條寺内松風 made with hama-natto instead of white miso (officia…
places.notes: [Wagashi · Nishi Hongan-ji, the matsukaze of a 600-year-old confectioner] An old confectioner opposite Nishi Hongan-ji that by its own history has supplied the temple's offerings since 1421. Its famous 松風 is a chewy, bread-like slab of fermented wheat dough, white miso and malt syrup, baked in a huge pan and scattered with poppy seeds — said to have started as siege rations in the 石山合戦, and named from a poem by 顕如. Eight pieces ¥700; cut-end bags are a bargain. Seasonal wagashi are sold only here. Takeaway only; 8:30–17:00, closed Wednesday.
places.chef: 株式会社亀屋陸奥 (founded as a company in 1964; official site); no person is named in the sources read · Per the official site: founded, by tradition, in 1421; supplier of offerings to Hongan-ji from about the time 蓮如 (Rennyo) led it; during the 石山合戦 (from 1570) a sweet first made as rations became matsukaze, named after 顕如’s poem once Hongan-ji settled at 六条堀川 (1591); around 1660 the house received a cypress turtle said to have floated in Hideyoshi’s Jurakudai pond, the 亀 of its name, and in 1715 the title 陸奥大掾 from the court; matsukaze specimens won silver at the 1900 Paris Exposition; incorporated in 1964. 司馬遼太郎 wrote matsukaze into 『燃えよ剣』 and 『関ヶ原』. Tabelog Wagashi WEST "Tabelog 100" 2026 (official site news, 29 September 2026). · Per the official site: to keep the taste handed down since the Warring States period and pass it on to the next era, one sheet at a time. · 松風; 憶昔; seasonal wagashi.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: the signature matsukaze is made of wheat flour, sugar, malt syrup and white miso (official site).
places.vgd: Ask. The matsukaze’s listed ingredients are wheat flour, sugar, malt syrup and white miso, with poppy seeds; the rakugan 憶昔 is sugar, white bean paste, rice flour, wasanbon, hama-natto and cinnamon (official site) — none lists animal products, but ask.

Lunch at ¥6,500–7,000 is the famous bargain and hard to book; the leftover kamameshi comes wrapped as rice balls to take home. The chef looks stern but is chatty and funny. Cash only; book for two or more; dress smartly; closed Thursday.

places.notes: [Itamae kappo · Shinmachi-Rokkaku, the first of its kind] Hamasaku opened in Gion in 1927 as Japan's first itamae kappo — the chef cooking at the counter in front of guests — and served Kawabata Yasunari, Shiga Naoya and Princess Grace of Monaco among others (official site); the third-generation master Hiroyuki Morikawa now cooks at an L-shaped counter in the new main shop on Shinmachi. One seasonal course built on outstanding dashi, around ¥100,000 a head. Regular service ends in March 2027 after a farewell year. Reservation by phone; jackets for men. Mon, Tue, Thu–Sat evenings.
places.chef: Hiroyuki Morikawa (森川裕之) · Third-generation owner (浜作三代目店主) and president of 株式会社浜作, per the official site · Gion, Kyoto (born 1962) · Per the official site: 森川裕之 was born in Gion-machi, Kyoto, in 1962, spent student days in Tokyo at kabuki, classical concerts and opera, and took over as third generation in 1991 on the death of the father, the second-generation 武; the founder, the grandfather 森川榮 (森川栄), opened Hamasaku on 1 September 1927 (Showa 2) in Gion Tominaga-cho as Japan’s first itamae kappo. The cookery school 浜作料理教室, started around the same time, has run some 2,300 sessions for 30,000 people; in 2017 the master was honoured as a Contemporary Master Craftsman, the youngest in Kyoto cuisine; books include 和食の教科書 ぎをん献立帖 and 京料理の品格. Guests listed on the site include the Showa Emperor, Kawabata Yasunari, Shiga Naoya, Mukoda Kuniko, Robert De Niro and Princess Grace of Monaco. The site announces that regular service ends at the end of March 2027, the 100th year, fulfilling a promise to the late father, after the master returned to the counter from a nine-hour heart operation over the New Year. Kitsune udon and rice bowls such as oyako-don are the alternatives. No bookings and no shared tables, so expect a queue — up to an hour or more in autumn 2026. Cash only; lunch daily, short evenings except Sundays.

Dinner runs about ¥30,000–50,000 a head plus 10% service. Reservation only; closed Tuesday. Aged meat has a distinct aroma — one regular warns it isn't for everyone.

Venison tripe, bear pâté, pheasant over charcoal, wild-boar spring rolls and botan-nabe come with Miyama's wild vegetables and house bread; reviewers say the meat has little gamey taste. Allow three hours — one December 2025 diner found service slow and the room cold. Reservation only; closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Kyoto Station, Kyoto–French in an old townhouse] A reservation-only kaiseki in a 100-year-old townhouse across the moat from Higashi Hongan-ji, five minutes from Kyoto Station. Chef Shohei Noguchi, from Fukushima and trained in France and at a sushi shop, mixes dashi, charcoal and rice with French sauces and organic vegetables: corn blancmange with sea urchin, Miwa somen dressed like pasta, ayu kamameshi to finish. Courses start together at 12:00 and 18:00; sit at the 9 m counter or in a private room. Dinner runs about ¥20,000–45,000; one October 2026 diner found it poor value.

From May to September you can eat on the yuka over the Kamo River at dusk. Courses only: a sea bream meunière or beef fillet at the centre, from ¥4,400 at lunch and ¥6,600 at dinner (more on the yuka). Book by phone; two-hour seating; cash only at lunch; closed Tuesday.

The ¥11,000 course starts with simmered liver and salt-grilled thigh. It reopened on 1 March 2026 after a long closure, with fewer seats — book ahead. Tatami rooms upstairs have tables and chairs. Closed Monday and Thursday.

Beef arrives in small plates in menu order — raw tongue, raw heart and yukhoe (¥1,200 each), blanched mino — until a Yanagawa-style dish signals the break; then order freely from the grill: tongue, tripe, loin, tail soup. About ten seats; reservations only, and the phone is busy. Closed Wednesday.

places.notes: [Yoshoku · Kiyamachi-Sanjo, the omurice show] A 16-seat counter yoshoku down an alley near Pontocho, open since 1978, made world-famous by its master's 'Happy Omurice' — the omelette flipped, slit and spread over ketchup rice with a flourish, demi-glace on top, and the room singing along. Omurice ¥3,000 (2026); soup and cream croquettes too. Booking online only, and slots go within minutes; one-hour sittings, mostly overseas guests. One February 2026 diner found ¥3,000 a lot unless you count the show. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Motokichi Yukimura (幸村元吉) · Master (マスター), per the official site · The official site names the master as 幸村 元吉 (Motokichi Yukimura) and is titled "オムライスで世界をHappyに!" ("making the world Happy with omurice"), with a fan club, music and overseas omurice events listed in its news. Tabelog: born in Kyoto in 1978 (opening day 2 December 1978), a western-style restaurant pursuing its own style, built on the idea that being able to order what you want, when you want, in the amount you want is the gateway to deliciousness. Reviewers describe videos viewed more than 100 million times, a visit by the King of Malaysia (January 2025) and fame in Taiwan (October 2024). · Per Tabelog: "May the feelings of both the cooks and the diners be in perfect harmony." · Happy Omurice.

places.cu: À la carte Sichuan cooking with drinks (Tabelog) · assorted appetizers ¥1,980 (January–February 2026) or ¥3,200 for two (September 2026): saliva chicken of Kyoto red jidori, spicy jellyfish, Sichuan potato salad, octopus with salt, lemon and Sichuan pepper, zha cai with green onion in chili oil, century egg with white sesame tofu · mapo tofu ¥1,650 (January and August 2026; ¥1,600 in September 20…
places.notes: [Sichuan · Fuyacho, a new hidden Sichuan kitchen] A 19-seat Sichuan restaurant at the far end of the ground floor of a multi-tenant building on Fuyacho-dori, opened in January 2026 by chef Keiichi Hara, who trained at well-known restaurants and in China per an opening-day reviewer. Order à la carte: a six-item appetizer plate, mapo tofu, a celery-and-bitter-melon chili shrimp, black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork on the bone and crab fried rice, with Shaoxing-wine sodas — numbing and hot but refined, say reviewers; solo diners are offered half portions. Most spend ¥6,000–8,000. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Keiichi Hara · Chef (named in a January 2026 review); a September 2026 reviewer calls the chef the owner · Per a January 2026 opening-day reviewer: chef Keiichi Hara trained at renowned restaurants and in China before opening this Sichuan restaurant, which mixes traditional flavours with a modern sensibility. Another January 2026 reviewer came because a favourite chef had opened a shop and enjoyed this chef’s Sichuan cooking again after a long time. A September 2026 diner found three people running the room and an open kitchen. Opened 21 January 2026 (Tabelog). Name written only in Latin letters in the source. · Mapo tofu; Yuan-style chili shrimp; black-vinegar pork on the bone.
places.gfd: Ask. Sichuan dishes built on chili oil, bean pastes and sauces, with gyoza, buns, noodles and fried rice; no gluten information is published (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Mostly meat and seafood (mapo tofu, twice-cooked pork, chili shrimp); a few vegetable plates such as steamed eggplant with leek and Sichuan pepper sauce and two Sichuan potato salads, but no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).

places.notes: [French bistro · Karasuma, a late-night wine bistro] A two-floor bistro behind a green door in an alley off Ayakoji, styled on Paris back streets, with a wooden counter round the kitchen downstairs and small tables upstairs. The menu sticks to bistro classics — steak frites, French onion gratin soup, pâté, crab croquettes — plus burrata with whatever fruit is in season, a torched-cheese Bolognese and Parmesan gnocchi, with wines picked by the sommelier. Reviewers like the late hours and the English-speaking staff; one solo diner was given a smaller pasta portion. Open until 1:30 (to 23:00 on Wednesday).
places.chef: Operator 株式会社ＧＭＩ (Gion; invoice T6130001067887), which also runs 焼肉マウム and 居酒屋 マウム; chef not named · Per the official site: Bistro Maumu does not chase trends and loves the unchanging scene of Paris bistros — steak frites, a daily pasta, honest food at the end of the day — with a resident sommelier choosing classic French and Italian bottles and New World wines. Opened 31 May 2024 (Tabelog). The invoice number belongs to 株式会社ＧＭＩ, whose head office is at the 焼肉マウム address in Gion (NTA corporate-number site; Tabelog). · Per the official site: "We make food that makes people happy" — a place to reset after work, not a special place you visit stiffly. · Steak frites; burrata with seasonal fruit; Parmesan-cream gnocchi.
places.gfd: Ask. A bistro menu of croquettes, fritters, gratin soup, pasta, gnocchi and bread; a few plates such as carpaccio, burrata with fruit and steak may suit, but no gluten information is published (official menu; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options; the menu is mostly meat, fish, cheese and egg, with a tofu-and-tomato caprese and truffle-mayo fries among the few meat-free plates (Tabelog; official menu).

places.notes: [Café · Ebisugawa, pudding and hand-drip coffee] An eleven-seat coffee house on Ebisugawa-dori south of the Imperial Palace, all warm wood, antique-style lamps, a bookshelf and mismatched cups. The owner explains the coffee of the day; the blend (¥550) is Kenya-based and the soft, silky pudding (¥450) with bitter caramel is the reason most come — it must be ordered with a drink. Tabelog Cafe 'Tabelog 100' 2021 and WEST 2025. Small and quiet: no groups over five. Closed Wednesday and the third Sunday.

places.vgd: Ask. Black coffee, shiso soda and the ginger drink look plant-based, but the pudding is egg custard and there is a milk coffee; no ingredient list is published (2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Korean · Pontocho, wagyu and kimchi over the Kamo River] The Kyoto branch of an Osaka-born chef's Korean restaurant that began in Daikanyama in 2000, here since 2009 and now in a stone-and-wood building on Pontocho with a counter round the kitchen and second-floor tables over the Kamo River. Courses open with a seasonal porridge and the house kimchi, then chijimi of Kyoto Kujo-negi, japchae and a main such as dakhanmari, bulgogi hot pot or black-pork samgyeopsal (¥7,000–12,000); à la carte runs to wagyu by the gram and bossam kimchi with seasonal fruit. 10% service. Tabelog Asian/Ethnic WEST 'Tabelog 100' 2026.
places.chef: 李 南河 · Owner-chef of the operator group (grate-ful.co.jp); the shop carries the chef’s own name · Osaka (official site). · Per the official site: in 2000 the Osaka-born cook 李 南河 opened 代官山 李南河 in Tokyo, naming it after the chef in the hope that guests feel as if eating at home; the Kyoto sister shop opened in a renovated old house in a Pontocho back alley and later moved to the riverside within Pontocho; the owner-chef visits producers and markets and buys wagyu at the Kyoto meat market; selected by ZAGAT and as a best Korean restaurant by the Korean Food Foundation; the bulgogi shop SURAGAN (Ebisu) followed in 2005. The operator グレイトフル株式会社 lists 9 restaurants and delis in Tokyo, Kanagawa and Kyoto, two named 李南河, and dates the Kyoto opening to July 2009 (grate-ful.co.jp). The invoice holder is the group company グレイトフルオペレーション株式会社 (Tabelog; NTA). · Per the official site: to keep trying new things with carefully chosen seasonal ingredients so people learn how good Korean food is. · Bossam kimchi with seasonal fruit; Kujo-negi chijimi; dakhanmari and bulgogi hot pots.

Lunch sets around ¥2,000; dinner around ¥6,000–8,000. Booking advised: it fills up even on weekdays. Closed Monday.

Try the set comparing yesterday's and today's saba. No bookings for the tables; some reviewers find it pricey for the portion. Closed Tuesday.

Omakase only: lunch ¥12,000, dinner ¥22,000, plus 10%. English menu and staff; no vegan or vegetarian meals. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
places.chef: 古賀 隆稚 (Koga Ryuji) · Chef · Fukuoka Prefecture (official site). · Per the official site: after École Tsuji's school in France and training in regional France, worked from 2006 at Joël Robuchon (Ebisu), then in France at Le Chabichou (Courchevel), Villa Archange (Cannes), Ledoyen (Paris) and as sous-chef at a one-star restaurant; from 2016 the first Japanese deputy head chef, also developing menus, at Le Cinq (Hôtel George V, Paris) under Christian Le Squer; back in Japan in 2019 as head chef at the Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto. RED U-35 bronze egg 2013 and silver egg 2014 and 2015. Opened KOGA on 9 January 2025 (Tabelog). An October 2026 reviewer writes that it holds one Michelin star in the 2026 Kyoto-Osaka guide. · Per the official site: a restaurant as a "総合芸術" (total art) of space, service and cuisine; respect for every ingredient and its producer; combining ingredients like a perfumer combines scents. · Warm salad of 30-plus vegetables; soufflé baked to order.

places.notes: [Kyoto cuisine · Gion Shirakawa, a counter by the stone lane] A tiny counter hidden on the Shirakawa stone lane in Gion, with eight seats in front of the cooks and one table. The nine-course omakase is ¥11,000, or order à la carte from the seasonal list: rolled omelette, karasumi with daikon, salt-grilled Kyoto chicken, saba-zushi to finish, and old-Kyoto drinking snacks such as funazushi and whale bacon. The head chef, named 筒井 on the official site, trained within the yagenbori group. ¥1,000 otoshi; closed Tuesday.
places.chef: 筒井 (head chef; reading not given) · Head chef 筒井, promoted after training at yagenbori (official site), Operated by the yagenbori group · The official site says the head chef, 筒井, was chosen to lead Wabisuke after training at yagenbori, and that the kitchen blends Kyoto tradition with new arrangements. A March 2026 reviewer first came about 35 years ago, when an elderly woman ran it alone; it later joined the yagenbori group, and the chef has changed on each visit since. A February 2026 reviewer says the present head chef has led the kitchen for a few years. · To bring out the character of fish from around Kyoto and Kyoto vegetables in Kyoto cuisine that shows the four seasons (official site). · Seasonal omakase; karasumi with daikon; saba-zushi.

places.notes: [Wine stand · Kiyamachi-Matsubara, natural wine by the coin] A small open-fronted stand on Kiyamachi where you feed ¥1,000 into a machine, get two coins, and pour your own natural wine from the servers — orange, Japanese, Spanish, French — about ¥500 a pour, from 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. Coffee, chai, beer, cheese, salami and canelé come from the counter, and bottles are sold upstairs. A sister of the soba shop next door, suba, so it works well before or after. Mostly standing; one November 2025 visitor found the system unexplained.

Regulars come for the nanakushi — seven creative kushiage (¥2,100) — and the duck and Kujo green-onion hot pot finished as zosui, with sashimi of local fish, bonito shio-tataki and a chirimen-sansho fried rice to close. A good blackboard of sake. Cash only; book by phone; closed Wednesday.

places.notes: [Sushi · Kiyamachi-Nijo, straw-flamed bonito at an eight-seat counter] Down a passage off Kiyamachi, a dark, bar-like counter of eight seats where the owner, with more than thirty years in Japanese cooking, serves omakase from Maizuru fish and beyond. The show is the straw grill: lights down, flames up, bonito seared in front of you; mackerel skin is pressed with live charcoal. About seventeen dishes at dinner, in two seatings that start together; lunch at noon. Reservations only; closed Wednesday.

places.notes: [Fish izakaya · Shimabara, the market’s back door] An unsigned izakaya in old Shimabara beside Kyoto’s Central Wholesale Market, where the cooks work at a counter level with your plate and the fish comes from a trusted market wholesaler. Evenings are courses — ¥6,000 or ¥9,900 — that change completely between visits: rare sashimi such as akou and ojisan, shio-koji yellowtail, simmered kinmedai head, cod fry, omakase sushi. Lunch has stopped for now. Closed Sunday and holidays; junior-high age and up.
places.chef: Kitchen team (unnamed) · Per the official site: opened in Shimabara next to the Kyoto Central Wholesale Market as a sign-less open-kitchen izakaya, buying through the market wholesaler 河市水産. Tabelog gives the opening as 1 October 2012. December 2025 and September 2026 reviewers note the popular lunch has stopped and evenings run on courses. · Seasonal fish close to ryotei standard at izakaya prices, served in the spirit of ichigo ichie (official site). · Seasonal fish courses; omakase sushi.
places.gfd: Ask. Fish courses of sashimi, grills, simmered dishes and sushi, including tempura and fried cod, which are not gluten-free (2025–2026 reviews).

places.hood: Marutamachi west of Karasuma, by the Imperial Palace — 2 min from Marutamachi Stn
places.cu: “Everyday Kyoto cuisine”: the original ochazuke house, a light meal of rice, pickles and sides (official site) · Suzushiro set ¥1,500 — dashimaki, red-miso soup, rice in a wooden tub for about two bowls, assorted seasonal pickles, hojicha (official site; July–September 2026) · Mizuna set with a seasonal simmered dish; a set with sea bream nanban (2026 reviews) · dashimaki of two eggs and a strong…
places.notes: [Ochazuke · Marutamachi, Kyoto’s everyday meal since the Taisho era] An old machiya by the Imperial Palace serving “ochazuke” in the Kyoto sense — a modest meal. The Suzushiro set (¥1,500, lunch or dinner) brings a feather-light rolled omelette made with a dashi started at 4 a.m., red-miso soup, a tub of rice and seasonal pickles, with Ippodo hojicha for the ochazuke. No reservations and queues in autumn; dinner ends early, at 19:00. Staff greet in soft Kyoto dialect and speak English. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Family business (unnamed in the sources) · Per the official site: an ochazuke house in business since the Taisho era. It began as a sweets shop in Gion named Junidanya after the twelve acts of Chushingura; ochazuke served to settle the palates of tipsy customers proved so popular that it has continued ever since. The site lists TV and press coverage and a 2025 article recalling 長嶋茂雄 as a patron. · Ochazuke as Kyoto cuisine in everyday dress — plain food that cannot hide anything; local and contract-farm vegetables, Ippodo tea (official site). · Dashimaki; the Suzushiro ochazuke set.
places.gfd: Ask. Ochazuke sets of rice, pickles, dashimaki and red-miso soup; the pickles and miso are not described for gluten (official site; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: dashimaki of egg and bonito-kombu dashi in every set; some sets add fish (official site; 2026 reviews).

places.cu: Japanese katsu and egg sandwiches on house shokupan milk bread, from a Brooklyn sandwich shop, with a sake bar counter · pork katsu or chicken katsu (breast and thigh) sando ¥1,500, potato-croquette or egg-salad sando ¥1,300, Japanese beef fillet katsu sando ¥4,000, matcha-strawberry sando ¥850, dashi fries ¥600 (Sanjo menu) · sake by the glass chosen by the owner-sommelier (Sanjo menu)
places.notes: [Sandwiches · downtown, Brooklyn katsu sando with sake] A twelve-seat counter south of Sanjo, the Kyoto outpost of a Brooklyn sando shop ("HELLO, Kyoto! WE ARE FROM BROOKLYN"), with a second Kyoto shop at Kiyomizu. Freshly fried pork or chicken katsu with cabbage and house sauce on milk bread, ¥1,500; egg-salad sando ¥1,300; beef fillet katsu ¥4,000. Portions are big — several diners took half home — and one found the sauce about to spill out. Sake picked by the owner-sommelier. English menu and staff; many overseas customers. Daily 12:00–17:00.
places.chef: Sakaki Nakamura (owner and sommelier, per the Sanjo menu; name known only in Latin letters) · Owner and sake sommelier (Sanjo menu: "Sakaki Nakamura, the owner/sommelier, curates fine sake from all over Japan") · Taku Sando began in Greenpoint, Brooklyn (29 Greenpoint Ave), "brought to you by the creative team of Takumen in LIC", around a shokupan milk bread baked in-house daily (takusando.com About page). The Kyoto site lists two Kyoto shops, Sanjo and Kiyomizu, beside Brooklyn; the Sanjo menu is headed "HELLO, Kyoto! WE ARE FROM BROOKLYN." The Sanjo shop opened on 15 October 2024 (Tabelog). · From the Brooklyn About page: the shokupan "represents a wholesome luxury, and is the heart of the meal". · Pork katsu sando; chicken katsu sando; tamago sando.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: every sandwich is on house shokupan milk bread, and the katsu and croquettes are coated in panko (Sanjo menu).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the two vegetarian sandwiches (potato croquette, egg salad) still use milk bread and karashi-mustard mayo; the fries carry a fish-and-vegetable dashi furikake (Sanjo menu). Shiso edamame is marked vegetarian — ask.
places.hours: Tabelog: daily 12:00–17:00 (food L.O. 16:30); schedule changes are posted on Google Maps. places.cu: Late-night takoyaki bar · 17 kinds of takoyaki, 8 for ¥800 (June 2025); half-and-half of two flavours +¥50 (June and November 2025) · sauce, salt, soy, pizza sauce with cheese, demi-glace, seaweed kimchi, green onion with wasabi (2025–2026 reviews) · beef tendon stew, gizzard with pepper; sake, shochu, beer, champagne (2025–2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Takoyaki · Gion, until 4 am] A thirteen-seat L-shaped counter under red lanterns on the ground floor of a club building on Hanamikoji, frying takoyaki till 4 am; diners say it has been there 20 years, with a second-generation owner greeting passers-by. Eight crisp-shelled, gooey balls for ¥800 in seventeen flavours — sauce, salt, pizza, seaweed kimchi — plus half-and-half; champagne and sake beside the beer. One diner found the beer glass small; another felt chilly in the half-open room in autumn and a little intimidated by the street at night. Smoking allowed. Cash or e-money.
places.chef: Second-generation owner (January 2026 review); not named in a source · The shop blog (ameblo, last updated 2012) calls 秀蛸 a takoyaki shop born in Kyoto, with a Gion main shop and a Kiyamachi shop; a February 2012 post mentions staff from all three shops of the time. Tabelog lists the Gion shop and a Kiyamachi shop today. A June 2025 diner and a January 2026 diner say it has been running for 20 years; the January 2026 diner calls the energetic young owner the second generation. · Takoyaki in many sauces, with half-and-half plates.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: takoyaki are wheat-batter balls; sauces include Worcester-style sauce, soy and demi-glace (2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: every takoyaki holds octopus, with mayonnaise and cheese toppings (2025–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Italian & shaved ice · Gion south, Matayoshi's casual sister] The casual sister of Gion Matayoshi, also on the south side of Gion, behind a patterned block lattice: by day a fish or wagyu lunch tray and natural-ice kakigori with house syrups, by night Italian à la carte on kaiseki plates — sea-urchin aglio e olio, wagyu Bolognese, veal cutlet. Diners in 2025–2026 praised sea-bream chazuke, rich matcha ice and warm send-offs; others found a ¥1,800 matcha ice average (July 2026), slow drinks with two staff (July 2026), and food average with uneven pacing and few drinks (October 2026). No cash.
places.chef: Sister shop of 祇園又吉 (official site); the chef is not named · The 祇園又吉 site announced the new shop また吉 on 1 August 2021; Tabelog reviews go back to January 2025. The また吉 site itself says it was born in October 2026, serving Italian with the same chosen ingredients and preparation as the main restaurant plus natural-ice shaved ice at casual prices; an August 2026 diner mentions a recent renovation, and an October 2026 diner calls it still new. A July 2026 diner writes that the owner hails from Okinawa. Natural ice from 四代目徳次郎 in Nikko (official site). · Official site: 「もっと軽い気持ちで、本物の味を楽しんで欲しい」 — "We want people to enjoy the real thing, with a lighter heart." · Natural-ice kakigori; Italian à la carte on Japanese tableware; lunch trays.
places.gfd: Ask. No gluten information: dinner is pasta, bruschetta and a veal cutlet beside carpaccio and charcoal-grilled meat; lunch sets are simmered fish or teriyaki wagyu with miso soup (official menu). Course changes for allergies must be phoned in ahead, not on the day (Tabelog).
places.vgd: Ask. Lunch sets and dinner dishes use fish, beef, pork or cheese (official menu); the shaved-ice syrups are fruit, matcha or brown sugar, with condensed milk as an extra topping.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion south, ten seats and handmade soba] A ten-seat kaiseki counter east of Hanamikoji, opened in 2014 and starred in the 2016 Michelin Guide (Tabelog). Courses start with a brown-rice soup and freshly shaved bonito, run through hamo, sweetfish and eel, and end with the owner’s own 100% buckwheat soba. An April 2026 couple found it rare for Gion: lightly seasoned, traditional Kyoto cooking from ¥12,000 at night, with the owners seeing them off. The site says no English is spoken — book through your hotel. Cash only. Closed Thursday.
places.chef: Moriwaki (surname from the shop name; Tabelog gives a full name only in machine translation, so it is not used) · Owner-chef (店主), per the official site · Per the official site: a small ten-seat shop born in Gion in 2014, serving seasonal kaiseki that ends with the owner’s handmade 100% buckwheat soba. Tabelog (in its English translation): the chef trained at ryokans, sushi restaurants and other places, then at "Irifune" and "Gion Okada" before going independent; opened 28 August 2014; a Michelin star in the 2016 Michelin Guide, about a year after opening. A January 2025 diner was served by the head chef, the proprietress and another chef. · Official site: to be a shop that always stays close by, for time alone or time with someone dear. · Seasonal kaiseki; handmade 100% buckwheat soba to finish.
places.gfd: Ask when booking. No gluten information; courses end with the owner’s handmade 100% buckwheat soba (official site), served in a dashi-based kaiseki.
places.vgd: Not vegan: a fish kaiseki opening with freshly shaved bonito flakes, with sashimi, sweetfish, eel and dashi soups (2025–2026 reviews).

places.cu: Seasonal tempura courses at a six-seat counter (official site) · "Gion no Bansan" course ¥12,100 (lunch ¥11,000): wagyu tail soup, sashimi of the day, seared Kuroge wagyu, about ten tempura such as kuruma prawn, eggplant, sea urchin, shiitake, yuzu-marinated sawara, eel, clam, wagyu and tilefish, then a tempura rice ball, red miso soup and dessert · lighter course ¥7,700 (lunch ¥6,600) · lunch "t…
places.notes: [Tempura · Gion, a six-seat counter] A tiny tempura counter on a Gion corner, where one chef fries course after course in front of six guests. Dinner (¥7,700 or ¥12,100) starts with wagyu tail soup, sashimi and seared wagyu, then about ten seasonal pieces — kuruma prawn, aosa seaweed piled with sea urchin, Kamo eggplant, eel, young ayu in summer, a rare-fried wagyu — and ends with a tempura rice ball. Lunch from ¥3,300 is the value pick. Book by the day before. Run by the small Kyoto group 京色; reviewers like the quiet chef and the price for Gion.
places.chef: Head chef (not named) who runs the counter alone (June 2026); operator 株式会社京色 · Per the operator site: 株式会社京色 was founded by its president 眞鍋 and the cooks 藤原 and 山内, who studied together at a cooking school and gained experience in Japanese, Western and creative cooking before reuniting; the company runs 5 Kyoto shops — うらやま京色, BANSAN 京色, 祇園 晩餐 京色, 祇園天ぷら晩餐 and 角打ちと麺 ばんさん. Per the official page: a counter of six seats, "the distance at which freshly fried tempura can be served without losing its taste." Opened 21 March 2021 (Tabelog). The chef told a July 2026 diner the oil is 100% cottonseed. · Per the official page: tempura needs both fresh ingredients and the cook’s skill — no letting up from buying to the moment it is served. · Aosa tempura topped with sea urchin; wagyu tail soup; tempura rice ball.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: a tempura counter — every course centres on battered, fried tempura and a tempura rice ball (official site; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: courses open with wagyu tail soup and run through prawn, fish, sea urchin and wagyu tempura (official site; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: Dinner from 17:00 to 25:00 (last order 24:30) and lunch from 12:00, lunch by reservation made by the day before (official site). places.notes: [Izakaya · Gion, Niigata sake till 3 a.m.] A small, smoky, late-night izakaya on Gion's Kiritoshi, run by an owner from Niigata. It pours Niigata sake — ask for the off-menu bottles — with a long list of homey plates: tuna macaroni salad, nikujaga, horse sashimi, giant Tochio fried tofu with negi miso, oden in winter, and the namesake pork miso soup to finish. Mostly locals, Showa pop on the speakers, ¥500 cover. Open until 3:00; closed Sunday.
places.chef: 安達 秀行 (Adachi Hideyuki) · Owner, 大将 (the invoice holder; from Niigata) · Niigata Prefecture (official site; 2025 reviews). · The invoice register lists an individual, 安達 秀行, for the shop’s invoice number; the official site links the Instagram account adachihideyuki. Per the official site: a slightly hidden shop facing Kiritoshi in Gion, with sake and local dishes from the 大将’s home prefecture of Niigata alongside popular modern dishes. Reviewers describe an owner from Niigata (June and October 2025) and a master who sometimes drinks along with guests (April 2025). Opened 26 November 2013 (Tabelog). · Per the official site: "空間、人、美味しさ" — the space, the people and good food; at-home and hidden at once. · Pork miso soup; Tochio fried tofu with negi miso; Niigata sake.
places.gfd: Ask. An izakaya menu of miso pork soup, fried dishes, oden, Saikyo-miso fish and soy-seasoned plates; no gluten information is published (official menu; 2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the signature is pork miso soup, alongside horse sashimi, fish, fried chicken and oden; a few plates such as grilled shiitake or Tochio fried tofu with negi miso have no published ingredients (official menu; 2025–26 reviews).

places.cu: Wagyu sukiyaki kaiseki cooked at the table by staff in the house warishita (official site) · dinner: wagyu sukiyaki kaiseki ¥24,500, Omi-beef sukiyaki ¥30,500, Omi-beef shabu-shabu with kombu dashi, house ponzu and sesame sauce ¥30,500 (book ahead), Kobe-beef sukiyaki ¥36,500, Omi-beef chateaubriand sukiyaki (limited) ¥42,500 — each with a starter, soup, the main, rice and dessert · weekend lunch…
places.notes: [Sukiyaki · Kiyamachi, private rooms over the Kamo River] A sukiyaki house in private rooms down a stone alley off Kiyamachi, in the building where the Bakumatsu samurai Takechi Hanpeita lodged when it was the ryotei 四国屋丹虎; some rooms look over the Kamo River, one onto a tsukubai garden by Kazuyuki Ishihara. Staff cook wagyu, Omi or Kobe beef sukiyaki at the table in the house warishita, after seasonal kaiseki starters; dinner from ¥24,500, weekend lunch from ¥12,100, service included. Reviewers praise the rooms and the river terrace; one found the sukiyaki too light. Run by the Kobe-based G LION GROUP. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: 料理長 (head chef, not named); operator G LION GROUP (Kobe; representative 菊地 秀武) · Per the official site: wagyu sukiyaki kaiseki in a new style by a cook long experienced in traditional Japanese cuisine, made in front of guests with the house warishita; the building was the ryotei 四国屋丹虎 in the Bakumatsu era, where 武市半平太 lived when in Kyoto, and the tokonoma board and pillar of the 半平の間 are kept unchanged; a box-staircase trace from that era was found during renovation; tsubo-niwa garden supervised by the garden designer 石原和幸. Press releases name the operator as the G LION GROUP of Kobe (representative 菊地 秀武), whose recruitment site describes about 150 group companies, mostly car dealerships. Tabelog Hot Pot "Tabelog 100" 2026 (Tabelog). · Per the official site: an out-of-the-ordinary sukiyaki experience — the seasons of Kyoto with all five senses. · Wagyu, Omi and Kobe beef sukiyaki kaiseki.
places.gfd: Ask when booking. Sukiyaki is cooked in the house warishita and kaiseki starters use dashi; the current menu publishes no gluten information. The operator once announced a gluten-free wagyu sukiyaki kaiseki for inbound guests (press release, now offline; per a search summary) — confirm it is still offered (official menu, November 2026).
places.vgd: Not vegan: wagyu sukiyaki and shabu-shabu kaiseki with dashi-based starters (official menu).

places.notes: [Sweets & café · Muromachi, castella in a 1700 townhouse] The flagship of a castella maker in a broad-fronted Muromachi townhouse built in 1700, with an earthen entry, an old kamado and well, a gallery and a tearoom over an inner garden. Its paper-baked castella of Kyoto eggs comes as a three-piece tasting set with tea (¥1,760), and seasonal plates — chestnut Mont Blanc and dorayaki in autumn, grill-your-own dango in winter — come with a drink for about ¥1,870. No bookings; expect a queue at weekends. Run by 長崎堂 of Osaka, which also has a café in Shibuya Hikarie. Open daily 11:00–18:00.
places.chef: Operator 株式会社長崎堂 (Osaka; founded 1960; chairman 荒木 貴史); not a chef-led shop · Per the official site: 然花抄院 opened its Kyoto Muromachi main store in August 2009 among old kimono merchants, with shop, café, gallery and workshop; the townhouse has a pillar inscribed with its building year, 元禄十三年, paving stones from the Kitano tram line, a well in the courtyard and kamado, and walls partly papered in karakami by 唐長; the name expresses hospitality with "a heart of flowers" and sweets in the true taste of each. The company page lists 株式会社長崎堂 (founded August 1960, capital ¥30 m) and two cafés, Kyoto Muromachi and Shibuya Hikarie ShinQs (opened April 2012), plus ZENKASHOIN gift shops in mass retailers and station and airport shops (official site). Tabelog Cafe WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025 (Tabelog). · Per the official site: "花も、菓も、然るべき姿へ" — flowers and sweets, each in its proper form; serving things plainly, without affectation. · Paper-baked "Zen" castella; seasonal sweet plates with tea.
places.gfd: Ask. The house sweets are paper-baked castella, dorayaki, cookies and Mont Blanc on castella; warabi mochi, ice cream and teas are also served, but no gluten information is published (official menu; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Castella and the egg sweets use eggs, and parfaits use cream and ice cream; Japanese teas and coffee are plant-based, but no ingredient list is published for the warabi mochi or other sweets (official menu; 2026 reviews).

Reviews split on the noodles — praised for the cut and lightness, faulted by some for lacking firmness in hot broth. Cash only, no bookings. Closed Monday and the second Tuesday.

Take a course built around the day, or order à la carte — grilled hon-moroko, sweetfish with roe, white-miso hot pot, wagyu with sea urchin — at an unhurried pace. Bills run ¥20,000–30,000 with 10% service; one 2024 guest found it a little dear. Reservations need a Japanese phone number. Closed Wednesday.

Nodoguro, crab gratin, wagyu, corn tempura and curry are favourites. Expect ¥20,000–30,000 or more. Listed in OAD 2026 (per a reviewer). Closed Sunday and the second and fourth Monday.

places.notes: [Music bar & natural wine · Kawaramachi Sanjo, a forest under ten speakers] A big, dim lounge just off Kawaramachi, produced by Fantastic Plastic Machine's Tomoyuki Tanaka, with a huge tree at its centre, plants everywhere and ten ceiling speakers. Come for natural wine — more than 120 bottles — or cocktails, plus bar food: the dashimaki brioche sandwich, sukiyaki spring rolls, tacos and shake-bag fries. Courses from ¥4,500; 10% service in the lounge. Some find the music too loud. Adults only; until 3:00 on Friday and Saturday.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, sesame tofu and saba sushi down a lane] A traditional kaiseki house tucked into a Gion back lane, with a counter and tatami rooms, some upstairs over a courtyard. Chef Akihiko Nishimura's nine or ten dishes run from a silky sesame tofu and a clear dashi soup through sashimi and a famous saba sushi to sea-bream chazuke; the saba sushi is also sold to take home. One June 2026 diner found the seasoning on the strong side. Reviewers spent about ¥20,000–30,000 a head; a 17% service charge applies. Mon–Sat evenings, reservation only.

Lunch on weekends is a bargain — soup, a plate of antipasti with gnocco fritto and prosciutto, and a pasta for ¥2,750 — booked by the day before. Dinners add Modena tigelle, cotoletta and slow-braised meats, and tiramisu. No seafood, no service charge. Closed Monday.

The food is fish-led and mostly under ¥1,000 a dish: thick sashimi, namero, simmered sawara, fried mehikari, grilled squid, with matsutake dobin-mushi in autumn. A ¥1,000 lunch set sells out. Book ahead; open nightly to midnight.

places.notes: [Eel · Gion, eel in a cedar tub] A Gion eel house down a lane west of Hanamikoji, with live eels by the door and tatami rooms upstairs. The house dish is the u-oke: Edo-style eel — steamed, then grilled with tare, soft and lightly sweet — laid like a raft across rice in a cedar tub for three to five people (¥12,600–21,000), so groups serve as much as each likes. Smaller parties take an eel bowl (from ¥4,200), umaki or the yawata-maki. The shop dug its own well for the water. Tabelog Unagi 'Tabelog 100' 2018, 2019 and 2022. Closed Monday; phone bookings in Japanese.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Miyagawacho, a playful Kyoto counter] An eight-seat counter on Miyagawacho's stone-paved lane of teahouses, run by a chef-sommelier who trained at Gion Sasaki. Gluten-free rice- or corn-flour pasta is offered. Lunch courses from about ¥5,500; ¥300 table charge at dinner.

Evenings bring shark fin, abalone, live-tank seafood, Peking duck and Shanghai crab in season. A longtime regular complains prices have doubled in two years. 10% service; open daily.

places.notes: [Hamo kappou · Kawaramachi-Shijo, since 1934] A third-generation kappou down an alley off Kawaramachi, where the hamo is bone-cut only after you arrive and the hamo-shabu broth is a family recipe. Summer and autumn bring hamo courses — otoshi with plum, tempura, hot pot, pressed sushi — winter brings Wakasa guji and soft-shell turtle. Hamo shabu course ¥12,100. Busy since a July 2026 TV feature. One August 2026 guest wanted service to match the room and found the hand towels too strongly scented. Closed Monday.
places.chef: A family restaurant now in its third generation (official site: 三代続く); the owner is not named. A June 2026 diner writes of "the owner and his wife". · Per the official site: founded in 1934 (Showa 9), with three generations of hamo technique and a hamo-shabu broth passed down in the family; the hamo is bone-cut and blanched only after guests arrive; the shabu broth is made daily from grilled hamo heads and bones with kombu and Kujo leeks; bamboo shoots fetched each morning from a farm under contract. Solo diners get smaller portions; families with small children are welcome. ¥300 salad cover. Tabelog Izakaya WEST 'Tabelog 100' 2024. Closed Sunday.

places.cu: Kyoto kaiseki of gentle dashi lifted by citrus, vinegar, ume and ginger (Michelin Guide; 2026 reviews) · lunch omakase ¥10,000–10,500, dinner about ¥24,000 (OMAKASE; September 2026) · summer: cold-brewed gyokuro to start, soft-shell crab and ito-uri, hamo, ayu, winter melon (July–August 2026) · autumn: fig with sesame dressing, egg tofu with hairy crab, grilled sawara with chilli vinegar, simmere…
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Marutamachi, a couple's quiet Kyoto counter] A twelve-seat kaiseki counter near the Imperial Palace, opened in May 2024 by chef 辻 義勝 — long trained at Oryori Hayashi and head chef at Aji Fukushima for eleven years — with the okami, a sommelier, pairing sake and wine. The cooking is gentle dashi sharpened with citrus and vinegar: soft-shell crab, hamo and ayu in summer, figs with sesame and matsutake in autumn. Lunch about ¥10,000, dinner about ¥24,000. Listed with a Michelin star soon after opening. Cash only; closed Sunday.
places.chef: 辻 義勝 · Owner-chef, with the okami (a sommelier and kikisake-shi) — a couple (OMAKASE; July 2025 review) · A hometown known for woodworking, per the Michelin Guide (the kumiko is from Okawa, Fukuoka). · Per OMAKASE: 店主 辻義勝 trained for many years at the long-established 御料理はやし, helped launch 味ふくしま and was its head chef for eleven years, then went independent and opened 辻布紗 in May 2024; the okami is a qualified sommelier and kikisake-shi who pairs wine and sake. An August 2026 reviewer adds training at "Yoshiyasu". Per the Michelin Guide: an owner devoted to Kyoto cuisine, attentive to the harmony of ingredients and dashi, using citrus and vinegar for rhythm; the name 布紗 refers to a hemp cloth used in Shinto rites, and plain hemp hangs as the noren. July 2026 reviewers note a Michelin star soon after opening. · Per the Michelin Guide: deep, nourishing flavour from the harmony of ingredients and dashi, with acidity giving the menu its rise and fall. · Dashi-led kaiseki; seasonal rice.
places.gfd: Ask when booking. Kyoto kaiseki built on dashi with citrus, vinegar and soy; no gluten information is published (Michelin Guide; 2025–26 reviews).

places.notes: [Onigiri · Gion near Yasaka Shrine, breakfast at four seats] A tiny morning counter in Gion where two cooks shape big, loose rice balls from clay-pot rice to order: salt, ume, marinated tuna, salmon, negi miso. Sit-down sets of two with miso soup are about ¥1,100; rice balls to take away are about ¥350. Four seats and 30-minute sittings, so book (Instagram works) or take away. One 2023 guest found the room too quiet and close for conversation. QR pay, no cards. Closed Monday.

places.gfd: Ask. Rice balls with fillings such as salt, ume, salmon, marinated tuna, chicken soboro, negi miso and salmon mayo, with miso soup; seasonings may contain wheat; no gluten information (2023–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Salt, ume and negi-miso rice balls appear, but the miso soup has been a meat-based broth (February 2024) and many fillings are fish or chicken (2023–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Yukke bowls · Gion by Yasaka Shrine, raw wagyu] A small second-floor room by Yasaka Shrine from the Oagari group, licensed to serve raw beef: the draw is the temari yukke don — a dome of finely cut black wagyu with egg yolk, ikura optional, finished as dashi chazuke — about ¥2,200–4,100, plus steak boxes and a sea urchin yukke bowl. GF on request (say so when ordering) and a Muslim-friendly menu with halal-certified wagyu. Photogenic; one diner preferred izakaya yukke. ¥330 otoshi at dinner. Open daily.
places.chef: Staff of the Oagari group (unnamed) · Per the official site: a yukke specialist of the Oagari group (おあがりグループ), which also runs 和牛火山おあがり in Arashiyama and Gion and うしとさかな in Sapporo; the group publishes a gluten-free policy and a Muslim-friendly policy (halal-certified wagyu, dedicated utensils, separate storage, staff training) that both name this shop. places.gfd: GF options on request: the shop's page lists gluten-free among its food-diversity options, and the group's policy says its GF menu excludes wheat, barley, rye and non-GF oats, with seasonings checked against manufacturers' labels. places.notes: [Indian · Kiyamachi above Oike, since 1987] A spacious second-floor Indian restaurant on Kiyamachi, open since 1987 and trusted by locals — one reviewer's Indian colleague called it the best curry ever. The lunch "Full Thali" (¥2,530, vegetarian or not) brings rasam, four curries, tikka and naan; two-curry sets start at ¥1,100, and biryani appears at weekends. Vegan, vegetarian, halal and Hindu options are listed; English spoken. Fast service. Open late. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · A January 2026 regular says the restaurant was founded in 1987 and is among the most trusted in the area. Reviewers in 2025–2026 describe a spacious room with rich decor, well-mannered staff and very fast service; Tabelog lists English-speaking staff. · The Full Thali; biryani; daily vegetable curry.

places.vgd: Some vegan options: Tabelog lists vegan and vegetarian options, and the lunch thali comes in vegetarian and non-vegetarian versions with dals, sambar and vegetable curries; confirm ghee and dairy with staff (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Hanamikoji, opposite the Kaburenjo] A long-established kaiseki house on Hanamikoji facing the Gion Kobu Kaburenjo, with a 14-seat counter where you watch the sashimi cut and the kamado rice cooked, and private rooms upstairs. Monthly courses of about ¥15,000–20,000 end with a choice of clay-pot rice — chirimen sansho or shirasu and mentaiko. Warm, unhurried service, with dishes explained in English; reviewers call it good value for Gion. 10% service from 1 Nov to 8 Dec 2026. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Chefs at the counter (unnamed), Floor staff · Per Tabelog: a seasonal course changing monthly, cherishing the traditions of Japanese cuisine while exploring new techniques and ingredients, with rice and sashimi prepared at the counter. A July 2026 regular since 2019 has watched the chefs grow and heard that one early chef has opened a Kyoto-kaiseki restaurant in Milan; a June 2026 family returned after several decades to find it unchanged. · Tradition and innovation in Japanese cuisine (Tabelog). · Kamado rice; monthly hassun.
places.gfd: Ask. Monthly kaiseki courses with dashi, white and red miso, soy-based sauces and clay-pot rice; no gluten information (2025–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Kissa · Kiyomizu-Gojo, a one-man tea room] A ten-seat tea specialist near Rokuharamitsu-ji, run single-handed by a kind, elderly owner who explains every tea. Pick your own cup and pot cosy from the shelves, then a Darjeeling-Assam blend or a fruit tea with crisp scones, cake, or the fresh-pasta lunch set. Blankets on the chairs in winter; tea leaves and sweets to take home, some made by people with disabilities. Closed Tuesday and the second Monday.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed), who runs the shop alone · A March 2026 reviewer describes the shop as run single-handed by a kind elderly gentleman; a January 2026 regular has come for about fifteen years. A November 2024 reviewer heard it is loved by Kyoto’s geiko and maiko. · Leaf teas; scones; fresh pasta.
