places.notes: [Vietnamese · Kiyamachi-Oike, pho and banh mi upstairs] A small, cheerfully decorated Vietnamese restaurant one floor up on Kiyamachi near Oike — the lift opens straight into the room. Lunch is the draw: the ¥1,200 Special S set brings half a pho, both kinds of spring rolls, a mini rice bowl, salad and che; or pair homemade banh mi with half a pho. Evenings run to beer and small plates. Seasoning is mild — add fish sauce at the table. Open daily.

places.notes: [Café · Shijo-Omiya, cheesecake by the Randen tracks] A machiya over a century old, opened up with concrete and old beams, right beside the Randen tram line near Shijo-Omiya — ask for a window seat upstairs and watch the trains pass. The order is specialty coffee (an Ethiopian medium roast is popular) with a cheesecake: classic Basque, matcha or a seasonal flavour, about ¥1,300 as a set. Expect a queue, sometimes an hour; pets welcome on the terrace. Closed Tuesday.

Come early for drinks and sashimi, or after midnight when it fills up. Smoking allowed. 19:00–4:00, closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Mizutaki · Kamo riverside, since 1788] A mizutaki house founded in 1788 by the Kamo River south of Shijo, in a heritage building with a garden-view counter, private rooms and summer riverside seats. The rich white chicken broth, boiled from bones, is the point — sip it first, cook the chicken in it, and finish with zosui. Lunch, newly added after a recent renovation, is ¥4,800 with a drink; dinner courses run about ¥15,000–30,000. Reservation only; adults only. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
places.chef: Long-running family house (unnamed); an October 2026 diner heard it has passed to the ninth generation · Per the official site: founded in 1788, it began as a poultry shop opened by the first-generation 彌助; the second generation, 彌三郎, began serving chicken dishes upstairs, and the building has kept its appearance since the founding. Tabelog’s shop text says the mizutaki was loved by Sakamoto Ryoma. Reviewers note a recent renovation and the start of lunch (May and July 2026), and an October 2026 diner heard the business had passed to the ninth generation. · Mizutaki in a white chicken broth; zosui.
places.gfd: Ask. Mizutaki in a chicken-bone broth with house-made ponzu and grilled mochi, finished as zosui or chicken soba; courses add sushi and fried fish (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

places.notes: [French · near the Imperial Palace, Kyoto-style French in a design hotel] The basement restaurant of the design hotel THE SCREEN, where chef Yasumasa Nakahira serves Kyoto-vegetable French to eat with chopsticks, in a room painted by Tetsuei Nakamura. Lunch courses (about ¥3,000–5,000) are good value; the 11-dish dinner is ¥15,730. Book the garden-view kotatsu room (¥1,100) and ask for a message plate — the pastry work is the talk of reviews. Service can be patchy. Open daily.

Lunch from ¥4,000; dinner from ¥9,900 plus 10%. Smart casual. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: 遠藤 浄 (owner-chef, per the official site; no reading in a source) · Owner and chef (official site: オーナー／シェフ 遠藤 浄), Co-owner and manager 佐藤 幹夫 (official site: オーナー／支配人) · Born 1962 in 長野県安曇野市 (official site). · Per the official site: the chef joined 株式会社揚子江 in 1982 and trained at well-known Chinese restaurants including 獅子琳, 翠園 and 翠凰, joined 株式会社グリーンハウス 謝朋殿 in 1998 and was head chef at its restaurants, then head chef of 四川豆花飯荘 東京店 from its opening in 2007. The co-owner and manager 佐藤 幹夫, born 1963 in 秋田県横手市, joined 東京丸の内パレスホテル in 1982, worked at 浦安ブライトンホテル, joined 謝朋殿 in 1998 and managed 四川豆花飯荘 東京店 from 2007. Diners praise the cheerful staff; one found the portions small for the price, another the endings repetitive. Closed Thursday.

Lunch is only 11:00–13:00 (evenings Friday–Sunday), queues are common, and phones and video are not allowed. Cash only.

places.chef: 藤本 宏和 · Owner-chef (the invoice holder) · Hiroshima (July 2026 review). · The invoice register lists an individual, 藤本 宏和, for the shop’s invoice number. Dinner omakase ¥22,000 plus pairing (¥8,000–11,000); lunch from about ¥8,800 is the easy way in. Everyone starts together; no under-13s. Closed Monday.
places.chef: 西別當 選 (Nishibetto Erabu) and 西 正希 (Nishi Masaki) · Owner-sommelier 西別當 選 (the invoice holder; master sommelier); chef 西 正希 · Owner: Kagoshima; chef: Mie (official site). · Per the official site: owner-sommelier 西別當 選, born 1956 in Kagoshima, joined Kobe’s Kitano Club in 1976, trained ten years in service and wine at Kyoto’s French restaurant Lyon, became chef sommelier of the grand maison Ginza L’Ecrin in 1989, later worked in hotels, was chef sommelier and manager at 粟田山荘 in 2014 and opened this restaurant in 2015; in February 2016 the owner became the first sommelier honoured as one of Kyoto Prefecture’s outstanding craftsmen (現代の名工). Chef 西 正希, born 1975 in Mie, trained 14 years at a kaiseki restaurant in Kobe and then at a two-Michelin-star ryotei in Mie. The invoice register lists 西別當 選. places.notes: [Tempura · Kawaramachi-Oike, twelve-seat counter] A twelve-seat tempura counter upstairs by Kyoto City Hall, run by a couple with a little help: the chef fries shrimp, corn and seasonal vegetables to order and explains how to eat each. Lunch sets are good value; dinner is a course ending in kakiage on rice or tencha. Diners like the chatty chef; others found the decor and background music in need of work (2024–2025) and, in April 2026, service so-so — no one offered more tea. 10% service at dinner.
places.chef: Chef (not named); a June 2024 diner writes the restaurant "is run by a couple and their staff" · Opened 19 September 2018 (Tabelog). Reviewers from 2023 to 2026 describe a counter where the chef fries each piece in front of guests and explains how to eat it; a July 2025 diner saw the chef handling everything alone at a busy dinner, and an April 2026 diner saw two people working the counter. · Tempura courses; kakiage tencha or tendon to finish.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: a tempura counter — wheat-batter tempura with dipping sauce, kakiage and tendon (2023–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: shrimp and cuttlefish tempura, a dashi dipping sauce and red miso soup (2023–2026 reviews).

places.hood: Gion, Shinbashi-dori east of Hanamikoji — 3 min walk from the north gate of Yasaka Shrine
places.cu: Neighbourhood sushi in Gion, by course or à la carte · omakase nigiri courses, then favourites to order; sashimi, simmered dishes, the day’s grilled dish, red miso soup with egg (2024–2026 reviews) · seen: engawa of sea bream and flounder, dancing shrimp with fried heads, grilled fin, uni, ikura, funazushi (2024–2026 reviews) · winter fugu course with sashimi, tempura, hot pot and zosui (December…
places.notes: [Sushi · Gion Shinbashi, relaxed and smoking-friendly] A thirteen-seat sushi shop near Yasaka Shrine that regulars call welcoming rather than formal: omakase nigiri, then whatever you like à la carte — dancing shrimp, engawa, funazushi — with a strong sake list and fugu in winter. Families return every Obon; one regular has been 27 times. Smoking and e-cigarettes allowed. ¥500+ otoshi. Lunch by reservation; closed Sunday.
places.chef: Owner, chef and hostess at the counter (2024–2026 reviews); not named · Opened 24 June 2010 (Tabelog). Reviewers from 2024 to 2026 describe a friendly chef, owner and hostess, a counter and sunken tables, à la carte ordering beside courses, and a sake list chosen with care; a June 2025 regular on a 27th visit was glad to see the couple again. · Omakase nigiri; à la carte sushi with sake; winter fugu.
places.gfd: Ask. No gluten information; a sushi and à la carte menu with simmered dishes, tempura in the winter fugu course and red miso soup (2024–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: sushi, sashimi, fugu, shrimp and dashi-simmered dishes (2024–2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: Mon–Sat 12:00–13:30 (lunch by reservation only) and 18:00–22:00; closed Sunday. A daily otoshi from ¥500 is charged (Tabelog; Japanese original 「つきだし 500円～ ※日替わり」). BYO allowed at ¥2,000 per bottle (Tabelog). 13 seats: 7 at the counter, 6 at sunken tables; smoking allowed (Tabelog), e-ciga…

places.n: ホーフベッカライ エーデッガー・タックス 京都店 (Hofbäckerei Edegger-Tax Kyoto)
places.hood: Okazaki — 411 m from Higashiyama Stn
places.cu: Austrian court bakery and café: the Kyoto shop of Graz’s Hofbäckerei Edegger-Tax, founded 1569 (official site) · Handkaiser rolls, pretzel ¥250, Hand-Kaiser with sesame ¥240, rye wholegrain ¥600, croissant ¥360 (September 2026), Kipferl, Salzstangerl, Vollkornbrot · Sachertorte, Kaiserkugelhupf, Sissi Busserl, chestnut tart, Mont Blanc, cornet with whipped cream, Danishes · café drinks on the ter…
places.notes: [Austrian bakery-café · Okazaki] The Japanese shop of a Graz court bakery founded in 1569, whose eighth-generation owner entrusted its recipes to a Vienna-trained Japanese baker. Handkaiser rolls, pretzels, rye bread and a giant cream cornet to take away, or Sachertorte and chestnut tart on the terrace. Breads sell out early on holidays. Closed Wednesday and Thursday.
places.chef: 野澤 孝彦 (のざわ・たかひこ, per the official site) · Chef of the Japanese shop, entrusted with the recipes by Robert Edegger (official site) · Born 1972 in 埼玉県上尾市 (official site). · Per the official site: Hofbäckerei Edegger-Tax in Graz, founded in 1569, held the Habsburg court warrant; the eighth-generation owner Robert Edegger, in charge since 1992, entrusted the recipes to 野澤 孝彦 and opened the Japanese shop, "from Graz to Kyoto". 野澤 was drawn to Austrian culture through piano lessons, went to Vienna at 22 and trained at the café houses Oberlaa and L. Heiner, learned bread-making at Wandinger in southern Germany, opened Neues in Japan in 1999 and received the recipes from Robert Edegger in 2012. A September 2026 diner remembers the shop near Mansei-bashi in Tokyo and writes that it has moved twice. Opened in Kyoto on 19 September 2020 (Tabelog). · Official site: 「いまを生きる伝統」 — a living tradition, not mere repetition. · Handkaiser; Sachertorte; Kipferl and pretzels.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: an Austrian bakery of wheat and rye breads, pretzels, croissants and cakes (official site; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: butter croissants and Danishes, cream-filled cornets, Sachertorte with cream (2026 reviews); ask about plain breads such as pretzels or rye.
places.hours: Official site and Tabelog: 10:00–18:00; closed Wednesday and Thursday. Products can be reserved; café seats cannot (Tabelog). Take-out is paid first, drinks ordered at the table (October 2026); breads often sell out by lunchtime on holidays (October 2026). Café with a terrace; non-smoking; parking …

places.n: ATELIER PAGES KYOTO (アトリエ パージュ 京都)
places.hood: Kawaramachi-Oike, above Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn — 94 m from the station
places.cu: Pâtisserie, gelato and chocolate from the chef of Paris’s Restaurant Pages (official site) · financiers (classic and chocolate), chocolates of Nicolas Berger couverture, gelato (chocolate 82%, Colombia 100%, seasonal fruit with fromage blanc, coffee) (official site) · canelé, Basque cheesecake, croissants and croffins ¥450, mango-coconut croissant ¥1,500, hojicha pudding (2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Pâtisserie & gelato · Kawaramachi-Oike] The Kyoto atelier of Ryuji Teshima, whose Restaurant Pages in Paris holds a Michelin star: AOP-butter financiers best warmed at home, chocolates, and gelato that diners say tastes of the fruit and cacao itself, to take away or eat in. Reviewers rave about the gelato and Basque cheesecake; one found the canelé and financier milder than hoped. Cashless only. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: 手島 竜司 (Ryuji Teshima, per the official site) · Owner-chef of RESTAURANT PAGES in Paris, whose products this atelier sells (official site) · From 熊本県 (official site). · Per the official site: began training at 19 in a French restaurant in Kumamoto, qualified as a sommelier at 23, moved to France at 26 and trained at starred restaurants including the then three-star Lucas Carton in Paris; studied meat at Boucherie Hugo Desnoyer and produce at Terroir d’Avenir; opened RESTAURANT PAGES near the Arc de Triomphe in the 16th arrondissement in 2014 at 37; named "Grand Chef de Demain" by Gault&Millau in 2015 and opened the wine bar 116 next door; one Michelin star in 2016, held eight years running; appointed a goodwill ambassador of Kumamoto in 2016; opened ATELIER PAGES KYOTO in July 2023. · Official site: an atelier for Paris and Kyoto, two cities of layered history, bringing "new esprit" from a Japanese chef shaped in France. · Financiers; gelato; chocolates.
places.gfd: Ask. Financiers, croissants, canelés and cakes are wheat; the gelato and chocolates may suit, but no gluten information is given (official site; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Butter financiers, croissants and cheesecake are not vegan; some gelato flavours (cacao, coconut) may be dairy-free — no information given (official site; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: Thu–Tue 10:00–18:00; closed Wednesday; hours may change. Cashless payment only — cards, IC cards and QR (Tabelog). Take-out by mobile order (official site). A booking-only café upstairs opened in February 2024 and a May 2024 notice paused it; the site still links café booking, and a Septem…

places.n: ぎおん石 京そば処 (Gion Ishi Kyo Soba Dokoro)
places.hood: Foot of the Yasaka Shrine steps, Gion — 5 min from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cu: Kyoto soba and udon (Tabelog; 2024–26 reviews) · zaru soba ¥800 (January 2026) · tempura soba hot or cold, tempura zaru soba, tempura bukkake soba · big kakiage soba of shrimp, onion, burdock and maitake with a tempura egg · oyako tofu soba with chicken and egg · duck soba · herring soba · soba with small shrimp and yuba · Kyoto-style beef sukiyaki with soba or udon (2024–26 reviews)
places.notes: [Soba · Gion, a quiet room above a stone shop] A calm soba room on the third floor of the Gion Ishi building, a gem and stone shop right below the Yasaka Shrine steps — ride the lift at the back of the shop, past the 2nd-floor café. Firm, cold zaru soba (¥800), a huge kakiage soba, duck or herring soba, and a beef sukiyaki with soba or udon, to jazz in the background. Few tourists find it, though a queue can form. Closed Wednesday and every other Thursday.
places.chef: Not named in any source found · Part of the Gion Ishi building at the foot of the Yasaka Shrine steps: a stone and gem shop on the 1st floor, the café Kissa Ishi on the 2nd and this soba room on the 3rd (2025–26 reviews). · Kakiage soba; zaru soba.
places.gfd: Ask. Soba and udon in soy-based dashi with tempura and kakiage; buckwheat noodles usually contain some wheat and no gluten information is published (2024–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, but the broth is dashi-based and most bowls add chicken, duck, beef, herring, shrimp or egg; no ingredient list is published (Tabelog; 2025–26 reviews).
places.hours: 11:30–19:00 (last order 18:30); closed Wednesday and every other Thursday (Tabelog). Bookings taken; can be a wait at busy times (Tabelog; August 2026). 20 seats: 12 at tables and 8 at the counter; non-smoking; cards; English menu; children welcome (Tabelog). On the 3rd floor of the Gion Ishi build…

places.hood: Alley off Higashinotoin south of Shijo — 2 min from Shijo Stn
places.cu: Wine bar with Italian and Japanese plates at night and a hamburg-steak lunch (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · lunch: classic hamburg steak (200 g) with demi-glace or a daily sauce, three obanzai, rice or bread and miso soup ¥1,300; comparison of the classic and a duck-and-negi hamburg (100 g each) with demi-glace and Kujo-negi sauce ¥1,700; extra rice ¥150 (April–October 2026) · dinner: three kinds of p…
places.notes: [Wine bar · Shijo-Karasuma, a one-man alley wine bar] A small wine bar down a narrow alley near Shijo-Higashinotoin, run single-handed by a quiet owner. At lunch it is a hamburg-steak shop — ¥1,300 for a 200 g steak with three homemade obanzai, rice and miso soup, or a classic-and-duck tasting for ¥1,700. At night it turns to wine, with prosciutto, foie gras pâté and ravioli, and an all-you-can-drink course. ¥330 charge at dinner. Sister bar: 葡萄酒堂 musica. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: 川口 真哉 · Owner (the invoice holder), who runs the shop alone (April and September 2026 reviews) · The invoice register lists an individual, 川口 真哉, for the shop’s invoice number. Reviewers describe an owner who runs the place alone, reserved but considerate (April 2026), with a well-kept range of wines (March 2026). Opened 14 February 2020 (Tabelog). A sister bar, 葡萄酒堂 musica, appears in the Tabelog crawl. · Hamburg steak lunch with obanzai; wine.
places.gfd: Ask. Lunch is hamburg steak with demi-glace and rice or bread; dinner brings ravioli, pâté and meat; no gluten information is published — the shop asks guests to mention allergies when booking (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: hamburg steaks of beef and duck, prosciutto, foie gras pâté and meat dishes; the obanzai sides have no published ingredients (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–13:30, café 13:30–16:00, dinner 17:00–24:00 (Tabelog lists last orders 23:00 food and 23:30 drinks, but also notes dinner last order 21:30); closed Sunday (Tabelog). No bookings for drinks-only or dessert-only café visits; tell allergies when booking (Tabelog). Dinner charge ¥330 per pe…

places.hood: Nakamachi-dori north of Ebisugawa, near the Imperial Palace — 6 min from Jingu-Marutamach…
places.cu: Seasonal Kyoto kappo, famous for ayu the owner catches himself (2025–26 reviews) · summer: live ayu as sashimi and grilled twice over charcoal so even the bones can be eaten, wild ayu from Wakayama compared with Lake Biwa ayu, ayu rice cooked with salt and sake only, botan-hamo soup, wild Amakusa turtle soup (July 2025 – September 2026) · spring: hassun of kogomi with sesame, junsai and koi with …
places.notes: [Kappo · Marutamachi, the angler chef's ayu] A small kappo near the Imperial Palace, formerly on Kawaramachi, where the owner — a keen angler who fishes for ayu on the weekly day off — cooks seasonal Kyoto dishes with the chef’s wife serving. Summer is the time: live ayu as sashimi and double-grilled until you can eat it bones and all, a side-by-side of wild and Lake Biwa ayu, and ayu rice to finish; spring brings young ayu and pea rice, autumn matsutake. Hard to book without an introduction; about ¥15,000–30,000. Closed Monday per regulars.
places.chef: Owner-chef (not named) and the owner’s wife, the okami, with a part-time student (September 2026) · A July 2025 regular has known the restaurant since it was on Kawaramachi-dori and says the owner, an expert angler, goes ayu fishing on Mondays, the regular day off, lately at Amano in Nara; a September 2026 diner says the couple caught the day’s live ayu in a river in Wakayama. A May 2026 diner praises the chef’s craft and the okami’s attentive service. Many guests are regulars (September 2026). · Ayu, live and grilled twice; ayu rice.
places.gfd: Ask when booking. Seasonal Kyoto kappo with dashi and soy; no gluten information is published (2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a fish-led kappo — ayu, hamo, turtle, shellfish — with dashi (2025–26 reviews).
places.hours: Hours are not published; a July 2025 regular says the shop is closed on Monday, when the owner goes ayu fishing. Reservation only; Tabelog notes it is not strictly introduction-only but bookings may be hard without one. AMEX accepted; non-smoking (Tabelog). Run by the owner and the owner’s wife wit…

places.hood: South of Yasaka Shrine, Higashiyama — 10 min from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cu: Chinese course of about 25 small dishes on the theme of the imperial Manhan banquet, with Kyoto produce (official site) · standard course, 25 dishes, ¥13,000 (dinner, 18:00–22:00), e.g. caviar rice noodles, seasonal vegetables with ham sauce, jellyfish, charcoal char siu, shark-fin pie, matsutake steamed soup, saliva chicken, water dumplings, Hong Kong noodles, hairy-crab spring rolls, Chinese gr…
places.notes: [Chinese · Higashiyama, 25 small dishes in an old townhouse] A modern Chinese restaurant in an old Kyoto townhouse south of Yasaka Shrine, opened in November 2024. Chef 佐藤 廉歩, trained in Ginza and Nishi-Azabu, sends out about 25 small plates in one course (¥13,000 at dinner) — caviar rice noodles, charcoal char siu, shark-fin pie, hairy-crab spring rolls, mango-mayo shrimp, Peking duck — with a sommelier's wine pairing from a 500-bottle cellar below. Michelin-listed. 10% service; a ¥3,000 water charge if you order no drinks. Two dinner seatings.
places.chef: 佐藤 廉歩 (Sato Renho) · Chef (official site); operator 株式会社ｐａｎｇａｅａ (the invoice holder) · Per the official site: chef 佐藤 廉歩 honed skills in Ginza and Nishi-Azabu, and cooks traditional Chinese methods with a modern sense; the restaurant offers a course themed on the Manhan banquet, Kyoto ingredients, wine and Chinese-tea pairings chosen by a sommelier, and a cellar of over 500 wines beneath the old townhouse. The invoice number belongs to 株式会社ｐａｎｇａｅａ (NTA corporate-number site). Listed in the Michelin Guide (official site news, April 2025; July 2026 review). Opened 10 November 2024 (Tabelog). · Per the official site: each plate brings the chef’s own sense to traditional methods and carefully chosen Kyoto produce. · Manhan-themed 25-dish course; shark fin; Peking duck.
places.gfd: Ask when booking — the shop asks for allergies in advance and may not adapt on the day. The 25-dish course includes dumplings, spring rolls, noodles, XO and black-vinegar sauces (official site).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a Chinese course of shark fin, char siu, saliva chicken, seafood, lamb and beef (official site).
places.hours: Lunch from 12:00; dinner in two seatings at 18:00 and 19:30 (official site: dinner courses 18:00–22:00, about 2.5 hours); open daily except 31 December and 1 January (Tabelog). places.cu: Tofu kaiseki in a machiya of 130–150 years (both figures appear on the site), with oboro yudofu refills in every course (official site; 2025–2026 reviews) · lunch 尾花 ¥5,000 (lunch only); 白河 ¥8,000; 清水 ¥12,000; 六波羅 vegetarian ¥12,000 — all plant-based; 清水G.F. and 六波羅G.F. gluten-free ¥13,000, by reservation three days ahead (official site, tax and service included) · autumn specials 6 November–6 De…
places.notes: [Tofu kaiseki · Higashioji, vegan and gluten-free courses] The Gion branch of a Kyoto tofu restaurant (the other is on Kiyamachi), in an old machiya with a converted storehouse room, between Yasaka Shrine and Kiyomizu-dera. Every course centres on refillable oboro yudofu, with dengaku, yuba and soy-milk dishes around it, from a ¥5,000 lunch. Unusually, there is a fully plant-based course, 六波羅 (no meat, fish, egg, dairy or fish dashi), and gluten-free versions of two courses — book these three days ahead. Open daily.
places.chef: Head chef (unnamed), per the official site · Per the official site: 豆水楼 has two shops, on Kiyamachi (a Taisho-era townhouse on the Kamo River, with a summer yuka) and in Gion (a machiya with a storehouse room, 古蔵庵). The site says gluten-free courses were started in response to many requests, mostly from visitors from abroad. A February 2025 regular has come for 22 years. · Tofu kaiseki in a traditional machiya; the vegetarian 六波羅 is presented as a new Kyoto tofu kaiseki (official site). · Oboro yudofu; vegetarian and gluten-free tofu kaiseki.
places.gfd: Some GF options: two gluten-free kaiseki courses, 清水G.F. and 六波羅G.F. (¥13,000), made without wheat flour and with wheat-free seasonings, tofu dengaku replacing nama-fu; book at least three days ahead. The regular courses use nama-fu (wheat gluten) and fried dishes. Cross-contact in the shared kitchen is not addressed — ask (official site).
places.vgd: Some vegan options: the 六波羅 course (¥12,000) uses no meat, fish, egg or dairy, and its dashi uses no niboshi or katsuobushi; a gluten-free version exists. Other courses include fish and Kyoto chicken (official site).
places.hours: Official site (Gion shop page): lunch 11:30–15:00 and dinner 17:00–22:00 Monday–Saturday, dinner to 21:30 on Sundays and holidays (elsewhere on the page 21:00); last entry 20:00; no fixed closing day, closed over New Year. Tabelog gives 11:30–14:00 and 17:00–21:30 Monday–Saturday, 12:00–20:30 Sunda…

places.hood: Kamo River west bank at Gojo — 3 min from Keihan Kiyomizu-Gojo Stn

places.notes: [Café · Gojo, the Kamo River from every window] A café in the old efish space on the Kamo River’s west bank at Gojo, where window counters and sofas look straight over the water — in summer, at people wading in the river. Come for a Basque cheesecake (¥700, ¥1,000 with a drink) or a kara-age lunch plate and a hand-drip coffee. Busy at weekends; ordering can be a little confusing. PayPay only; pets on the terrace.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · Tabelog gives the opening as 12 December 2022; an August 2026 reviewer notes it took over the former efish site and found it less cosy than before. · Basque cheesecake; river view.
places.gfd: Ask. Basque cheesecakes, gâteau chocolat, financier cake, pudding and parfaits, plus kara-age and hamburg lunch plates and sandwiches; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Hand-drip coffee and Americano suit; the cakes, pudding and lunch plates use dairy, egg or meat (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 10:00–18:00 daily; irregular closures (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). PayPay only — no cards or e-money (Tabelog). No service charge (Tabelog, original text: なし). 18 seats: window counter facing the Kamo River, sofas, counter and a terrace where pets are allowed (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Non-s…

places.notes: [Rice · Yasaka Shrine, breakfast built on the rice] The restaurant of a Kyoto rice merchant, right in front of Yasaka Shrine, where the star is the white rice — cooked in pots, refilled as often as you like, then served as crunchy okoge and finally as chazuke. A grilled-fish set (¥1,980–2,480) carries it. Book a breakfast slot: you order outside ten minutes early and have 50 minutes at the table. Dinner Friday–Sunday only.
places.chef: Operated by 株式会社八代目儀兵衛 (rice merchant) · Per the operator’s job listing (en-japan): a Kyoto rice merchant founded in 1787 (incorporated 2006) that runs three rice restaurants — Kyoto Gion, Tokyo Ginza and OMOYA. An October 2026 reviewer notes Kyoto restaurants and hotels that serve 八代目儀兵衛 rice. · Pot-cooked white rice; Saikyo-miso sablefish.
places.gfd: Ask. Pot-cooked white rice with grilled fish (Saikyo-miso sablefish, salmon), dashimaki, pickles and mentaiko; the miso and soy seasonings are not described for gluten (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: set meals built around grilled fish, egg and dashi (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Breakfast and lunch 8:00–15:00 (food L.O. 14:30) daily; dinner 17:00–20:00 (L.O. 19:15) Friday–Sunday and holidays; lunch on some days only (check the site); irregular closures; per Tabelog, closed in February and August (Tabelog). Reservations recommended; 50-minute seating; arrive 10 minutes earl…

places.notes: [Soba izakaya · Nijo-Tominokoji, open until 2 a.m.] A rare late-night spot south of the Imperial Palace: a counter downstairs and sofas upstairs, a long sake list and careful drinking snacks — sawara tataki, duck with shungiku, crab-miso croquettes — then handmade 100% buckwheat soba to finish, cold as zaru or in hot broth (until it sells out). Fair prices. Smoking is allowed inside. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: Kitchen (unnamed) · Tabelog gives the opening as 29 April 2014. A December 2025 Japanese reviewer calls it a valuable late-opening izakaya in the Goshominami area. · Handmade 100% buckwheat soba; sake.
places.gfd: Ask. The soba is 100% buckwheat, but the dipping sauce and broth are soy-based and not described for gluten, and the menu has tempura, croquettes and fried dishes (2023–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: soba broth and izakaya dishes built on dashi, fish, duck and meat (2023–2026 reviews).
places.hours: 18:00–2:00, Monday–Saturday; closed Sunday; hours may change (Tabelog). Handmade soba until it sells out (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cards and e-money accepted; no QR (Tabelog). 21 seats: 7 at the counter, 14 at tables and sofas upstairs (Tabelog; August 2024). Smoking allowed (Tabe…

places.n: 祇園 かにを喰らう (Gion Kani o Kurau)
places.hood: Gion near Yasaka Shrine and Chion-in — 6 min walk from Gion-Shijo Stn
places.cu: Live-crab specialist run by a Kasumi crab wholesaler founded in 1941, which trucks crabs from the Shibayama and Kasumi ports of Hyogo and keeps the crabs alive until cooking; no seafood but crab (official site) · live Shibayama crab (Matsuba crab) courses from November to March; live Kasumi crab (Benizuwai) from autumn to early summer; Hokkaido hairy crab full course in summer (official site; 202…
places.notes: [Crab · Gion by Chion-in, live crab from Hyogo] A crab-only restaurant near Yasaka Shrine run by a Kasumi crab wholesaler (in business since 1941) that trucks live crabs from Shibayama and Kasumi ports and cooks each to order: Matsuba (Shibayama) crab in winter, Benizuwai in spring, hairy crab in summer — as sashimi, grilled, shabu-shabu and zosui. Lunch courses are about ¥12,000–14,000, or try the crab bowl finished with dashi. Reviews range from "worth the price" to a March 2026 diner who felt overcharged and was served Kasumi crab instead of the Shibayama on the menu. Reservation only.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed) and staff · Per the official site and Tabelog: a crab wholesaler at the Shibayama and Kasumi fishing ports since 1941 (Tabelog EN gives "Kani Nakaori Kaneni", supplying ryokans and restaurants in Kasumi), focusing on the "Shibayama crab" brand of top-graded Matsuba crab, opened this Gion restaurant in February 2024; crabs are kept alive in tanks at the port and delivered by the company's own trucks. An August 2026 reviewer found the owner kind. · "Live, ultimate crab" — crabs alive until just before cooking (official site). · Live Matsuba crab; crab bowl with crab-miso shell.
places.gfd: Ask. Crab courses with sashimi, grilled and shabu-shabu crab, crab-miso in the shell, crab bowls with dashi, zosui and ramen; no gluten information (official site; 2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a crab-only restaurant — every course is built on live crab (official site).
places.hours: Daily 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:00 (food last order 20:00); closed the day after a holiday, with variable closures (Tabelog). places.notes: [Yakiniku · Gion opposite Chion-in, grilled for you at the counter] The Gion counter of a long-loved Kitano Hakubaicho hormone house: one omakase course of beef and offal grilled in front of you and served at just the right moment — fresh tongue, Chateaubriand, abomasum with green onion — ending with a curry many ask seconds of. About ¥10,000–15,000; drinks are Gion-priced. Chatty owner and staff, but one 2024 newcomer felt out of place among regulars. Hidden at the back of the building. No children. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed) and staff · Per Tabelog: the owner of a popular, long-established yakiniku restaurant in Kitano Hakubaicho opened this Gion shop, serving one omakase course of cuts grilled at the counter; opened 1 June 2021. A November 2024 reviewer recalls the parent Ebata near Senbon Imadegawa, famous for gyū-ranegi. Reviewers describe an entertaining manager (July 2025), owner and staff who talk with regulars and first-timers (March 2023), and "the couple running the restaurant" (March 2026). · A traditional hormone house's flavours served as a counter course (Tabelog). · Omakase meat course; curry to finish.

Coffee and tea run about ¥400–500. Popular with visitors from abroad, so busy at times. Open daily 9:00–18:00.

places.notes: [Sake hall · Takoyakushi Karasuma, 40 sakes in a townhouse] A renovated townhouse near Shijo Karasuma turned into a sake hall: forty-odd sakes from across Japan, poured by the half-gō or in tasting flights, with knowledgeable staff to guide you, and inventive snacks — octopus or kara-age with shibazuke tartar, yuba pizza, fig and blue-cheese spring rolls. The ¥450 otoshi includes a glass of sake. Counter, tables, a standing area and a courtyard; open from 3 pm at weekends. Drinks can add up. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · Per Tabelog: a renovated Kyoto townhouse with a courtyard, more than 40 sakes chosen from across Japan and changing daily, creative Japanese dishes, and weekend daytime drinking. Lunch is a casual ¥3,000–4,000; dinners à la carte run higher, and a couple of reviewers found value only fair. No service charge. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: Chef and pizzaioli (unnamed in the sources) · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): Neapolitan pizza from a custom wood-fired oven by craftsmen who took first place in the Japan representative qualifiers, and fresh pasta by an award-winning chef; opened 27 October 2020. An August 2025 diner noted a pizzaiolo with experience in Italy. · Neapolitan pizza; fresh pasta.

places.notes: [Obanzai & oden izakaya · Gion Shinbashi, a 150-year-old machiya] One of four Kyoya Kiyomizu izakaya, this one in a renovated Gion Shinbashi townhouse with a counter downstairs and tatami rooms above. Order the obanzai platter, Kyoto oden in a gentle kombu dashi, yuba sashimi and nama-fu dengaku, with Kyoto sake. Courses from about ¥5,000, good value for Gion. Open 16:00–22:30 daily; 2-hour limit when busy.

places.notes: [Japanese bistro · Kawaramachi Marutamachi, one cook and a clay pot] A ten-seat counter north of Marutamachi run by a single cook, with a long seasonal à la carte list — sashimi, vegetables in kuzu sauce, agedashi sesame tofu — and rice cooked to order in a clay pot (order it first; it takes half an hour), perhaps shirasu and shiso or sakura shrimp and corn. Gentle, careful cooking for about ¥5,000–10,000. Closed Monday; Sunday from 13:00.

places.notes: [Udon · near Kawaramachi, chewy handmade udon and crisp tempura] A modern machiya-style udon shop opened in December 2025, with a noodle-making room upstairs. The firm, chewy udon comes cold with big shrimp and vegetable tempura, in curry, or as a cheese-and-yolk carbonara; about ¥1,500–2,400. No bookings — sign up on the waiting list (often an hour in the evening) and wander off. Some found the broth and service uneven. Open daily.
places.chef: Udon shop; staff unnamed · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): freshly made, chewy udon with a rich bonito dashi and seasonal vegetable tempura, made in a noodle room on the second floor; opened 3 December 2025. places.notes: [Set meals · Sanjo-Takakura, one man and one soup, three dishes] Up three floors among antiques, a quiet owner cooks and serves alone: one ¥1,000 set a day — a simmered main, two small sides, brown rice, miso soup, pickles — gentle, vegetable-rich Kyoto home cooking that diners call nourishing. Expect a wait at noon and in the evening. A hot May 2026 day with only a fan was uncomfortable. Cash only. Closed Wednesday.

places.notes: [Curry ramen · Sanjo-Takakura, an old-style diner] Up the stairs beside the Museum of Kyoto, a nostalgic diner known for curry ramen: a thick, dashi-rich curry broth clinging to thin noodles, with fukujinzuke to stir in and rice for the last of the soup. Daily sets pair shoyu or miso ramen with a mini curry. Regulars love it; one found the noodles unremarkable. Open late on weekdays. Smoking allowed; no cards.

A September 2026 reviewer calls it a long-established ramen shop; an October 2026 diner was greeted by two friendly women and noticed a noodle-making machine by the second-floor entrance. · Curry ramen; curry rice.

places.notes: [Sukiyaki · Kiyamachi by the Kamo, Omi beef the Kansai way] An old townhouse down a narrow lane off Kiyamachi, with tatami rooms and terrace seats in summer, where staff — sometimes the owner — cook Omi-beef sukiyaki at your table the Kansai way, searing the beef in its fat with sugar and soy, then serving it with egg, Kujo negi and yuba. About ¥10,000–15,000; some find it a little dear for the amount of meat. Popular with visitors. Open nightly.

places.notes: [Charcoal kaiseki · south of the Imperial Palace, a new eleven-seat counter] Opened in November 2025 in a renovated townhouse, this counter's young chef — trained at Sumibi Kappo Ifuki — builds an omakase around the charcoal: salt-aged Asahi shrimp, tuna head simmered for three days, sawara and sirloin cap seared over binchotan, then clay-pot rice crowned with firefly squid and uni. The chef told a March 2026 diner the restaurant is still evolving. · Charcoal-cooked fish and meat; clay-pot rice.

places.notes: [Taiwanese · Gion, dumplings in a back lane] A tiny, retro Taiwanese kitchen in a Gion back lane, a favourite second stop. Order the homemade boiled dumplings — twelve to a plate, heavy on chives — then squid balls, garlic-soy clams or danzai noodles, with warm Shaoxing wine. Some dishes are very spicy and salty. About ¥2,000–5,000. Cash only. Closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Kaiseki · Gojo, a ryotei of 350 years] A long-established Kyoto ryotei south of Gojo, more than 350 years old, with a courtyard and rooms for two to thirty — a favourite for family celebrations and memorial meals. Full kaiseki runs about ¥8,000–30,000; the mini kaiseki lunch (about ¥4,000–5,000) is served in the big upstairs hall. Seasonal, gently seasoned cooking with a few modern touches like an almond-batter tempura. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Long-established ryotei; chefs unnamed · Per the official site: a Kyoto-cuisine ryotei founded more than 350 years ago in Higashiyama Gojo. Reviewers speak of a history of about 360 years and a well-kept building (November–December 2025), and of a sister patisserie, Famille de Chie Hari Se, whose roll cakes appear at dessert (November 2025). · Seasonal kaiseki; mini kaiseki lunch.

places.notes: [Japanese omakase · Shijo-Karasuma, behind an izakaya] Walk through the busy fish izakaya 鯛之鯛 and open the door at the back: an eight-seat hinoki counter where the owner, twelve years at 山玄茶, starts every course with a broth made in front of you from deep well water and bonito. Seasonal, beautifully plated dishes; lunch ¥11,000, dinner about ¥20,000. A Michelin Guide Selected restaurant. Reservation only; no strong perfume.
places.chef: 古川 毅 (owner, per a press release; no reading in a source) · Owner-chef (press release: 店主 古川毅) · Per a press release on san-tatsu.jp: owner 古川毅 trained for twelve years at the Kyoto restaurant 山玄茶 before opening 蛸薬師ふるかわ; the restaurant was listed as a Michelin Guide Selected Restaurant and began full lunch service in November 2025; it sits behind the lively izakaya 鯛之鯛 near Hankyu Karasuma and Shijo stations, with a single-plank hinoki counter. Opened 11 June 2024 (Tabelog). Reviewers in 2026 praise the owner’s warmth and the sake recommendations. · Broth made to order from well water and bonito; seasonal omakase.

places.notes: [French bistro · Oike, a Paris bistro’s Kyoto namesake] A small two-floor bistro in a former obanzai house, named after Chez Michel in Paris, where the chef trained three years under Thierry Breton. Everyday Parisian cooking with little butter or cream — rillettes, terrines, mushroom potage, roast Kyoto pork — and desserts from Blé Sucré training, by A/B/C course or à la carte. Lunch from about ¥3,000. One diner found the small rooms full of cooking smells by dessert (December 2024). Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: 大川 (surname only, from the official site: シェフ大川; no given name or reading) · Chef (official site) · Per the official site: the chef trained at hotels in Japan, then spent five years in Paris, three of them under chef Thierry Breton at the bistro Chez Michel, and learned desserts at the pâtisserie Blé Sucré in the 12th arrondissement; on opening in Kyoto, the mentor urged the chef to become "the Chez Michel of Japan". Michelin Guide Kansai 2014 Bib Gourmand. Opened 29 April 2009 in the building that was the obanzai restaurant 三月 (Tabelog). · Official site: bistro cooking that knows its ingredients — meat on the bone, butter and cream kept down, finished with good bouillon — eaten happily, even with the fingers. · Bistro courses; Paris-Brest; rillettes and terrines.

places.cu: Quiet, traditional Kyoto kaiseki in a machiya, built on dashi from well water the chef draws each morning (official site) · lunch course ¥8,500; dinner ¥13,500, ¥16,500 or ¥19,800, tax and service included (official site) · seen: nagaimo tofu with blue crab and ikura, matsuba crab with yuba, sweetfish and daikon soup, sashimi of Setouchi sea bream, tuna and bonito, grilled barracuda pressed sushi…
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Oshikoji-Takakura, a quiet chef and well water] A machiya south of the Imperial Palace where a quiet chef, once an opening cook at 祇園 なん波, serves textbook Kyoto kaiseki with little meat, its dashi made from well water fetched each morning. Seven counter seats and one private room; lunch ¥8,500, dinner from ¥13,500 all-in. Regulars return every season; reservations are hard to get. A 2022 diner found some seasoning salty. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: 岡田 晃 (Okada Akira, per the official site) · Owner-chef (official site) · Born 13 September 1979 in 長野県千曲市 (official site). · Per the official site: began in 1999 at the local kaiseki restaurant 竹葉亭, trained at 祇園はやかわ from 2002, joined 祇園 なん波 as opening staff in 2006 and served as its simmering cook, and opened 押小路岡田 with about six counter seats in June 2018; in 2021 moved across Oshikoji to a larger machiya with a gallery upstairs; draws dashi water from springs around the shop every morning; also caters boxed meals for guests of the hotel 東山 四季花木. A January 2022 reviewer saw the owner working almost alone at the old shop, with more help after the move. · Official site: 「ただ直向きに 丹念に、京都の 想い出の料理 こしらえます」 — true flavour lies in well water, ingredients that meet in season and a faint scent of dashi, not costly ingredients or showmanship. · Seasonal Kyoto kaiseki; pressed sushi; dashi.

Staff are kind and explain what keeps. Hours not published — check before going. Smoking allowed.

places.notes: [Galettes & crêpes · south of the Imperial Palace] A bright, relaxed Breton crêperie on Ebisugawa-dori: crisp buckwheat galettes (ham, cheese, egg; peach and prosciutto in summer) and chewy sweet crêpes like Échiré butter and sugar. Lunch sets about ¥2,000. Cash only; book at weekends. Open daily from 10:00.

places.notes: [Yakitori standing bar · near Karasuma-Bukkoji] A clean, lively standing bar hidden in an alley near Shijo-Karasuma: small, well-grilled skewers, steamed tsukune that eats like shumai, and a ¥500 chicken ramen to finish. places.notes: [Café · Gojo Ohashi, rice burgers by the river] A small blue-and-grey café at the foot of Gojo Ohashi whose big windows look straight onto the Kamo River. Rice burgers with a nori-and-dashi aroma and bread sandwiches (the mackerel one is a regular favourite) are made to order and come in burger bags — eat in, or take the bag down to the riverbank. Art on the walls. Cashless only — no cash; open daily 9:00–17:00.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · Tabelog gives the opening as 10 February 2020. · Rice burgers; mackerel sandwich.

places.cu: Kyoto kaiseki and lunches beside the Kamo River, with a summer yuka (2025–2026 reviews) · lunch from about ¥1,890 (April 2026) to ¥2,900 + 10% (September 2026): white-miso hot pot with cheese to add; a choice of nama-fu and yuba gratin or pork kakuni, Kyoto obanzai, rice with chirimenjako (2026) · mini kaiseki of Kyoto classics; hōjicha pudding (July 2026) · dinner courses: hassun of octopus and …
places.notes: [Kyoto kaiseki · Kiyamachi, lunch on the Kamo River yuka] A riverside restaurant on Kiyamachi whose yuka over the Kamo River runs into mid-October. places.notes: [Kappo · Fuyacho-Nijo, a couple’s counter with an Okinawan accent] A calm, dimly lit ten-seat L-shaped counter west of Kyoto City Hall, run by a couple, where you can take the omakase or order à la carte from the day’s list — sashimi, clam soup, hamo and matsutake, fig tempura — and the husband cooks in front of you. Reviewers spot Okinawan touches such as sea grapes, goya and brown-sugar sorbet. Easy for solo diners; ¥800 otoshi if you skip the course.
places.chef: Chef (unnamed) and the chef’s wife, who run it as a couple · Reviewers from May 2025 to August 2026 describe a counter run by a couple — “a young couple” (June 2025), “a quiet husband and wife team” (May 2025). Two reviewers think the husband may be from Okinawa (June 2025: “Perhaps due to the owner’s Okinawan background”; August 2026: “The husband appears to be from Okinawa”), and the August 2026 reviewer adds that neither seems to be originally from Kyoto. A November 2025 diner wondered where “the charming lady of the restaurant” came from. · Seasonal à la carte kappo; Okinawan-accented touches.

Start with a few appetizers — grilled salmon belly, simmered collar, whale bacon — then an omakase of ten or order piece by piece; finish with clam-heavy red miso soup. Book ahead; closed Sunday.

Lunch sets run from ¥1,000 to multi-cut gozen; dinner courses from ¥6,500, the top ones adding A5 wagyu. Some diners find the cuts small for the price; most love the freshness. Closed Tuesday.

places.notes: [Udon · Kyoto Station, iriko udon from 7 a.m.] A busy udon counter on the second basement level of JR Kyoto Station, by the east exit, open from 7:00 — handy before a Shinkansen. Homemade noodles come in a clear iriko broth made from Kujukushima anchovies; the hit is the creamy chicken-and-egg curry udon (about ¥900), and kake udon is about ¥400. Help yourself to free tenkasu and crunchy fried iriko. Buy a ticket, order, then grab a seat. Open daily.

The invoice number belongs to 株式会社神戸ゴマルゴ (NTA corporate-number site); つくもうどん 天神橋店 in Osaka is the only other branch in the Tabelog crawl. · Chicken-and-egg curry udon; kake udon with free fried iriko.

Dinner only; closed Thursday.

places.notes: [Tendon · Higashioji by Yasaka Shrine, fifteen bites in a bowl] A nine-seat café-like counter north of Yasaka Shrine frying tendon to order: the "Hannari" bowl of fifteen bite-sized tempura — a big shrimp, nama-fu, cheese, scallop, vegetables — is ¥1,600, with eel as an upgrade and a chilled tencha finish for ¥300 more. Bright, friendly staff; popular with visitors from abroad; queues at opening. Closed Monday (sometimes open — check Google Maps).
places.chef: Chef with a Japanese-cuisine background (unnamed), Manager and staff · Reviewers in 2026 describe a tendon shop "crafted with care by a chef from a Japanese cuisine background" (September 2026), a bright manager and staff (August 2026), a Western-style name and interior, and a room where an August 2026 family were the only Japanese guests. · Hannari Ten-don; chilled tencha.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: wheat-battered tempura over rice with a sweet soy sauce, including nama-fu (wheat gluten) tempura (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: tendon bowls with shrimp, scallop, eel and cheese tempura; tencha finished with dashi (2026 reviews).

places.hood: Sakaimachi just south of Oike — 5 min walk from Karasuma Oike Stn
places.cu: Café of the Babaghuri brand below its three-room inn: muffins and cookies baked daily with no sugar, egg or dairy, hand-drip organic coffee, herb teas and gelato (official site) · lunch: MALDA curry of seasonal vegetables and lentil dal with organic brown and black rice, four sides and raita — vegetarian, the Jurgen Lehl company-canteen favourite (official site; September 2026); Taiwanese-style c…
places.notes: [Café · Sakaimachi Oike, egg-, dairy- and sugar-free baking] The Babaghuri brand's café under its three-room inn: a calm, wooden room where everything sweet — muffins, cookies, gelato — is made without sugar, egg or dairy, with gluten-free rice-flour muffins. Lunch is a vegetarian lentil-and-vegetable curry on brown and black rice (raita on the side) or a Taiwanese congee; herb teas from Lehl's Ishigaki farm. Cards only from ¥5,000. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
places.chef: Café staff (unnamed) · Per the official site: MALDA opened in July 2018 on Anekoji as a café and inn embodying the life philosophy of Babaghuri; desserts are baked in-house every morning without sugar, egg or dairy, and the lunch curry is a favourite from Jurgen Lehl's company canteen; seasonal fruit and herbs come from Jurgen Lehl's farm on Ishigaki Island. The inn upstairs takes three groups a day. · "Simple, yet born over time from facing people, things and the environment honestly" — Babaghuri's philosophy of living (official site). · Egg- and dairy-free muffins; vegetarian curry; congee.
places.gfd: GF options: the official menu labels two rice-flour muffins gluten-free (maple; matcha with adzuki), and the almond gelato is made with rice flour; the lunch curry comes with organic brown and black rice. Wheat muffins (maple, banana-cocoa-coconut) are baked in the same kitchen every day, so ask about cross-contact (official site, 2026; October 2026 review).
places.vgd: Some vegan options: all desserts are made with no sugar, egg or dairy (official menu), and the gelatos are dairy-free. The lunch curry is vegetarian but served with raita (yogurt), and the chai contains milk — the menu says "not vegan" (official site, 2026).
places.hours: Wednesday to Sunday 11:30–19:00, lunch 11:30–14:00; closed Monday and Tuesday (official site). Tabelog gives 11:30–17:00. places.hood: Kojinguchi, a block west of the Kamo — 3 min walk from the Kojinguchi bus stop
places.cu: Second-floor café roasting and selling its own coffee (August 2025) · Kamogawa blend, a deep roast with a hint of sweetness; lightly roasted coffees brewed cup by cup (2025–2026 reviews) · scone set with fresh cream, toast, smoothie set with yogurt, fruit and toast (2025–2026 reviews) · cakes such as apple crumble (May 2026) · onion gratin with cheesy hamburg steak; lasagna after 15:00 (June 2026…
places.notes: [Café · Kojinguchi, house-roast coffee upstairs] A high-ceilinged second-floor café on a quiet street near Kojinguchi and the Kamo, with colored-glass windows you open yourself, rakugo posters, books and magazines — a student-quarter coffee house roasting its own beans. The Kamogawa blend, scones with cream, an apple crumble, a smoothie-and-toast set; lunch is limited. Open late at weekends. Cash only. Closed Thursday.
places.chef: Café staff (unnamed) · Reviewers in 2025–2026 describe a long-running café that roasts and sells its own beans, with high ceilings, colored-glass windows and posters for solo rakugo shows; a May 2026 regular says it was once known as "Sarasa Kamogawa" and thinks its operation may have changed (not confirmed elsewhere). · Kamogawa blend coffee; scone set.
places.gfd: Ask. Coffee with scones, toast, cakes such as apple crumble, lasagna and a cheesy hamburg-steak gratin; no gluten information (2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Black coffee and a soy-milk chai appear, but the scones come with cream and the food uses cheese, butter and meat; no vegan information (2025–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Kappo · Gion, down a narrow alley] A tiny kappo hidden in one of Gion's narrowest alleys near Yasaka Shrine: seasonal kaiseki with a rich Kansai dashi, finished with kamadaki rice. Mini kaiseki lunch about ¥5,000–6,000; dinner about ¥10,000–19,999. Six counter seats; book. Closed Sunday.

A November 2024 reviewer heard it had held a Michelin star four years in a row but no longer does. · Mini kaiseki lunch; kamadaki rice.
places.gfd: Ask when booking — the shop asks about likes, dislikes and foods guests cannot eat (August 2025); dashi-based kappo with tempura; no gluten information.
places.vgd: Not vegan: kappo of fish on dashi (2024–26 reviews).

places.notes: [Izakaya · near Sanjo and Kyoto City Hall] One of Kyoto's hardest-to-book izakaya, loved by restaurant people after hours: eleven seats and a stream of small, deeply flavoured plates — cilantro and white-sesame salad, lamb shumai, spiced fried shrimp, Thai-style noodles. About ¥4,000–10,000. Cash only; bookings open monthly; closed Sunday.
places.chef: Tetsu-san (as a November 2025 reviewer calls the chef) · Head chef · Per reviews: a popular izakaya that restaurant workers visit after hours (May 2026); a November 2025 reviewer had eaten the chef's cooking at an inn the chef runs with a friend in Yura before coming here. When the head chef is away on Saturdays the staff run a shorter menu (April 2026). · Cilantro and white-sesame dishes; small plates for drinking.
places.gfd: Ask. Kara-age, fried noodles, shumai and spiced fried dishes; no gluten information (2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan in practice: pork, chicken, lamb, shellfish and oysters run through the menu (2025–26 reviews).
places.hours: Mon–Sat from 18:00 (last order 21:00 per Tabelog); closed Sunday and some other days (Tabelog). A March 2025 reviewer says there is no time limit and the rice is ready around 21:00. places.hood: Yanaginobamba-dori near Oike — 3 min from Karasuma-Oike Stn
places.cu: Two faces: at lunch, Kyoto-style dashimaki rice bowls — a thick, dashi-heavy rolled omelette made in the "Kyomaki" way — with chicken soboro and golden ginger sauce ¥1,430, meat soboro ¥1,430, mentaiko, or eel (half sizes) (2026 reviews); at night, fish from a live tank prepared with ikejime, line-caught wild kue from Nagasaki's Goto Islands as nabe, Awaji fugu, yellowtail shabu-shabu and fish co…
places.notes: [Dashimaki bowls & seafood · near Karasuma-Oike] By day, a queue for rice bowls crowned with a huge, wobbly Kyoto dashimaki omelette (about ¥1,430, cash, no bookings); by night, a fish restaurant with live-tank seafood, Goto-island kue hot pot and fugu, courses from ¥5,000 plus a 10% seat charge. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed; chats with guests at the counter per the operator and reviews) · Per the operator: fish kept alive in tanks and dispatched with ikejime by optical fibre; wild kue line-caught off Nagasaki's Goto Islands shipped alive; fugu from Awaji. A July 2026 reviewer watched the dashimaki made in the "Kyomaki" way, with more dashi and no air. · Kyoto dashimaki rice bowl; kue nabe.
places.gfd: Ask. Dashimaki bowls with dashi, soy-based sauces and soboro; fish courses; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: egg and dashi bowls with chicken, meat or eel; fish courses (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

places.hood: Kawaramachi-Nijo, north of Kyoto City Hall — 5 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn
places.cu: Classic French bistro from an Alsace-trained chef (April 2025): charcuterie platter of liver pâté, rillettes, smoked chicken, pâté de campagne, house roast ham and sauerkraut ¥1,540 per person; thick-cut smoked Shinshu salmon ¥3,080; white or German asparagus with egg sauce; mushroom salad; gazpacho with foie gras and venison; saffron trout; chicken-liver mousse (2024–26 reviews) · omakase course…
places.notes: [French bistro · Kawaramachi-Nijo] A ten-seat bistro run by an Alsace-trained chef since 2010: generous charcuterie, thick-cut smoked salmon, foie gras and game, with good wine. Omakase ¥8,800 or à la carte (portions are large). Book well ahead; dinner only, closed Wednesday and Thursday.
places.chef: Chef (unnamed; trained in Alsace per an April 2025 reviewer) · Opened 12 December 2010 (Tabelog). An April 2025 reviewer calls it a Bib Gourmand bistro run by a chef trained in Alsace; a December 2024 guest returned after about eight years. · Charcuterie; thick-cut smoked salmon.
places.gfd: Ask when booking. Bistro dishes with sauces, pâtés, bread and croutons; the omakase can be adjusted on request (December 2024); no gluten information.
places.vgd: Not vegan: charcuterie, foie gras, venison, salmon and trout (2024–26 reviews).
places.hours: Mon, Tue, Fri, Sat, Sun 17:30–21:30 (last order 19:30); closed Wednesday and Thursday (Tabelog). Bookings needed, often a month or two ahead, also online (2025 reviews). places.hood: Just south of Sanjo, upstairs — 297 m from Karasuma Oike Stn
places.cu: Kyoto’s first granola specialist (official site): organic granola and roasted nuts, acai bowls and ice cream upstairs · nut flavours made with famous Kyoto makers: Gion 原了郭 black shichimi (30 g ¥700, 65 g ¥1,290, August 2025), 九重味噌 white miso, 北尾 black-bean kinako, Uji organic matcha, yatsuhashi cinnamon, Ogawa Coffee, Nile Restaurant curry (official site; 2025–2026 reviews) · acai bowl with frui…
places.notes: [Granola & nuts café · Karasuma-Oike, upstairs] Kyoto’s first granola specialist, up a flight of stairs: organic nuts roasted in Kyoto with black shichimi from 原了郭, white miso, matcha or yatsuhashi cinnamon — boxed for souvenirs, with tastings — and acai bowls or soy-sauce ice cream to eat in. The café closes before the shop. One August 2026 buyer found them good, practical gifts rather than incredible; a black-pepper lover wanted more heat. Closed Tuesday (official site).
places.chef: Nut roasters in its own Kyoto factory (official site); not named · Per the official site: the first granola specialist to open in Kyoto, treating granola as a health and beauty food with almost all-organic ingredients; nuts are roasted one by one by nut craftsmen in its factory in central Kyoto, adjusting for Kyoto’s seasons; flavours made with old Kyoto makers (原了郭 black shichimi, 九重味噌 white miso, 北尾 kinako, Uji matcha); shops in Kyoto and in Tokyo at Yurakucho Marui and Ginza Melsa. · Official site: 「毎日食べてココロもカラダもHAPPYに」 — granola eaten daily to make heart and body happy. · Black-shichimi nuts; organic granola; acai bowls.
places.gfd: Ask. Granola usually contains oats and no gluten information is given; the black-shichimi nuts use an organic gluten-free tamari (official site), but other flavours are not labelled.
places.vgd: Ask. Organic nuts and granola, and soy-milk ice cream (January 2026), may suit; acai bowls come with fruit and granola, but no vegan labelling is given (official site; 2025–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Okonomiyaki & teppan · Shijo-Karasuma, Kyoto-style with a French twist] A stylish counter and sunken-seat room on Nishiki-koji where dashi-rich, fluffy Kyoto-style okonomiyaki shares the teppan with creative plates — avocado with blue cheese, grilled vegetables, Saikyo-miso pork — served on ceramics. Multilingual menus; staff warm and quick. Some found the yakisoba bland and the prices a little high for the taste (2026); you will leave smelling of sauce.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Opened 1 December 2010 (Tabelog). Reviewers in 2026 describe a large teppan behind the counter, a sunken-seat area at the back for parties, regulars at the counter, Kyoto-style okonomiyaki and teppan dishes with French and Italian touches; an August 2026 diner found it via the Kansai TV programme "Yoi Don" featuring the mochi-cheese okonomiyaki. · Kyoto-style okonomiyaki; creative teppan plates.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: wheat-batter okonomiyaki, negiyaki and yakisoba with sauce (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the Kyoto-style okonomiyaki is rich with dashi and topped with bonito flakes (2026 reviews); Tabelog lists vegetarian options — ask.

places.notes: [Japanese & obanzai · Teramachi-Imadegawa, refills on the house] A counter-and-tatami restaurant east of the Imperial Palace run by a chef trained in Okura and Royal hotel kitchens, beloved at lunch for set meals with unlimited obanzai and rice — okara, hijiki, pumpkin, simmered satoimo — beside sashimi, tempura or Saikyo-grilled fish, ¥2,300–4,200. Dinner is kaiseki and soy-milk hot pot. One diner found the seasoning on the sweet side; obanzai are now served by staff rather than self-serve. Lunch cash or PayPay. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: 谷口 寿幸 (owner-chef, per the official site; no reading in a source) · Owner and chef (official site: 店主 / 料理人 谷口 寿幸) · Per the official site: trained in Japanese cooking at the Kobe Oriental Hotel from 1991 (Heisei 3) and in Kyoto cuisine at 京大和, then worked at the Rihga Royal Hotel Tokyo, Hotel Okura Tokyo and Hotel Okura Kyoto, often cooking at the state guesthouse and the Prime Minister’s residence; opened 寺町よしくら independently in 2006 (Heisei 18). The site also lists a sister shop, よしくら 北店, in Kita-ku, and sells Saikyo-marinated black cod and pickles online. · Official site: to keep improving ingredients and menu and never forget the beginner’s mind, thanks to guests and staff. · All-you-can-eat obanzai lunch; Saikyo-miso grilled fish.
places.gfd: Ask. No gluten information; lunch sets with tempura and dashi-simmered obanzai, Saikyo-miso grilled fish (2026 reviews).

places.cu: Ramen, with a breakfast menu from 8:00 (Tabelog) · shoyu “Issunboushi ramen” ¥900 with seasoned egg ¥300 and rice ¥300, a light shellfish shoyu (March 2026) · ¥500 plain morning ramen on a shellfish broth (August 2026) · “Mochi Mochi Enmusubi” morning ramen with mochi and egg, with a takikomi-gohan set; the shoyu broth moved from clam to chicken and seafood (January 2026) · salt, shoyu and white-…
places.notes: [Ramen · below Kiyomizu-dera, breakfast bowls from 8:00] A ten-seat counter on the walk down from Kiyomizu-dera, open from 8:00 with a morning menu (a ¥500 bowl, a vegan bowl, porridge) and then ramen until the day’s 100 bowls are gone. Light shellfish and chicken-seafood shoyu and salt broths, a vegan soy-milk ramen, and showpiece bowls up to a ¥7,000 Wagyu sirloin. Most diners are overseas visitors; multilingual menus. Reviews split: fans of the clean broth, critics of the prices (one 2025 reviewer called the ¥7,000 bowl an overcharge aimed at foreigners), slow turnover and a drop in quality noted in October 2026.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed), Manager (unnamed) · A June 2025 reviewer saw “the male owner” training a new staff member at the counter. A March 2025 reviewer described the team as two Brazilian staff who “seem to be working hard but are not adequately trained” and “one unfriendly Japanese chef”; a January 2026 reviewer wrote that “most of the staff are also from abroad”. An August 2025 family wished more staff besides the manager spoke English. · Light shellfish and chicken-seafood shoyu ramen; morning ramen; a vegan soy-milk ramen.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: every bowl is wheat noodles, the vegan ramen included; the shoyu broths use soy sauce (Savor Japan menu; 2025–2026 reviews).

places.cu: Natural (wild-caught) fish, prepared in front of the counter (2017–2026 reviews) · a ¥15,000 course of ten dishes (November 2025) · the house’s top course: a hassun of ten small dishes, rock oysters, a five-kind sashimi platter, hamo sashimi with plum sauce, grilled and fried dishes, agedashi tofu (July 2026) · dobin-mushi, oysters, swordtip squid sashimi with ginger soy, tempura, seasoned rice (…
places.notes: [Fish · Fuyacho-Nijo, wild fish since 2003] A natural-fish restaurant on a quiet stretch of Fuyacho, open since 2003, where the fish is cut and cooked in front of the counter. Go for a course — ten dishes for ¥15,000, or the top course with a ten-item hassun, rock oysters, five kinds of sashimi and hamo sashimi in summer — or order à la carte, though a 2024 diner found that very expensive (¥8,800 for the sashimi platter). Reviewers like the friendly chef; one asks families with children to stay away.
places.chef: Head chef (unnamed) · A July 2017 reviewer described “the friendly surf-loving chef” who “specializes in natural seafood dishes”; an August 2024 reviewer called the head chef “friendly and approachable”, and a November 2025 guest enjoyed the conversation at the counter. · All-natural fish (April 2024 review). · Natural-fish courses; hamo sashimi in summer.
places.gfd: Ask. Natural-fish courses and à la carte — sashimi with soy sauce, grilled and fried fish, tempura, agedashi tofu, seasoned rice; no gluten information (2024–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a fish restaurant; dobin-mushi and dashi dishes (2024–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Sushi · Nijo-dori, a one-man counter, no perfume] A glass-fronted, café-like room on Nijo-dori, easy to walk past but for the lantern, where the owner works the counter alone: seasonal small dishes, then ten or twelve slim nigiri on small red-vinegar shari, with sake tasting sets. Lunch from ¥3,300, dinner courses from ¥8,800. Reservation only; no perfume or strong scents (a cancellation fee applies) and no children under 13. Some find the service reserved.
places.chef: Morimoto · Owner-chef, working alone · Yamaguchi (Tabelog shop text: “sake from the owner’s hometown, Yamaguchi”) · A January 2026 regular names the master as Mr. Morimoto and writes that the family runs a ryotei. Reviewers describe a one-man counter: “Although it was a one-person operation, the speed of food and drink service was good” (June 2026); the owner was alone on an early May 2026 evening and talked at length with the only guest. A February 2026 reviewer, echoing others, found the service “a bit cold … more welcoming to regular customers”; an August 2026 lunch guest noted little conversation but smooth service. · Ingredients chosen by the owner at the market, carefully prepared and often seasoned with salt (Tabelog shop text). · Sushi courses with creative small dishes; uni ice with sesame tofu; sake tastings.

Buy a ticket at the machine. No cards. Closed Monday; check hours, which have changed.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed) · Per the official site: a ramen shop of "authentic aori (stir-fried) miso" that opened on 1 May (2021, Tabelog) on the south side of the Furukawa-cho arcade, and has appeared in 究極のラーメン 2020 and 2022 (関西版) and a LEAF guide to Kyoto and Shiga ramen. Lunch courses about ¥5,300 (cash only), dinner ¥8,300 with a drink. Reviews mention a Michelin Bib Gourmand (2021–23). Service can be slow when one person runs lunch. Closed Wednesday.

Taste the sake before you order. Book by the day before. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: A couple (unnamed), per a March 2026 review, Manager · Reviewers in 2026 describe "the lovely couple who runs the place" (March 2026), the owner's meticulous craftsmanship and sincere service (March 2026), a manager who explains each dish (March 2026), and staff who explain the sake breweries and styles (June 2026). It works by referral: no phone number is published, and reviewers came by introduction or membership. Smart dress.

places.cu: Family-run counter of à la carte dishes written on paper strips above the counter and taken down once sold out — Japanese, with some Italian touches (2025–2026 reviews) · e.g. sea bream shirako with ponzu ¥1,000, yuba sashimi with canola flowers and wakame ¥850 (April 2026); sweet-shrimp and sea-bream sashimi, deep-fried ayu, fried maitake with fu (September 2025); beef shabu-shabu, fried bamboo …
places.notes: [À la carte counter · Ebisugawa Kawaramachi, kaiseki taste at izakaya prices] A small family-run counter near City Hall where the day's dishes hang on paper strips and come down once sold out: shirako ponzu, yuba sashimi, fried bamboo shoots, agedashi eggplant, eel tempura, a celebrated sesame tofu and tonkatsu chazuke, mostly around ¥1,000. Regulars call it kaiseki-level at izakaya prices, so it is booked out: reservations open a month ahead, two people max. Cash only. Open Tuesday to Friday.

Counter, semi-private seats and kotatsu rooms. QR ordering. Open nightly.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · Per Tabelog: a modern space in a renovated machiya specialising in homemade smoked dishes over mild hickory chips, from bacon and cheese to nama-fu, yuba and fried gyoza, with kamado rice of Kyohoku aigamo rice and a list of sake, wine and whisky. Reviewers in 2026 praise attentive staff and note QR-code ordering. · Smoking for the aroma, not just preservation (Tabelog). · Smoked appetiser platter; smoked nama-fu; kamado rice.

Chicken sashimi and tataki, tulip kara-age and a rich carbonara to finish round it out, with a deep sake list. Courses about ¥5,000. Open to midnight every day; book for early evening.
places.chef: Owner not named · Per Tabelog’s official introduction: chicken delivered directly from Nishiki Market, grilled slowly on a special stone with a strong far-infrared effect; over 200 drinks and more than 30 sakes; limited Kagoshima chicken sashimi and Nagoya Cochin liver and heart sashimi. The operator is not stated. · Seven-cut stone-grill platter of jidori.

places.notes: [Yoshoku · Sanjo bridge, grown-up kids' lunch plates] A small blue-toned house just over the Sanjo bridge where a chef from old-school yoshoku and hotel French kitchens cooks in front of a teppan. Lunch is the famous "adult's kids' lunch": pick three or four of hamburg, kataifi-wrapped giant fried shrimp, crab cream croquette, roast wagyu or fried hamo on one plate (¥3,800–5,000). Dinner is à la carte or courses, with wines chosen by the owner-sommelier; half portions on request. 5% service. Closed Monday and alternate Tuesdays.
places.chef: Shuhei Koishi (小石 修平) · Chef; the owner is a sommelier (not named) · Per the official site: trained at long-established yoshoku restaurants and in hotel French kitchens; after going independent ran ROKUMEI, a pop-up curry shop known for European-style curry and grown-up kids’-plate lunches; cooked at Dining Bar MO-JI in Gion for a year, then became chef at its sister restaurant Severance. Severance ran a five-day pop-up at 404Kitchen in Shibuya Sakura Stage on 8–12 May 2025 (official news). Opened 6 January 2023 (Tabelog). · Per the official site: the name means a dividing line — "beyond the door, a blissful space and food apart from everyday life"; old-style yoshoku such as hamburg and steak, updated for today. · "Angel" fried shrimp wrapped in kataifi; the adult’s kids’ lunch plate.

À la carte has a ¥5,500 seat charge that covers two or three dishes of the day; dinners run ¥15,000–20,000. Use the separate door beside the bar. Open late; closed irregularly.

Reviewers in December 2025 and July 2026 note a new head chef. The invoice number belongs to 株式会社ＦＯＩＳ. places.notes: [Sushi · Gion, kappo and Edomae sushi as you like it] A ten-seat Gion counter off Hanamikoji where the motto is "what you like, how you like, as much as you like": kappo dishes such as hamo, fugu or turtle hot pot first, then Edomae nigiri on red-vinegar rice, ordered piece by piece or as a course (from ¥25,000; most spend ¥30,000–50,000). Several reviewers describe it as introduction-only and hard to book; the official site takes enquiries by phone or LINE. Dinner, bookings only.
places.chef: 吉田紀彦 · Owner (店主) and chef · Per the official site, signed by the owner 吉田紀彦: kappo and Edomae sushi served in peak condition, with care over the number of dishes, temperature and ageing, matched to each guest’s taste; à la carte, omakase courses or dishes to a budget; a raised area and an upstairs private room for business use. Opened November 2014 in Hanamikoji (Tabelog official introduction). · Per the official site: 「お好きなものを お好きな様に お好きなだけ」 — what you like, how you like, as much as you like; a food utopia where truly good things can be enjoyed freely. · Edomae nigiri on red-vinegar rice after à la carte kappo dishes.

places.notes: [Kushikatsu · Shijo Karasuma, since 1972] A small second-floor counter and tatami room on Shijo-dori, founded in Arashiyama in 1972 and here since 2009. Light, finely battered skewers with Kyoto touches — Manganji pepper, yuba, nama-fu, shiso-wrapped sweetfish — fried to order and handed straight to your plate, with free cabbage. Take the ¥3,280 Arashiyama set or the omakase until you say stop; single skewers from ¥120. ¥300 cover.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed) · The official site dates the shop to 1972 in Arashiyama; it closed in 2006 and reopened near Karasuma Station in 2009. An August 2025 reviewer, back after more than ten years, read that actors Shun Oguri and Osamu Mukai had visited. A July 2025 diner was thanked by the owner for eating so many skewers. · Light-battered kushikatsu with Kyoto vegetables.

places.notes: [Lyonnais bistro · Teramachi-Nijo, cash only] A Parisian-looking bistro with a terrace on Teramachi below Nijo, from the Bellecour group (since 1985). Lunch is the draw: ¥2,100 for salad, free baguette and a main — the grilled hanging tender with fries is the favourite — or ¥2,600 with dessert. At night, Lyonnais classics: gratinée, tripe, cochonnaille, cassoulet. Phone bookings only, at set hours; cash only; fills by noon.

No chef is named on the pages opened. · Lyonnais bistro cooking; grilled hanging tender (onglet).

places.notes: [Japanese small plates and sake · Marutamachi, open late] A 14-seat house in a back lane near Marutamachi run by an owner qualified as a sake master (酒匠) and sake taster, who picks a sake for each dish and talks you through it. A long à la carte list on a washoku base with Italian-influenced freedom — horse sashimi, Earl Grey duck, karasumi daikon, keema-curry spring rolls, A5 Wagyu gyudon — or a seasonal course booked two days ahead. places.chef: 和久 秀郎 (Waku Hiderō) · Owner-chef · Itami, Hyogo (official site) · Per his own profile page: born 12 February 1982 in Itami, Hyogo; 174 cm, blood type O. Studied at 育成調理師専門学校 in Hyogo, a three-year cooking school combined with high school, 1997–2000, working part-time in an izakaya, an udon chain and a family restaurant; cook’s licence 2000. From April 2000 worked at ryotei in Kyoto — one with a Kamo River summer platform, one at Nanzenji, one in Nishikyo — then filled in at dozens of kitchens: a sushi kappo in Shinsaibashi, Kibune riverside restaurants, Gion kappo, Kodaiji and Nanzenji inns, hotels in Kusatsu, Nagoya and Kyoto, an Asian restaurant in Otsu. Japanese-cuisine cooking-skills certificate 2007; opened Waku in Higashiyama on 14 September 2007, and kept taking stints elsewhere afterwards; fugu licence 2013. Also lists a heavy-motorcycle licence. · Official site: 「京料理を主体としながら、私らしい料理も日々考えております」 — Kyoto cooking at the core, with dishes of his own worked out day by day; 「おもてなしの料理を作りたい」. · Omakase kappo course with counter-side talk.

places.notes: [Bar with kitchen · Kiyamachi Sanjo, oysters till 3 a.m.] A fourth-floor bar at the Sanjo–Kiyamachi corner that eats like a restaurant: oysters all year, kombu-cured sea bream, bagna cauda with crab miso, acqua pazza finished as risotto, karasumi pasta — with fresh-fruit cocktails or a highball. Good for a second stop or a late dinner. Open 18:00–3:00.
places.chef: Bartenders and two kitchen staff (unnamed; April 2026 review) · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): fresh seafood from the market, Italian dishes with seasonal vegetables, and desserts and cocktails of seasonal fruit. An April 2026 diner saw several bartenders at the counter and two cooks in the kitchen; the chef came out to chat with a May 2026 group. · Oysters; acqua pazza finished as risotto.
places.gfd: Ask. Seafood, pasta, pizza, fried potatoes and satsuma-age alongside oysters and sashimi (2026 reviews). No gluten information.
places.vgd: Ask. Vegetable dishes such as bagna cauda (with a crab-miso sauce) are offered, but the menu is seafood-led (2026 reviews).
places.hours: 18:00–3:00 (last order 2:00); closed irregularly (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, advised for groups (Tabelog; October 2026). places.hood: Karasuma-Takoyakushi — 242 m from Karasuma Stn
places.cu: Tuscan cooking with Kyoto vegetables: hearty meat, homemade pasta (Tabelog official introduction) · pasta lunch with soup and focaccia ¥1,500 (April 2026; ¥1,400 before) · one-plate lunch of pasta, quiche or omelette and salad, with drink and dessert, ¥2,000 · pair or share sets of pasta and meat · e.g. Shogoin-turnip or squash potage, homemade tagliatelle with beef ragù, clam and zucchini celery…
places.notes: [Italian · Karasuma-Takoyakushi, a couple's Tuscan basement] Down a steep stair off Karasuma-dori, a small, homely trattoria run by a couple, the chef having trained four years in Tuscany. Lunch is the bargain: potage, warm focaccia and a homemade pasta for about ¥1,500, or ¥2,000 with drink and dessert; share sets add a grilled meat. Dinner brings antipasti, wild-boar pappardelle and steaks. Book — it fills at noon. No elevator. Closed Monday; Sunday lunch only.
places.chef: Chef not named; run by a couple · Per Tabelog’s official introduction: run by a friendly couple; the chef trained for four years in Tuscany and pairs traditional Tuscan cooking with fresh, seasonal Kyoto vegetables. Opened 1 June 2021 (Tabelog). · Per Tabelog’s official introduction: to recreate authentic Tuscan flavours faithfully with an abundance of seasonal Kyoto produce. · Homemade tagliatelle and pappardelle; grilled meat.
places.gfd: Ask. Homemade pasta, focaccia, quiche and desserts; no gluten information is published (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Plenty of Kyoto vegetables, but the menu centres on meat, fish and cheese; nothing vegan is marked (Tabelog; reviews).
places.hours: Tuesday–Saturday lunch 12:00–15:00 (last order 14:30) and dinner 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); Sunday lunch 12:00–15:00; closed Monday (Tabelog). places.cu: Chiffon cake and roll cake, from the Kyoto branch of a Shibuya, Tokyo café (2026 reviews) · chiffon of Hokkaido wheat and red-yolk eggs, plain, as "cake butter toast" or half and half, e.g. Shoto Cake Half & Half with cream and maple ¥1,070 (August 2026), half & half chiffon ¥750, with ice cream and maple · egg-white roll cake in four heights, SS 3.5 cm to L 14 cm, S ¥550 (February 2026) · freshl…
places.notes: [Café · Sanjo Keihan, chiffon cake in a machiya] The Kyoto outpost of Shibuya's Shoto Cafe, in a renovated townhouse on a quiet lane just north of Sanjo Keihan. The star is the chiffon cake — fluffy, lightly salty, best as crisp-edged "cake butter toast" heaped with cream — and a tall egg-white roll cake sold in four heights. Climb the steep stairs to a small upstairs room; the owner is warm and chatty. Cash only. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Owner not named · Tabelog gives the opening as 1 March 2024. Reviewers in 2026 describe it as the second shop of 松涛カフェ of Shoto, Shibuya, Tokyo, known for chiffon and roll cakes; the chiffon is made with Hokkaido wheat flour and red-yolk eggs, the roll cake with egg whites only (December 2025). · Chiffon "cake butter toast"; roll cake in four heights.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: a chiffon-cake and roll-cake café; the chiffon is made with Hokkaido wheat flour (December 2025 review).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the chiffon uses eggs, the roll cake egg whites, and both come with whipped cream (2025–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Duck · Gion by the Shirakawa, Kyoto duck every way] A duck house a minute from Gion-Shijo Station, cooking Kyoto's brand duck as salad, yakitori, katsu, ham, yukhoe and seared nigiri. Lunch is a choose-your-main set from ¥2,300 ending in a showy glass parfait; dinner courses run ¥7,400–13,800, and the old house speciality, charcoal kuwa-yaki, needs booking. Most reviews are warm, though a few 2026 diners found the duck gamey. Private rooms upstairs; maiko dinners can be arranged.
places.chef: 岡本 賢志 · Representative (代表) of 株式会社北斎; head chef not named · Per the official site: run by 株式会社北斎 under representative 岡本 賢志; the duck is 京鴨, raised entirely in Kyoto by 山城農産; the business was founded 75 years ago and serves its traditional skills; it calls itself the birthplace of kuwa-yaki, cooked over charcoal. Tabelog gives the opening at this address as 4 July 2022. The invoice number belongs to 株式会社北斎, at the same address. · Per the official site: a serene space and a luxurious meal; the true flavour of carefully chosen ingredients. · Kyo-duck courses; charcoal kuwa-yaki.
