places.cu: Neapolitan pizzeria with a wood-fired oven imported from Italy and about 80% of ingredients from Italy, following traditional Neapolitan methods (Tabelog) · pizzas such as Margherita, Bufala, Quattro Formaggi with honey, Bismarck and Bismarck Bianco with mushrooms and egg, salsiccia with greens, 'nduja, prosciutto and arugula, half-and-half on request (2026 reviews) · caprese with buffalo mozzare…
places.notes: [Pizza · Higashiyama Sanjo, Naples by wood fire] A lively little pizzeria near Higashiyama Sanjo built around an Italian wood-fired oven: chewy-crusted Neapolitan pizzas — Bufala, Quattro Formaggi with honey, an egg-topped Bismarck Bianco, 'nduja, salsiccia — with half-and-half on request, plus caprese and fritto. Lunch sets are good value; pizzas arrive fast. Young, friendly staff; one diner found plates cleared too briskly. Strollers must fold. Open daily.
places.chef: Pizzaiolo and staff (unnamed) · Per Tabelog: a pizzeria dedicated to Naples in ingredients, methods and its Italian wood-fired oven, with seats close to the kitchen and about 80% of ingredients imported from Italy; opened 7 August 2017. Reviewers in 2026 describe young, kind and attentive staff ("The staff were incredibly cute as well", March 2026), quick service and many guests from abroad. · Authentic Neapolitan methods and ingredients (Tabelog). · Bismarck Bianco; Quattro Formaggi with honey.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: a Neapolitan pizzeria — wheat-dough pizzas from a wood-fired oven, plus fritto and tiramisu (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. A marinara-style pizza without cheese may be possible, but the menu is built on mozzarella, buffalo mozzarella, sausage and prosciutto; no vegan information (2026 reviews).

places.cu: Casual wine bar run by a sommelier, with Italian dishes made to go with wine (Tabelog) · "Solo Set" of five half-portion dishes, ¥2,500 (March 2023) — e.g. potato salad, smoked salt mackerel, chicken confit with rosemary, eggplant with pancetta in balsamic, cheese risotto (May 2022) · Yokowa tuna carpaccio, daikon risotto (December 2024); karasumi pasta (November 2024); bagna cauda of unusual veg…
places.notes: [Wine bar · Matsubara Karasuma, a sommelier and a piano] A calm, late-opening wine bar west of Karasuma where the sommelier-master pours wines from many countries — sometimes without naming the wine, so you taste first — and cooks small Italian plates to match; solo guests can take a five-dish half-portion set (about ¥2,500). Bagna cauda, karasumi pasta, risotto and ajillo; on some nights the master plays the piano. Many regulars; one newcomer felt a little left out. Last entry 22:30. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Owner-sommelier ("master", unnamed), Staff · Per Tabelog: a casual wine bar run by a sommelier, whose dishes are made to pair with wine, with a five-dish "Solo Set" and occasional live piano. Reviewers describe a gentle master who plays piano at times (2022–2024), wines served without disclosing origin to encourage tasting without preconceptions (October 2025), and nights when the master works alone (February 2026). · Wines tasted without preconceptions (October 2025 review). · Solo Set; wine pairing.
places.gfd: Ask. Italian wine-bar dishes such as risotto, pasta, ajillo, bagna cauda and confit; no gluten information (2022–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Bagna cauda vegetables, fruit and some vegetable dishes appear, but anchovy, pancetta, cheese, fish and meat run through the menu (2022–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Kappo izakaya · Gion Shinbashi, pick from the seafood box] A long-running Gion counter where you choose from boxes of the day's seafood — Matsuba crab, torigai, mantis shrimp, whale bacon — or let the owner recommend: sashimi, tempura, soft-shelled-turtle hot pot, matsutake dobin-mushi, a famous beef cutlet. Portions are generous and courses come fast. Prices are higher than the homely look suggests; reviewers warn that following every recommendation adds up. Smoking allowed. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed) and staff · Per Tabelog: seasonal dishes from fresh ingredients from across Japan; 50 seats with a wooden counter, a banquet room and private rooms; relocated from Gion-machi in 2012; a sister restaurant, Bistro Nonki, opened in 2023 in front of Kyoto Station. Reviewers in 2026 describe a pleasant owner who recommends dishes, many regulars, and a chef who once warned that the course was coming too fast (August 2026). · Seafood box; beef cutlet; seasonal tempura.
places.gfd: Ask. Seasonal Japanese dishes including tempura, kakiage, fried nameko, beef cutlet, katsu sandwiches, sushi and hot pots; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a seafood-led menu — sashimi from a seafood box, whale bacon, crab, fugu, soft-shelled turtle — with dashi (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Monday to Saturday 17:00–22:00; closed Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). places.notes: [Curry · Sanjo-Muromachi, the meringue curry] A 12-seat counter for European-style curry near Karasuma Oike: one house sauce, sweet and fruity first with the heat arriving later, under fresh-fried katsu, shrimp or croquettes. The signature Takayama curry, styled on a Gion Festival float, is crowned with whipped egg-white meringue and a yolk (¥1,100). Curries from ¥850, large rice free, spices for sale. Lunch and dinner, closed Sundays.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed) · An August 2025 reviewer writes that the owner “apparently retired early from the police force to open this curry shop” and has a vibrant personality. The official site says the owner personally selects every ingredient. In January 2026 the shop’s connection with the Aomori team was told on NHK’s broadcast of the 44th National Women’s Ekiden in Kyoto (official site). · A two-stage sauce, fruity and sweet first, then spicy; high hospitality and “wagamama” special orders where possible (official site). · Takayama curry; European-style curry.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: a European-style curry sauce (roux not described) served with breaded katsu, menchi katsu, fried shrimp, croquettes and fried oysters (official site; 2024–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Clams and sake · Sanjo-Muromachi, a couple’s counter] A homely L-shaped counter on Sanjo-dori run by a husband and wife, where the day’s omakase ends in the house clam shabu-shabu finished with soba. Seven dishes ¥5,000, or the clam course with croquette, ajillo and shabu-shabu with two hours of drinks for ¥8,000; about ten sakes, and a pairing course. Bookings are for courses; à la carte after 21:00. Solo-friendly. One drink each.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed) and the owner’s wife; invoice holder 株式会社べっぴんや · Reviewers describe a couple behind the counter: “the cheerful demeanor of the owners (a couple)” (May 2026); the owner and the owner’s wife “very friendly” (February 2026); “the charm of the owner’s wife is truly captivating” (February 2026). An April 2026 diner also mentions staff. A February 2026 visitor booked after seeing the clam course on a TV show visited by Tohru Kazama. Tabelog’s invoice number T2130001044213 is registered to 株式会社べっぴんや (NTA invoice registry). · Seasonal vegetables and fresh fish, cooking that is kind to the body and stomach; a new dish each visit (official site). · Clam shabu-shabu; sake.

places.notes: [Café · Okazaki, by the Shirakawa] A glass-walled concrete café with a terrace on the Shirakawa, steps from Heian Shrine and the KYOCERA Museum — useful before a museum, Noh at the Kanze Kaikan, or a shrine visit. Breakfast from 9:00 (French toast, honey cheese toast, morning plate), sandwiches and dry curry at lunch, and a showcase of puddings, Mont Blanc and huge scones. Order at the counter. Open to 21:00 on Fridays and Saturdays. Busy; expect waits at breakfast.
places.chef: Café team (unnamed) · Kyotopi (October 2023) reports the café opened in March 2023 on the site of a bistro that closed during the pandemic, as a sister shop of cafe KaimanaLio in Kusatsu, Shiga, known for specialty coffee. A November 2026 reviewer found the man who served the table “a bit brusque”, if busy. · Breakfast toasts; pudding; scones; coffee.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free as a menu: toast, French toast, sandwiches, scones, quiche, cakes and cookies (Kyotopi 2023; 2026 reviews). The pudding and granola with Greek yogurt are not described — ask.

places.notes: [Izakaya · Shijo Karasuma, Showa-retro and loud] A packed two-floor taishu sakaba south of Shijo from the team behind 酒呑気びんご, serving small, cheap, well-made plates — the meat tofu, dote-yaki, sesame-miso sea bream, burst-of-broth stuffed peppers, fried yam — with sake and beer poured two ways. Staff push recommendations with gusto. Book ahead; ¥330 otoshi.
places.chef: Operated by 株式会社Atari · The company site of 株式会社Atari, which proposes “new sakaba rooted in Kyoto”, lists four shops: 酒呑気びんご, 六角ace, 酒ﾉみつぼし and ageru. Reviewers call it the sister of “Bingo” and “Rokkaku Ace” (August and September 2026). An October 2026 reviewer wrote that “all the staff were handsome, with one beautiful girl”, and called the service outstanding; a September 2026 diner admired the staff’s energetic recommendations. · “Bringing washoku to the sakaba” (和食を酒場へ) (company site). · Meat tofu; dote-yaki; fried chicken.

places.notes: [Meat bar · west of City Hall, steak and sausages, big lunch plates] A twenty-seat meat bar open since 2013: homemade sausages and steak by the pound at night, and on weekdays two or three hefty set lunches — kara-age, chicken nanban, a tonteki in a rich sauce — that sell out early. Regulars split on the rice: "declining a bit" (September 2025), "a bit too soft" (May 2026). Smoking allowed. PayPay but no cards. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Opened 22 March 2013 (Tabelog). The Tabelog blurb calls it a pioneering meat bar — a meat tavern with homemade sausages and steaks, about ten snacks always on, and popular meat set lunches that end when they sell out. An older shop blog (2016) announced dinner from 18:00 daily, Friday-only lunches then, and a "chicken mountain" as its speciality. Reviewers in 2024–2026 describe a lunch board at the entrance, two or three set meals a day, and a menu posted on Instagram. · Steak by the pound; homemade sausages; tonteki set lunch.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: lunch is kara-age, chicken nanban, fried oysters and tonteki in sauce (2024–2026 reviews).

Lunch around ¥7,000. Two older gripes: a sukiyaki finish (2018), a hard-centred mochi in the New Year ozoni (2024). Reservations only; closed Monday.

Closed Wednesday and Thursday.
places.chef: Per the official site (junidanya-kyoto.com): 「牛肉の水炊き(しゃぶしゃぶ)発祥の店」. In 1949 (昭和24年) the second-generation owner, advised by a doctor friend from Tottori (吉田璋也) and others, devised beef mizutaki, which became the shabu-shabu known across Japan. The same owner opened the Hanamikoji shop to make it easier to drop in; the main shop is four doors east, and the site marks the two as separate shops. · Shabu-shabu with house sesame sauce; beef sukiyaki.

places.chef: 荒木 一雄 · Third-generation owner (店主) · Per the official site: founded in 1936 in Gion (Nawate, above Shinbashi) by 荒木 信次, a leading craftsman of decorative sushi who spread the technique nationwide and wrote a sushi textbook; the second generation, 照雄, held senior posts in the sushi trade association; the third, 荒木 一雄, built today’s "sushi and kappo" style. The shop moved to the 占出山 float district in March 2011. A May 2025 reviewer recalls seven or eight 重兵衛 in Gion some 30 years ago, including one at the now-closed Fujita Hotel. · Per the official site: gratitude to guests, to ingredients and to the trade; as a Kyoto-sushi house the rice comes first — aged Kyoto or Omi rice cooked in kombu dashi so it tastes deeper the more you chew. · 名物 磯巻; 名代 鯖寿し; omakase of sushi and kappo dishes.

places.notes: [Italian · Okazaki, a forager's vegetable Italian by Heian Shrine] Big windows onto the Heian Shrine torii and the scent of a wood fire: chef Toshifumi Nakahigashi, son of the family behind 草喰 なかひがし, picks wild plants and vegetables every morning as the heart of Italian courses — leaf minestra, matsutake tagliolini, venison with wild grape, herbal tea to close. places.chef: Toshifumi Nakahigashi (中東 俊文) · Chef-owner · Born 1982 and raised in Kyoto · Per the official site: born and raised in Kyoto in 1982; the father runs 草喰 なかひがし at Ginkakuji and a cousin runs 美山荘 in Hanase. Went to Italy alone at 18 and cooked mains at the two-star Ristorante Arnolfo in Tuscany, then trained at Villa Fiordaliso on Lake Garda (one star) and Alain Ducasse au Plaza Athénée in Paris (three stars). Back in Japan, head chef of Prinz in Ichijoji, then opening chef for The St. Regis Osaka from 2010; opened erba da nakahigashi in Nishi-Azabu, Tokyo, in 2016, renamed it 草片 cusavilla on 22 February 2021 with a stronger vegetable focus, and opened ristorante DONO in Okazaki, Kyoto, in April 2024. Listed with a Michelin Green Star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto–Osaka 2025 (official site). A May 2026 reviewer names the chef Toshifumi Nakahigashi, second son of the Nakahigashi family; the invoice registration is in the chef’s own name. · Per Tabelog’s official introduction: "Dono" means sharing in Italian — to share nature’s gifts, gathered from the mountains and fields every morning, with guests. · Vegetable and wild-plant courses; matsutake tagliolini in autumn.

Each month brings 100% buckwheat soba from three regions — taste all three side by side for ¥1,500, with salt. Lunch sets add mackerel sushi or soba-gaki; Thursday to Saturday evenings bring soba-mae snacks and soba kaiseki. Service can be slow when busy. Closed Wednesday.

Help yourself to sake and beer from the shop fridges at retail prices and tell the owner. About ¥12,000–15,000 all in. Booked months ahead; cash only. Closed Sunday.

places.notes: [Izakaya · Nishikikoji, a lively townhouse sakaba] A buzzing, booking-only izakaya in an old townhouse west of Karasuma, with a cheerful crew at the counter. Good-value and strongly seasoned, built for drinking. Open daily from 16:00; book ahead.

Handy before or between Kabuki at Minami-za.

places.chef: 大村 壮史 · Owner-pâtissier (official site) · Per the official site: made cream puffs and café desserts at Crème de la Crème (2004–2006); wedding and café cakes at スター株式会社 (2006–2008); restaurant desserts and take-out cakes at Il Ghiottone (2008–2013); chocolate café desserts at マリベル (2013–2014); wedding cakes and desserts at the Westin Miyako Hotel (2014–2017); then opened Mikan in September 2017 as an assiette-dessert shop. places.cu: A natural-wine bistro bar in a renovated machiya: bottles to choose from the shelf, with a lean towards the Loire (2022–2023 reviews) · glasses from ¥950 (October 2025) · assorted cured ham (two kinds) ¥1,600; chicken-liver pâté with country bread ¥850; sautéed gizzard confit ¥800; grilled corn omelette ¥1,200 (August 2025) · caramelised onion tart, pâté de campagne, lentil and pumpkin salad, bon…
places.notes: [Natural-wine bistro · near Shijo-Karasuma, Loire bottles] A twelve-seat bistro bar in a machiya near Shijo-Karasuma, with records playing and a shelf of natural wines to pick from — many from the Loire — beside pâté de campagne, an onion tart and cured ham. Tables only, for two or more. Glasses from ¥950. Cards or cash, no PayPay. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Owner, not named; has a Loire connection per a September 2022 diner · Reviewers from 2019 to 2025 describe a natural-wine bistro in a renovated machiya near Shijo-Karasuma that feels like a Paris bistro, with French cheeses, bottles on the shelf to choose from, a strong showing of Loire wines (the owner seemed to have a Loire connection, September 2022), records in the background, and a small but wine-friendly menu with seasonal Kyoto vegetables. · Natural wine by the bottle; pâté de campagne; onion tart.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: onion tart, pâté with country bread, and bread served alongside the cheese and ham (2022–2025 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: charcuterie, pâtés, gizzard confit and cheese (reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: 18:00–22:00; closed Tuesday; hours may change. 12 seats, tables only, for groups of two or more (Tabelog); a November 2023 diner says the name, "two pigs", reflects that it takes parties from two. places.n: 京都生ショコラ オーガニックティーハウス (Kyoto Nama Chocolat Organic Tea House)
places.hood: Okazaki, near Heian Shrine and the zoo — 3 min walk from the Okazaki-michi bus stop; 15 m…
places.cu: A tea house of nama chocolate in an old house with a garden, with organic coffee and drinks of pesticide-free juice (official site) · chocolate set with a drink ¥1,320: four nama chocolates — sweet, bitter, matcha and cranberry or berry (June and October 2026) · chocolate cake on a plate of fruit and herbs, apple-raisin cake, marble cheesecake, cold chocolate (2026 reviews) · organic Japanese bla…
places.notes: [Nama-chocolate tea house · Okazaki, an old house and garden] Down a narrow lane near Heian Shrine, a tea house in an old farmhouse-style home with two tatami rooms and an engawa over the garden, run by a couple — she explains in English, he in Japanese (June 2026). A ¥1,320 set of four nama chocolates with a drink, cakes plated with flowers, and boxes to take home. No air-conditioning in summer. Up to three groups booked at once.
places.chef: Run by a couple, not named (June 2026) · Opened 17 September 2005 (Tabelog), in a renovated old Kyoto house near Heian Shrine (official site). A June 2026 diner describes a couple: the wife, from overseas, serves mainly in English with detailed explanations, while the Japanese husband helps take-out customers in Japanese; they brought a cushion and moved the fan for comfort and dimmed the lights for the chocolate. An October 2026 diner found the owner running it alone that day. Earlier visitors (2016) met a dog and a cat. · Official site: organic, body-friendly drinks and cakes; nama chocolate that melts in the mouth. · Nama chocolate set.
places.gfd: Ask: the nama chocolate itself is not described as containing wheat, but the cakes (chocolate cake, apple-raisin cake, marble cheesecake) are not confirmed either way (2026 reviews). Ask the owners.
places.vgd: Not vegan: nama chocolate is made with cream; cakes come with cream (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: 12:00–19:00 (last order); closed irregularly; Tabelog remarks also say closed Tuesday but open on holidays, while the official site says closed on public holidays. places.notes: [Coffee house · Kawaramachi-Imadegawa, the Ooya roaster’s flannel-drip café] A second-floor café in a retro building near Demachiyanagi, run by the Kyoto roaster Ooya Coffee: no blends — pick the origin and say "rich" or "light", and it comes flannel-dripped in a little pot. Coffee floats with clove-and-orange ice cream, banana toast. Smoking is allowed inside. Busy with tourists on weekends. Closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Run by オオヤコーヒ焙煎所 (official site); a September 2026 diner names the roaster as "Minoru Ooya" · Per the official site of オオヤコーヒ焙煎所 (ooyacoffee associees, since 2007): the roaster’s directly run shops are this flannel-drip coffee house in Kyoto, a ten-days-a-month stand in Shirahama, Wakayama, and Café gewa in Kurashiki, Okayama; it also sells by contract and wholesale. Reviewers in 2026 describe a clean, calm second-floor room with a green view, friendly staff, a counter facing an open kitchen, and a crowd of couples, women and tourists. · Flannel-drip single origins; coffee float.
places.gfd: Ask: coffee itself is fine, but the food is toast, cakes and bread (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask: black coffee is plant-based; floats, cheesecake and banana toast are not (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: 12:00–21:00; closed Tuesday, open when a holiday falls on Tuesday; hours may change; temporary closures posted on the roaster’s site (official site). places.notes: [Crêperie · by Yasui Konpira Shrine] A narrow, European-style crêperie where galettes and crepes come crisp and fragrant, one at a time: prosciutto-camembert-fig galette, then a crepe with house caramel or seasonal fruit. About ¥1,500–2,500. Cash only; no bookings; one order each. Closed Mon and Thu.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · Opened 10 April 2015 (Tabelog). A June 2026 diner felt it was run like a family business. · Crisp galettes; caramel crepes.
places.gfd: Ask. Savoury galettes and sweet crepes; the batters are not described, and crepe batter is usually wheat (2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: butter, caramel, cheese, ham and egg (2025–26 reviews).
places.hours: Tue, Wed, Fri–Sun 11:30–18:00; closed Mon and Thu; hours may change (Tabelog) — a July 2026 regular found it open by 10:30, opening as soon as everything was ready. No bookings; one order per person; no photos of the interior (menu and food photos are fine) (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog). 10 table …

menu.en: Fresh melon crepe with caramel sauce (seasonal)

places.notes: [Obanzai & sansho · Kiyamachi] A small adult counter bar on the Kiyamachi lane, with a tiny garden, built around sansho from its own farm: obanzai platters, grilled Miyama chicken, kinpira and highballs all tingling with it, and extra sansho on the table. About ¥4,000–8,000. Evenings only; cash or PayPay; closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · Opened 25 January 2008 (Tabelog). Per the official site: a small, quiet adult drinking spot where one can unwind alone after work or sightseeing; sansho grown without pesticides on its own farm, and ingredients mainly from Miyama, Kyoto. · Sansho dishes for their fresh aroma and distinctive tingle (official site). · Sansho dishes; obanzai.
places.gfd: Ask. Obanzai and grilled dishes with soy-based seasoning; dumplings and salt yakisoba are wheat (2022–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Vegetables lead, but obanzai and oden use dashi and there is chicken (Tabelog; 2022–26 reviews).
places.hours: 17:00–21:00; closed Tuesday; may close early without notice; see the website for closures (Tabelog). Bookings by phone or e-mail; a cancellation fee applies to no-shows (Tabelog). Charge: Tabelog's Japanese original says 「お通し代 あり」 — an appetizer charge. No cards; PayPay (Tabelog; official site). En…

places.hood: Demachi shopping street — 8 min from Demachiyanagi Stn
places.cu: Quiet seasonal Kyoto cuisine, as a ¥12,000 course or à la carte (official site): a seasonal appetizer platter, sashimi of sawara and sea bream, the seasonal steamed dish — chestnut with fish in October, green peas in March — guji (sweet sea bream) cooked as you choose: salt-grilled, sake-steamed, fried, simmered or agedashi; tempura of kuruma prawn, firefly squid and mountain vegetables; hamo in …
places.notes: [Kyoto cuisine · Demachi shopping street] A calm little Kyoto restaurant off the Demachi arcade, by counter, table or tatami room: seasonal appetizers, a celebrated steamed dish of the season, and guji cooked whichever way you like. Course ¥12,000 or à la carte, plus tax only. Book ahead; closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed) with the proprietress · Per the official site, running since about 2008 (site copyright 2008–2026); its motto is 「ゆき過ぎず ひかえめに」 — never overdone, always restrained — following Kyoto's seasons in nourishing food. A July 2026 diner describes the owner and the hostess. · Restrained cooking that follows the Kyoto seasons (official site). · Guji prepared to order; the seasonal steamed dish.
places.gfd: Ask. Dashi-based Kyoto cooking with soy, tempura and cha soba; no gluten information (2024–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: fish-centred Kyoto cuisine in dashi (2024–26 reviews).

places.hood: Shijo Karasuma, an alley off Kamanza — 3 min from Shijo Stn

places.notes: [Charcoal grill and wine · Shijo Karasuma, a machiya in a back alley] A hidden machiya with a bar counter downstairs and sunken-kotatsu rooms upstairs, grilling seasonal vegetables and meat over charcoal to go with a long wine list — plus ajillo, appetizer platters and penne. Courses with all-you-can-drink from ¥5,500 suit groups; staff are lively, though big parties slow the kitchen. Open to midnight; closed Sunday.

places.gfd: Not gluten-free as a menu: pasta (penne, peperoncino), bread with the ajillo, macaroni salad (2025–26 reviews). Ask about the charcoal-grilled meat and vegetables.
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, and the shop grills seasonal vegetables over charcoal (official site); most courses include meat and fish.

places.cu: Yoshoku and bistro cooking with organic vegetables from producers, natural wine and champagne, with pairings (Tabelog, shop text) · Anpurusu lunch: amuse-bouches such as carrot mousse and a mushroom-walnut pâté canapé, salad, and a choice of five mains (November 2025; January 2026) · Anpurusu plate of demi-glace hamburg steak, fried shrimp and crab cream croquette, ¥1,870 (August 2024; 2025–26 re…
places.notes: [Yoshoku bistro · Shijo Omiya, demi-glace and natural wine] A small neighbourhood yoshoku house where the owner-chef chats across the counter: a rich demi-glace hamburg steak, shrimp fry and crab cream croquette on the Anpurusu plate, beef stew and bistro à la carte at night, with natural wines and homemade canelés to finish. Regulars come back a dozen times; book, as lunch fills. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed), who talks with guests at the counter (Tabelog, shop text) · Per Tabelog (the shop’s own text): authentic bistro cooking at an affordable price, organic vegetables bought directly from producers, and natural wines and champagnes chosen to pair. places.gfd: Not gluten-free as a menu: crab cream croquette, fried shrimp, chicken and fillet katsu, demi-glace hamburg steak (2023–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: hamburg steak, beef stew, duck, shrimp and crab dishes (2024–26 reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–13:30, dinner 18:00–21:30 (last order 20:30); closed Tuesday, Wednesday and irregularly (Tabelog). places.notes: [Japanese wine izakaya · Karasuma Oike northwest] A twelve-seat, homely wine izakaya devoted to Japanese wines, poured with pairing tips from the owner: doteyaki in demi-glace and Hatcho miso, gnocchi, skewers with wine sauces, kimchi and Korean snacks, skirt steak and dishes sent over from sister shops nearby. Guests stay for hours and come back the next night. A ¥500 salad otoshi. Evenings; closed Monday.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed), who selects Japanese wines and suggests pairings, Part of a small group with the restaurant 両川 (November 2026 review) · Per Tabelog: an izakaya, pasta and wine bar by Karasuma Oike; registered as an official listing by the shop. places.vgd: Not vegan: liver, skirt steak, salsiccia, mussels, beef tendon and omelette dominate the menu (2025–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [French · near Jingu-Marutamachi, one chef, twelve seats] A calm twelve-seat French dining room where the owner-chef cooks and serves every course alone, with uncanny timing: seasonal, inventive plates such as venison-blood pie, ayu with bouillabaisse, Ezo venison or wagyu with cheek, ending with the house pound cake — and a late-night dessert course after midnight. Lunch from ¥7,500, dinner ¥12,100, plus 10% service. Reservation only; closed Thursday.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed), who cooks and serves alone (June 2025 review) · Per Tabelog: a reservation-only French restaurant "to enjoy with all five senses", with lunch, dinner and a late-night dessert course; registered as an official listing by the shop. A June 2025 reviewer writes that the owner-chef manages everything from cooking to serving alone, with warm, attentive service; a July 2025 guest was given an explanation of the name and a photo as a parting gift. · A French restaurant to enjoy with all five senses (Tabelog). · Seasonal course; pound cake.
places.gfd: Ask when booking: the restaurant asks to be told of allergies in advance and may not manage on the day (Tabelog); a 2025 guest found allergy requests well handled. Courses include pies, pound cake and bread (2025 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: set courses of venison, pork, wagyu, fish and shellfish, with dairy desserts (2025–2026 reviews).

places.chef: Owner couple (unnamed) · Tabelog’s shop text says guests are “welcomed by our friendly owner couple”; a January 2024 reviewer describes a restaurant “run by a couple who also have a YouTube channel”, and another (January 2024) a warm, family-run atmosphere. places.gfd: Ask. Wagyu with a homemade secret sauce, salted tongue, yukhoe, kimchi and namul, Kujo green-onion tempura, clay-pot rice with shigure-ni; the sauce ingredients are not given (Tabelog shop text; 2024–2025 reviews).

places.notes: [Chinese · Oike near Shinmachi, a family machiya since 1988] A family-run Chinese restaurant in a two-storey machiya on Oike-dori with retro tables and a gentle, Kyoto-style touch. Cash only; closed Tuesdays.
places.chef: Family-run (unnamed); now the son runs the restaurant (February 2026) · Tabelog’s shop text: established in 1988 in a renovated townhouse, with Kyoto-style Chinese cooking refined after training at Sichuan restaurants and hotels. A February 2026 regular learned from the owner that the founder died about two years earlier and the son has taken over, and was shown a plaque explaining the name: 鳳城, from Du Fu’s poem “Night”, is an elegant name for Chang’an (Xi’an), chosen for the friendship between Xi’an — sister city of Kyoto since 1974 — and Kyoto. An October 2026 reviewer calls it a long-established restaurant “run by a family in a historic Kyoto townhouse”; an April 2026 diner found the owner very attentive. · Dandan noodles; fried rice.
places.gfd: Ask. Chinese dishes with soy sauce and wheat noodles — dandan noodles, chashu ramen, fried rice, bone-in kara-age, sweet-and-sour meatballs; no gluten information (2026 reviews).

A terrace takes dogs and smokers. Tablet ordering; no service charge.

Six counter seats and one small room; omakase runs about ¥20,000–30,000. Cash only. Book ahead.

No service charge. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

No drink menu and no prices shown, so one diner found the bill higher than expected. Open nightly till midnight.

Reviewers describe a brick-walled entrance, a long wooden counter, a garden at the back, knowledgeable staff, and seasonal events. · Cocktails to order; antique glassware.

Order à la carte (¥300 seat charge) or the ¥10,800 course. Dinner only; closed Sunday.

The ice is shaved into fine, wide ribbons that melt at once, under house syrups of the season's fruit — fig with cheese and peanuts, peach, Kyoho grape — with ice cream hidden inside. About ¥1,500 a bowl; a favourite of penguin fans. Closed Wednesday.

places.chef: Atsushi Nakahigashi (中東 篤志) · Owner chef and culinary director (刻toki, Friday–Saturday), Kazuhiro Inui (いぬい) cooks Tuesday–Thursday as 膳いぬい · Born in Kyoto · Per the official site: born in Kyoto into a family of restaurateurs, trained under the chef’s father at 草喰なかひがし from the age of 12, then worked at the vegan restaurant Kajitsu in New York from 2011; founded One Rice One Soup Inc. in the US in 2016 and One Rice One Soup株式会社 in Japan in 2019 (the invoice holder); based in New York and Kyoto; opened this counter on 25 October 2019. Kazuhiro Inui runs the Tuesday–Thursday dinners. · Per the official site: a flat, welcoming place for anyone who loves to eat and drink, where people keep coming back; per a December 2025 review, "so" stands for origin and essence and for the seasoning order sa-shi-su-se-so. · Clay-pot rice and seasonal small plates.

places.chef: 株式会社 松葉 (representative director 松野 和代, official site) · Per the official history: founded in 1861 when 初代 松野与衛門 opened a soba shop at 18; in 1882 the second generation, 松野与三吉, created nishin soba, moved to a corner of Minamiza and named the shop 松葉. 松野与三吉 died in 1940. In 1945 the wooden Meiji building was torn down in a forced wartime clearance to protect Minamiza from air raids; in 1946 松野貞雄 returned from the war and became owner, and in 1951 the first post-war building, four storeys, rose on the same plot. The present building dates from 1973–74; 北店 opened opposite in 1976; 松野貞雄 (third 松野与衛門) died in 1981; the Kyoto Station shop opened in 2003; 松野和代 became representative director in 2024. · Nishin soba.

In 1951 the founder’s elder brother, also a cook, was granted a noren by たん熊 and opened たん新 in Gion Shinbashi; in April 1964 the founder went independent and opened たん義. After the founder died in November 1998, aged 73, the founder’s only daughter, the okami 三津川 都 (born 1953), carried on the shop and its flavours; the okami’s son 三津川 義弘 took over as third generation in 2015. places.n: 手打 とおる蕎麦 (Teuchi Toru Soba)

places.cu: Handmade juwari soba (all buckwheat) with an Edo-style dashi dipping sauce (2025–2026 reviews) · zaru soba ¥1,200 regular (August 2026), 1.5× and double portions; grated-daikon (oroshi) soba, spicy oroshi, yamakake, a small bowl of tororo (2025–2026 reviews) · soba-gaki zenzai (sweet red-bean soup with buckwheat dumplings), cold ¥900 (August 2026) · soba-yu in a pot with extra dipping sauce; sake…
places.notes: [Soba · Gosho-minami, handmade juwari by one man] An eight-seat counter on a quiet street near Karasuma Oike where the owner alone makes, boils and serves handmade juwari soba: firm, fragrant noodles with a bold bonito dip, big portions, and soba-gaki zenzai to finish. Lunch only, Thursday to Sunday; expect a queue at noon and many visitors from abroad. One diner found the dip too mild (April 2026). Cash only.
places.chef: Owner, not named; runs the shop alone (2025–2026 reviews) · Reviewers in 2025–2026 describe an eight-seat counter in a residential street of Gosho-minami where one owner handles everything — drinks, boiling, serving and clearing — with a quick rhythm, handmade juwari soba compared to Edo or Echizen styles, generous portions, and lately many foreign customers. The shop’s own site and Instagram (toru_soba) post holidays. · Juwari zaru soba; soba-gaki zenzai.
places.gfd: Ask: the soba is handmade juwari (all buckwheat), and diners in April and June 2026 say gluten-free orders are taken, but the dipping sauce is soy-based and the shop has not published how it handles this. Ask the owner.

places.hours: Tabelog: Thu–Sun 11:30–14:30; closed Monday to Wednesday; hours may change. places.cu: Omakase-only modern Japanese at an eight-seat counter, joining New York freedom with Kyoto technique: Kyoto vegetables and local sake, chosen seafood, Satsuma kuroge wagyu (official site) · seen: Satsuma wagyu strip loin with yuba and mibuna sauce to open, Aichi eel sushi, young-ayu tempura, chicken takikomi-gohan, saba-zushi (July 2025); tomato and sake soup with oysters and clams, grilled eel, …
places.notes: [Modern Japanese · Sanjo-Kiyamachi, a New York-raised chef’s counter] An eight-seat fourth-floor counter at Sanjo-Kiyamachi where chef 富永 暖, raised in New York and once head chef of MEGU in Tribeca, cooks an omakase of Kyoto produce and Satsuma wagyu — often starting with the meat — and chats across the counter. Popular with visitors from abroad; a Maiko Dinner can be booked. Reservations only; ¥20,000–40,000 a head. No service charge.
places.chef: 富永 暖 (Dan Tominaga) · Owner-chef (official site); cooks and serves alone (March 2023; November 2025) · Grew up in New York (official site) · Per the official site: grew up around cooking, moved to New York at 10 and helped at his parents’ food shop; after high school he returned to Japan alone to train in Japanese cuisine in Kyoto, at Michelin-starred restaurants including 貴船ひろや and 日本料理櫻川; went back to New York in 2004 as head chef of MEGU in Tribeca; returned in 2009 to lead the kitchen of 多伽羅 in Nishijin; then opened Another C. A July 2025 diner gives the name as Dan Tominaga. An August 2023 diner met "the chef and his wife." · Official site: a hideaway where each guest is the star — borderless food and space, freer, more fun and more stylish. · Omakase of Kyoto produce and Satsuma wagyu; the Maiko Dinner.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: courses include tempura, sushi and a small burger to finish (2023–2025 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask: Tabelog lists vegetarian options, but the omakase leans on Satsuma kuroge wagyu, eel and fish with dashi (official site; reviews).

places.notes: [Curry counter · Kyoto Station Hachijo exit] A tiny counter at Avanti serving some of Kyoto's cheapest curry — ¥390 plain, ¥550 with a freshly fried pork cutlet — sweet at first, then properly spicy, with plenty of rice. Expect a lunchtime queue; it can sell out. Closed Sunday.

Reviewers like the room and food; some found dishes unexplained (September 2025) or the pasta less good than before (February 2026). Closed Monday.

places.chef: Owner (unnamed) · Per Tabelog and reviewers: one of the few cheese specialists in Kyoto, with a cheesecake counter in the basement. · Cheesecake.

places.cu: Neapolitan-style café: cappuccino ¥620 (March 2026) in Passalacqua cups, espresso; one breakfast set — a hot sandwich of chicken, cheese and lettuce with a soft-boiled egg ¥1,040 (June 2026), earlier toast, egg and yogurt; fresh orange juice from a Zummo press; Italian craft beers such as KBIRR's PullicenHell and still waters (2025–26 reviews)

Popular with Italian and other foreign visitors; English spoken.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed), who also runs a guesthouse · A June 2026 reviewer says the owner, passionate about coffee, also runs a guesthouse; an August 2026 regular of four years says the café was featured in the southern Italian paper Il Mattino and on Italian media, and draws ever more Italian visitors. · Cappuccino.

places.n: blend kyoto (ブレンド キョウト)
places.hood: Takeyamachi-Fuyacho — near the Imperial Palace grounds
places.cu: Light-roast specialty coffee stand where you smell the beans (labelled a to i) and pick two to blend into your own cup (2024–2026 reviews) · e.g. a blended coffee ¥1,210 (May 2025); spiced options such as a cinnamon coffee (March 2026) · prices on the higher side (March 2026)
places.notes: [Coffee · Takeyamachi, blend your own cup] A tiny, stylish specialty-coffee stand on the way to the Imperial Palace grounds, run by a barista from Tokyo's GLITCH COFFEE & ROASTERS. Sniff your way through jars of light-roast beans labelled a to i, choose two, and the barista blends and brews your cup — about ¥1,200 a cup. Just two seats, so plan to stroll with it. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Owner-barista not named · Per an April 2026 review: the owner trained at the renowned GLITCH COFFEE & ROASTERS in Tokyo before opening this shop in Kyoto. Reviewers describe a wide choice of light-roast beans from which guests pick two for a custom blend. · Two-bean custom blend.
places.gfd: Ask. A coffee stand; no food or gluten information is published (Tabelog; reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Black coffee is plant-based; ask about milk drinks (reviews).

places.n: 京都ビアラボ (Kyoto Beer Lab)

places.cu: Brewpub pouring its own craft beers, half (US-style) or pint (2026 reviews) · e.g. Yakima Valley IPA ¥1,200 a pint, hōjicha stout ¥1,200, kabusecha white ale ¥700 a half, macadamia brown ale, fruit sours from ¥800 a half, Sudachi Mint Seltzer ¥500 (May–June 2026) · snacks: house kara-age ¥850, edamame ¥450, fried cheese with black pepper ¥600, fries, salmon jerky (2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Craft beer · Shichijo, a brewpub by the Takase River] A small brewery-bar beside the Takase River near Shichijo, pouring its own beers — from a Yakima Valley IPA to Kyoto-tea brews like hōjicha stout and kabusecha white ale — by the half (about ¥700–800) or pint (about ¥1,100–1,200). Order at the counter, sit by the water, add kara-age or fried cheese. Open daily 13:00–23:00.
places.chef: Brewer not named · Per Tabelog: opened 30 March 2018, with its first batch and grand opening on 27 April 2018. places.gfd: Not gluten-free: a brewpub of malt beers, with fried snacks (2026 reviews).

places.hood: Kitashirakawa, across from Kyoto University of the Arts
places.cu: Café of curries and homemade sweets among plants and old furniture (official site; reviews) · combination curry with soft-boiled egg about ¥1,200 (June 2025), butter chicken curry, pork keema and chicken curry · carrot cake with cream cheese and walnuts, seasonal pudding à la mode ¥990, chocolate-and-berry parfait ¥890 (September 2025), iced café au lait, herbal tea (2025–2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Café · Kitashirakawa, curry and parfaits among old furniture] A leafy, quietly stylish café run by the antiques shop SOWGEN, opposite Kyoto University of the Arts on Shirakawa-dori. Lunch is a gentle, vegetable-rich curry — the combination plate is about ¥1,200 — and the sweets are worth the trip: carrot cake, pudding à la mode (¥990) and small parfaits. Weekdays only; online bookings taken.
places.chef: Run by SOWGEN (antiques, plants and design); staff not named · Per the official site: SOWGEN deals in antiques, brocante, plants and interior design; そうげんカフェ is its Kitashirakawa café, which absorbed the café of its Shijo shop. Tabelog gives the opening as 1 August 2005; a June 2025 reviewer calls it a local staple of more than 15 years. · Combination curry; pudding à la mode.
places.gfd: Ask. Curries with rice, carrot cake, parfaits and pudding; no gluten information is published (2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Chicken and pork curries and dairy sweets; nothing vegan is marked (2025–2026 reviews).

places.hood: Aburanokoji-Nakadachiuri — 13 min from Imadegawa Stn
places.cu: Kuroge wagyu yakiniku (reviews) · owner’s recommended thick-cut harami and horumon in a sweet-savoury marinade; wagyu tongue; kalbi; an assorted Kuroge wagyu platter with cubed fillet steak; chateaubriand off the menu; chirimen rice bowl; vegetables (2024–2026 reviews) · about ¥5,500 with two drinks for a light meal (December 2024); typically ¥6,000–10,000 a head (2025–2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Yakiniku · Nishijin-south, a neighbourhood wagyu house] A well-loved yakiniku shop tucked in a residential street west of the Imperial Palace, where the friendly owner talks you through the cuts. Try the thick-cut harami and marinated horumon, wagyu tongue, and ask about the off-menu chateaubriand; a chirimen rice bowl rounds things off. Most spend ¥6,000–10,000. Open only Monday and Friday to Sunday evenings.
places.chef: Owner not named · Per 2024–2026 reviews: a long-regarded yakiniku restaurant in the Imadegawa area known for fresh Kuroge wagyu, a generous owner full of grilling tips, and an off-menu chateaubriand. · Thick-cut harami; off-menu chateaubriand.
places.gfd: Ask. Wagyu yakiniku with sweet-savoury marinades and tare; no gluten information is published (reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a wagyu yakiniku house (reviews).

places.n: 湯葉料理 かめや本家 (Yuba Ryori Kameya Honke)
places.hood: Omiya just north of Shijo — 1 min from Hankyu Omiya Stn
places.cu: Yuba and tofu kaiseki in a townhouse, with the popular yuba hot pot, yudofu and nama-fu (official site) · shojin kaiseki “Rokujo” ¥5,000 plus tax: sakizuke, appetizers, yudofu, sesame tofu, fresh yuba sashimi, dengaku, small dish, simmered dish, shojin tempura, steamed dish, rice, soup, pickles and dessert — fully plant-based (official menu) · yuba kaiseki: fresh yuba sashimi, three-flavour denga…
places.notes: [Yuba · Shijo-Omiya, a Taisho-era yuba house with a vegan course] An old townhouse yuba restaurant by Hankyu Omiya Station: fresh yuba sashimi, dengaku, the soy-milk yuba hot pot, and a fully plant-based shojin kaiseki (no fish dashi, egg, dairy or alliums) for ¥5,000 plus tax. Reservation only; dining room upstairs, shoes off; no strollers or wheelchairs. Weekend lunch by advance booking.
places.chef: Kitchen (unnamed) · A March 2026 reviewer calls it a long-established yuba restaurant dating from the Taisho era. Photos of Showa-era stars line the walls (November 2025). Reviewers describe friendly women staff (November 2025). · Yuba hot pot; fresh yuba sashimi; shojin kaiseki.
places.gfd: Ask. Yuba and tofu kaiseki served with soy sauce, nama-fu (wheat gluten), shojin tempura and yuba-and-shrimp spring rolls; no gluten information (official menu; 2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Some vegan options: the shojin kaiseki “Rokujo” (¥5,000 plus tax) is made without fish, shrimp, crab, meat, shellfish, egg, dairy, green onion, garlic, nira, rakkyo, onion or fish dashi, per the official menu. The yuba kaiseki courses include yuba-and-shrimp spring rolls. Book the Rokujo course ahead.
places.hours: Dinner 17:00–21:30 (food L.O. 20:00, drinks 20:30), Tuesday–Saturday; Sunday 17:00–21:00; closed Monday; lunch on Saturdays and Sundays by reservation made the day before (Tabelog). places.n: ミーミーミー (ME ME ME)
places.hood: Near Kawaramachi-Marutamachi by the Kamo River — 5 min from Jingu-Marutamachi Stn
places.cu: American-style breakfast café, said “Mi Mi Mi” (September 2025) · pancake set with bacon, sunny-side-up egg, salad, fruit and a drink ¥1,800 (November 2025) · cornmeal pancakes with bacon, eggs, fruit and salad (December 2025; February 2026) · French toast (March 2026) · coffee and toast breakfast about ¥1,400 (August 2026) · café latte, chai latte, straightforward coffee (2025–2026)
places.notes: [Breakfast café · near the Kamo River at Marutamachi] A small retro, American-feeling café in an alley off the Kamo, open from 8:30 for pancake plates — cornmeal pancakes with bacon and eggs, French toast — and good coffee or chai. Order at the register; queues by 10:00. Some reviewers found the service brusque.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · No owner is named in the sources read. Two 2026 reviewers found the service cold, one describing food and napkins being tossed onto the table (April 2026). · Cornmeal pancakes; breakfast plates.

places.vgd: Not vegan: breakfast plates with bacon, eggs and dairy (2025–2026 reviews).

places.hood: Between Higashi and Nishi Hongan-ji — 15 min on foot from Kyoto Station
places.cu: A café in a Taisho-era townhouse with seasonal Kyoto-vegetable plate lunches by an experienced chef (Tabelog shop text) · one plate lunch, different on weekdays and holidays: sawara and assorted vegetable tempura (March and September 2026); tofu hamburg steak plate (March 2026) · firm, old-fashioned pudding; tea (February 2026)
places.notes: [Plate lunch · between the Hongan-ji temples, a one-person machiya café] A 100-year-old townhouse café down narrow alleys, with tatami and low tables over two floors, where a single cook turns out one carefully made plate lunch a day — crisp sawara and vegetable tempura, a tofu hamburg — and a firm Showa-style pudding. Book (even same-day) to avoid waiting; slow but worth it. Cash only.
places.chef: Owner-cook (unnamed) · Tabelog’s shop text describes dishes by an experienced chef in a converted Taisho-era townhouse. An April 2026 reviewer found the café “being managed by just one person”, cooking at the entrance kitchen; a February 2026 guest marvelled at one staff member covering both floors. A March 2026 reviewer wondered whether a couple runs it. A May 2026 guest found the building’s age and a restroom without a hand basin unsettling, though the food was outstanding. · Seasonal plate lunch; pudding.
places.gfd: Ask. A single plate lunch that changes — sawara and vegetable tempura, tofu hamburg steak — plus pudding; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Seasonal Kyoto-vegetable plate lunches, sometimes with a tofu hamburg, but most days include fish, and dashi and seasonings are not described (Tabelog shop text; 2026 reviews).

places.hood: Nanzen-ji approach, Okazaki — 7 min from Keage Stn
places.cu: Tea in the house of Yamagata Aritomo’s villa, overlooking the garden by the seventh-generation Ogawa Jihei (Tabelog shop text) · café set ¥1,200, any combination of seven or eight drinks and sweets (July–October 2026): matcha (hot or chilled) with dorayaki or Kyo-azuki dorayaki; monaka ice of matcha and red bean; Japanese white peach juice; dry sweets; Russian cakes from Murakami Kaishindo; Kyoto…
places.notes: [Garden café · Nanzen-ji, Yamagata Aritomo’s villa] Tea on the tatami of a Meiji-era villa looking over one of Kyoto’s great modern gardens, laid out by the seventh-generation Ogawa Jihei for Yamagata Aritomo. Pay the ¥600 garden entry, then a ¥1,200 set of matcha or juice with a sweet (dorayaki, monaka ice, Murakami Kaishindo Russian cake). Book ahead; open from 9:00.
places.chef: Garden café staff (unnamed) · Tabelog’s shop text: the villa was built for the politician Yamagata Aritomo between 1894 and 1896, and the garden was made by the seventh-generation Ogawa Jihei on Yamagata’s instructions. Reviewers note an explanation of the garden before tea (August and October 2026) and its role in pre–Russo-Japanese War diplomatic talks (August 2026). · Matcha and sweets with the garden view.
places.gfd: Ask. A tea-and-sweets set — matcha, dorayaki, monaka ice, dry sweets, Russian cakes from Murakami Kaishindo — none described for gluten (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Matcha and juices are plant-based; the sweets are not described (2026 reviews).

places.n: グランドバーガー (GRAND BURGER)

places.notes: [Burgers · Teramachi south of Imadegawa] A small burger café by the Imperial Palace side of Teramachi: thick, juicy handmade patties with bacon, cheese, plenty of avocado or a fried egg, fish and chips with tartare, and hot fries — a set comes to just under ¥2,000. Lightly seasoned, with no signature sauce; busy with takeaway and visitors from abroad. One February 2026 guest found it soggy and pricey. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Kitchen and counter staff (unnamed) · Per Tabelog: a hamburger, café and pancake shop on Teramachi south of Imadegawa. Reviewers in 2025–2026 describe carefully handmade burgers, many takeaway orders and overseas visitors, and a small room that fills quickly. · Bacon cheeseburger; avocado burger.

places.notes: [Japanese set meals and izakaya · by Demachiyanagi Stn] A renovated townhouse near Demachiyanagi that one reviewer likens to a kaiseki kitchen: lunch sets of thick-cut sashimi, tempura or fried fugu with five small obanzai for ¥1,200–2,000, and evenings of obanzai, saikyo-yaki and beef-tendon stew with sake. Popular with locals, so book; when the owner works lunch alone, expect a wait and brisk manners. Irregular closures on Instagram.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed), sometimes alone at lunch (April 2026), Male staff in the evening (July 2025) · Per Tabelog: an izakaya opened 13 March 2023 near Demachiyanagi; registered as an official listing by the shop. A July 2025 reviewer calls it the lunch of a Japanese kaiseki restaurant; reviewers in 2026 note fish said to be shipped from Kochi (August 2026) and an owner handling a full room alone at lunch (April 2026). · Sashimi set lunch; obanzai.

Lines at weekend lunch; the beef cutlet is paused while beef is dear. QR, no cards. Closed Thursday.

Book for the terrace. Some find portions small for the price, and one August 2026 table waited for water and food. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Kitchen and floor staff (unnamed) · Per Tabelog: a trattoria-pizzeria, bar and pasta restaurant on Kiyamachi with a Kamogawa summer deck; registered as an official listing by the operator. Reviewers in 2026 describe terrace or indoor seating chosen at booking, a quick fill on holidays, and a regular who works nearby. · Pizza; terrace dining by the Kamo River.

places.n: 日本料理と日本酒 惠史 (Satoshi)
places.hood: Ogawa Aneyakoji, between Nijojo-mae and Karasuma Oike — 5 min from Karasuma Oike Stn
places.cu: Japanese cooking and sake: seasonal produce such as Ise lobster, eel and Kyoto vegetables grilled on a dedicated hearth over binchotan, with red miso soup made from the lobster shells (official site) · every sake in the shop can be bought to take home (official site) · omakase three-course meals ¥5,500 (April 2025) and ¥6,000 (November 2025), opening with many small appetizers — fuki miso, miso-c…
places.notes: [Japanese cuisine and sake · Nijo, a former Wakuden head chef’s counter] An 11-seat renovated townhouse where the owner, 17 years at Wakuden, cooks almost single-handed: a run of small sake snacks, sashimi, and seasonal fish, Ise lobster or eel over binchotan, from a ¥5,500 three-course omakase. Strong on sake, with frequent sake events; drinks are pricey and late arrivals pay 10% service. Strict cancellation fees.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed on the site’s pages read; "Tomofumi Hoshina" in a January 2025 review), formerly head chef of Murasakino Wakuden’s bento kitchen (official site) · Per the official site (店主紹介): born 28 June 1975; worked at 鶴清 from 1997 and joined Wakuden in April 1999, rising through the grill, the cutting board and the simmering station at Kyoto Wakuden in Kyoto Isetan, then becoming head chef of the Murasakino Wakuden bento workshop in the owner’s thirties, with further kaiseki work at Kodaiji, Nagoya and Osaka Wakuden; left in September 2016 after 17 years and opened 日本料理と日本酒 惠史 in June 2020. Some furniture and tableware date from the Edo period. · To work worthy of the Wakuden name, in gratitude to the okami and seniors there (official site). · Charcoal-grilled seasonal dishes; sake.
places.gfd: Ask. Kaiseki-style courses with miso-cured and soy-seasoned dishes, sashimi, and charcoal-grilled seafood (official site; 2025–26 reviews); no gluten information.
places.vgd: Not vegan: a Japanese kitchen built on katsuo dashi, with charcoal-grilled Ise lobster, eel and fish (official site; 2025–26 reviews).

An August 2026 reviewer chose it as a regular entry in Tabelog’s top-100 lists that allows smoking at all seats. · Assorted horse sashimi; horse liver.

places.vgd: Not vegan: a horse-meat specialist — sashimi, liver, yakiniku and hot pot (2026 reviews).

Tabelog notes closures at New Year and over the Chinese Spring Festival. · Mapo tofu; dim sum.

places.notes: [Izakaya · Shijo-Karasuma, yakitori in an alley townhouse] A renovated townhouse at the end of a narrow alley off Yanaginobanba: big Kyoto-chicken skewers, grilled offal, Kyoto vegetables, yuba with ikura and a homemade pizza, with a long sake list — popular for dates and parties, so book. One diner found the yakitori salty and the corn tempura heavy (August 2026). One drink each. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: Not named in a source; run by 株式会社 京色 (official site) · One of five Kyoto restaurants run by 株式会社 京色, founded by a president and two chefs who studied together at a cooking school and trained in Japanese, Western and creative cooking (official site); its sisters are うらやま京色 (kushiage), 祇園 晩餐 京色, 祇園天ぷら晩餐 and 角打ちと麺 ばんさん (official site). Reviewers in 2026 describe a stone-paved approach, a counter downstairs and sunken seating upstairs, individually plated course dishes, and fish from the central market each morning. · From the site: particular about ingredients such as Kyoto Akadori chicken and fresh vegetables, for "bold dishes with delicate technique hidden in them" (official site, translated). · Kyoto Akadori yakitori; grilled vegetable platter.

places.notes: [Sake-lees cooking · Shijo-Karasuma, Tamanohikari brewery's townhouse] Fushimi brewer Tamanohikari's own townhouse: a ground-floor bar where ¥1,500 buys 30 minutes of self-pour from about fifteen of its sakes, and an upstairs dining room of gentle sake-lees and koji lunches with amazake and kasujiru, and sake-paired courses at night. Some found portions small and service slow (September 2026). No service charge.
places.chef: Not named in a source; run directly by 玉乃光酒造 (official site) · Run directly by the sake brewer 玉乃光酒造 of Fushimi, which began brewing in 1673 in Wakayama and is now in its 13th generation (official site); opened 1 March 2022 (Tabelog). Reviewers in 2026 describe a renovated townhouse with a bar on the ground floor, a dining room upstairs, staff in Tamanohikari T-shirts, and sake events such as a September 2026 sanma night. · Per its site, a place to eat dishes made with the brewery's junmai sake lees with its sake, and a showcase of ideas for using them at home (official site, paraphrased). · Sake-lees and koji cooking; self-pour sake bar.

places.notes: [Kyoto sake and duck · Kyoto Station, a one-man basement counter] A seven-seat basement counter by Kyoto Station where the owner, alone, pours sake from every one of Kyoto Prefecture's 40 breweries in small measures with the story of each, alongside Kyo-Tamba duck from tongue to tenderloin. Portions are small (August 2026); a little hard to find and to walk into. Call ahead. Cash only. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
places.chef: 川嶋隆徳 · Owner, running the shop alone (official site) · Per the official site, owner 川嶋隆徳 runs the seven-seat counter alone, pairing Kyoto sake with Kyo-duck raised in Kyotamba, and stocks sake from all 40 breweries in Kyoto Prefecture, large and small. Diners in 2024–2026 describe a basement counter close to the owner, careful explanations of each brewery, rare duck cuts, and mostly solo guests. · From the official site: Kyoto sake for visitors and locals alike — "京都の日本酒にこだわり" (particular about Kyoto sake). · Kyo-Tamba duck with Kyoto sake.

places.cu: Kyoto-style motsu-nabe in a Kyoto dashi broth (official site; 2025–2026 reviews) · Kyo motsu-nabe ¥1,880 a portion: "white" (Kyoto white miso, the signature), "golden soy", "spicy red", "yellow" (this shop only); mentaiko motsu-nabe ¥2,400; summer "kara-nabe" ¥2,100 (official site) · toppings: Omi beef offal ¥1,100, pork belly ¥880, Daisen chicken ¥770, honeycomb tripe, Hanbei three-colour nama-f…
places.notes: [Motsu-nabe · Pontocho alley, Kyoto white-miso hot pot] The original shop (2008) of a three-shop Kyoto motsu-nabe house, tucked in an alley between Kiyamachi and Pontocho: Omi beef offal in a Kyoto dashi broth — the white-miso version is the one to order — finished with stone-ground noodles or egg zosui, and all-you-can-drink courses from ¥5,000. Book on the website; winter fills. ¥380 table charge.
places.chef: Second-generation manager known in the shop as "Pe-san" (official site); owner not named · Per the official site, 亀八 本店 opened in April 2008 as the first shop; the name pairs 亀 (turtle, for luck) and 八 (eight, for endless happiness). Early on the first manager stood outside every day calling in customers; word of mouth made it so busy that winter tables could not be booked, without spending on advertising. The second-generation manager, a regular of a sister shop since university who joined in 2009 and worked at the annex 亀八別館 first, keeps the founding recipe (official site). Sister shops: 亀八別館 (Pontocho) and 亀八 山科店 (official site). · From the site: a hot pot that starts from taking dashi, the heart of Kyoto cooking — "a hot pot made for drinking the soup" (official site, translated). · Kyo motsu-nabe "white" (white miso).

places.notes: [Ramen · Marutamachi, Matsusaka-beef ramen] A small, polished ramen shop thirty seconds from Marutamachi Station, simmering Matsusaka beef for ten hours into a milky, creamy broth set with Kyoto dashi. Shio, shoyu or Kyoto miso (¥1,500–1,700) come with rare A5 wagyu slices, a soft egg and a free extra serving of noodles. Pricey for ramen, and many diners are tourists, but even sceptical locals came away impressed. Closed Sunday.

The shop calls itself Japan's oldest candy maker, over 450 years old. A bag is ¥700 (¥400 small), with Uji teas beside it — a gentle sweetness and a story to take home. Open daily 10:00–16:00; cash only.
places.chef: Family shop, people not named (official site signs as みなとや一同) · Per the official site: Japan’s longest-established candy shop, over 450 years old; the legend: in Keicho 4 (1599) a wife of the 江村 family was buried, and days later a baby’s cry was heard from the grave — the child of the dead wife; a woman had come every night to buy candy and stopped once the child was dug out; the child became a monk at eight and a renowned priest, dying at 68 in 1666; the candy came to be called the ghost’s child-rearing candy. The shop has supplied its candy to はぐくみハッピーギフト, a Higashiyama ward gift for new parents, and received a letter of thanks (official site, March 2021). Candy and tea are made by hand (official site, September 2026). · Per the official site: to keep passing on the story of “the candy that carried a life”. · Yurei kosodate ame.

places.chef: 川口聡 · Fourth-generation proprietor (serai.jp) · Opened in 1930 as a French-style café by the bakery 進々堂, which began in 1913 and was the first in Kyoto to sell French bread; the founder, 続木斉, had studied bread-making in Paris and modelled the café on those in the Latin Quarter, hoping Japanese students would also learn Western esprit (serai.jp). The long one-piece tables and benches were commissioned from the woodworker 黒田辰秋 so many students could sit at once (serai.jp; rurubu; November 2025 review). The fourth-generation proprietor 川口聡 says the café's atmosphere stays the same because of the founding ideals (serai.jp, undated). The group follows 医食同源 (food as medicine) and uses pesticide-free vegetables from contract farms. · Per the official site: 医食同源 — preventing illness through food, cooking that is delicious and good for the body, shared by all the group’s shops. · Xiaolongbao.

One October 2026 reviewer credits the menu to a chef from a well-known Osaka French restaurant. Open till 23:00; book ahead.

Value set lunches of kara-age or chicken nanban from ¥1,000, a weekend mini kaiseki, and fish-led dishes and courses at night. One August 2026 group found the kaiseki portions small and some drinks never came. Open till 22:30.

The operator lists five restaurants. A reviewer notes the menu changed over six years (October 2025). · Freshness and flavour judged by the cooks (operator site). · Set lunches; banquet courses.

places.notes: [Vietnamese · Kitashirakawa, Vietnamese-French in a canal-side house] A small Vietnamese-French restaurant in a white house by the Shirakawa canal, near the Philosopher's Path: an 11-dish lunch of six pretty starters, a gentle collagen-rich pho and desserts for about ¥2,900, made with Kyoto farm vegetables, and warm hosts who talk about Vietnam. No vegetarian or vegan requests. Book; closed Tuesday and some other days.
places.chef: Producer: フォン (named on the official site); the chef is not named · Southern Vietnam (the producer's home cooking, per the official site) · Per the official site, XUAN began in Tokyo's Nihonbashi in 1997, opened as VIETNAM FRENCH XUAN on Gokomachi in Nakagyo-ku in 2001, and moved to Kitashirakawa in 2014. Its cooking is based on the southern Vietnamese food the producer, フォン, grew up with, using produce from Kyoto farms and fishing ports, Asuka in Nara, and ingredients sourced in Vietnam; it also runs a sweets and ao dai brand, リンホア, and Vietnam tours. Reviewers in 2026 describe a chef and a lady who explain each dish and chat with guests, and the mezzanine sells made-to-order ao dai (Tabelog). · From the site: using fresh ingredients as they are, cooked in the way of Vietnamese daily life (official site, paraphrased). · Eleven-dish lunch; chicken pho.
places.gfd: Ask: rice-noodle pho and rice-paper spring rolls, but fried spring rolls, sauces and desserts are not described for wheat (2025–2026 reviews).

places.n: 日本料理 藤井 (Nihon Ryori Fujii)
places.hood: Philosopher's Path, below Ginkaku-ji — 1 min from the Minamidacho bus stop
places.cu: Seasonal Kyoto kaiseki that begins with a cup of dashi, in an old house by the Philosopher's Path (official site; 2023–2026 reviews) · no fixed menu — courses change monthly at ¥8,000, ¥15,000 and ¥20,000+ (plus tax and 10% service) (official site) · signature fried sesame tofu; hamo and eel in summer; firefly squid, bamboo shoots and cherry salmon in spring; sea bream rice with sesame sauce; a N…
places.notes: [Kaiseki · Philosopher's Path, dashi first] A calm kaiseki restaurant in a renovated house a minute from the Philosopher's Path, where every meal opens with a cup of dashi: monthly courses from ¥8,000 at lunch, with fried sesame tofu and summer hamo the dishes people remember, at a counter facing the chef or in rooms overlooking maples. Reviewers mention a Michelin star (2024–2025). Plus 10% service; cancellation fees. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: 藤井 孝之輔 · Owner-chef (official site) · Per the official site, 藤井 孝之輔 trained at 高台寺 和久傳 and 櫻川, became head chef of 水円 in Gion-Yasaka, and opened 日本料理 藤井 near Ginkaku-ji in February 2018; the hobbies listed are skiing, futsal and driving. The site describes the cooking as "質実、枯淡" — plain and austere — for newcomers to Japanese food and connoisseurs alike. Reviewers from 2023 to 2026 describe a stylishly renovated old house where every table looks onto seasonal plants, a counter facing the chef, careful tableware, and a one-Michelin-star rating (February 2024; January 2025). · From the site: "日本料理 藤井での食事のはじまりは、出汁から。全ての料理の礎です。" (a meal here begins with dashi — the foundation of every dish). · Fried sesame tofu; hamo.
places.gfd: Ask: the shop asks for allergies and dislikes at booking (official site); courses include tempura (sesame-tofu tempura is a signature) and soy- and dashi-based dishes (2023–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: every meal starts from a kombu-and-bonito dashi (official site; January 2025); fish courses such as hamo and sea bream.
places.hours: Official site: last entry 11:30–13:30 for lunch and 17:00–20:00 for dinner (Tabelog: 11:30–15:00, 17:00–22:00); closed Wednesday. places.notes: [Curry · Mototanaka, a decades-old neighbourhood curry house] A small curry house a minute from Mototanaka Station on the Eizan line: well-balanced Indian-style chicken, korma and vegetable curries with white or brown rice, a green curry with konjac, and home-made carrot cake and apple crumble. A diner back after 20 years found the taste and staff unchanged (October 2025); another found it just okay (October 2023). Cash only; closed Wednesday and Thursday.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Reviewers from 2016 to 2025 describe a long-running local curry house with flowers on each table and the same staff over decades; one diner returning after about 20 years found it unchanged (October 2025). · Chicken curry; korma.
places.gfd: Ask: Indian-style curries with white or brown rice, but roux, cakes and the Thai and green curries are not described for wheat (2022–2025 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask: a vegetable curry set is on the menu (May 2023), but the korma uses fresh cream and other curries are chicken (2022–2023 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: 11:00–22:00 (last order 21:30); closed Wednesday and Thursday (the next day when either is a public holiday). No reservations. 18 seats; non-smoking; children welcome; take-away. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). 1 min walk from Eizan Railway Mototanaka Stn.

places.notes: [Yoshoku · Senbon-Imadegawa, pick-your-own plates and pancakes] A homely yoshoku café in a renovated townhouse on Senbon-dori near Kitano Tenmangu: pick two or three of hamburg, fried shrimp, ginger pork or karaage with rice and miso soup for about ¥1,400, or hamburg omurice and pancakes. Diners mention waits and hard-to-flag service (March 2023, July 2024) and so-so coffee (November 2023). Cash only; closed Friday.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Reviewers from 2022 to 2026 describe a renovated Kyoto townhouse with chair and tatami seating, a home-like feel, and a fifteenth anniversary in July 2026. A regular has logged 17 visits since 2015 (Tabelog). · Choose-your-sides plate; hamburg omurice.

Cash only; closed Thursday, with extra days off posted out front.

places.notes: [Yudofu · near Honen-in and the Philosopher’s Path, about 50 years] A long-established tofu restaurant in a quiet Japanese house with tatami rooms and a stone-garden view: smooth yudofu in the house dashi, rich goma-dofu and yuba tempura in sets from ¥2,618. English menu and staff; free parking; closed Wednesday.
places.chef: 折田 真人 · Owner (the invoice holder) · Tabelog’s invoice number T7810562887990 is registered to the individual 折田 真人 (NTA register). The shop’s Tabelog text says it has been open about 50 years and that its yudofu dashi is unchanged since it was founded; an August 2026 guest returned after 40 years and found the tofu unchanged. · The yudofu dashi has not changed since the founding (Tabelog). · Yudofu; goma-dofu.
places.gfd: Ask. Tabelog tags gluten-free options, but no dish is described as gluten-free; the yudofu comes with a soy-based dipping sauce, the sets include tempura, and awafu dengaku is made with wheat gluten (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog tags vegan and vegetarian options, but the yudofu uses the shop’s traditional dashi and comes with bonito flakes, and the sets include shrimp tempura (Tabelog; April 2026).

Cash only; BYO allowed; closed Monday.
places.chef: Owner-chef (unnamed) · Reviewers say the restaurant is run by one person, who cooks and serves with good timing (March, May and December 2025), and who chooses the tea served at the end (December 2023). · Vegetable “flower crown”; seasonal French courses.
places.gfd: Ask. Vegetable-led French courses — potages, the “flower crown” vegetable starter, fish and meat mains with several sauces, bread on the side; no gluten information (2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options and the courses are rich in vegetables (the flower crown uses dozens of kinds, May 2024), but the mains are fish or meat and nothing is described as vegan.

places.chef: Per Tabelog and the official site: a café and dining bar devoted to Kyoto craft beer and sake, with obanzai and set lunches. places.gfd: Ask. Obanzai small plates, kara-age, onigiri and pasta alongside beer (2026 reviews); kara-age and pasta contain wheat; no gluten information.
places.vgd: Not vegan: dashi-based obanzai, grilled mackerel, octopus, kara-age (2026 reviews).

places.cu: Temple shojin cuisine and Kyoto set meals (official site) · Shojin Gozen ¥3,520: seasonal dressed dish, simmered dishes, fried dish, rice, pickles, Negoro-jiru soup, dessert — marked vegan (official menu) · Dashimaki Gozen ¥2,530 with fresh yuba; Tempura Gozen ¥2,750; tempura rice bowl set ¥1,760; yuba udon or soba ¥1,650 (official menu) · dinner box Kikyo ¥3,630 (official menu) · limited shojin …
places.notes: [Shojin and Kyoto set meals · Higashiyama Shichijo, inside Chishakuin temple] The restaurant and café of the Chishakuin temple lodge, near Sanjusangendo, with a round counter and garden views. The Shojin Gozen is plant-based with a kombu and shiitake dashi and marked vegan by the restaurant; dashimaki, yuba and tempura sets too, plus a limited shojin afternoon tea. Open daily 10:00–20:00.
places.chef: Per the official site: the tearoom (saryo) of Chishakuin, the head temple of the Shingon Chisan school, serving the temple's shojin cuisine and Kyoto dishes, on the ground floor of Chishakuin Kaikan. Operated by 株式会社ハトヤ瑞鳳閣 (official company page). Reviews in 2026 describe the lodge renovated to hotel standard. · Shojin cuisine as practised at the temple: no meat or fish, seasonal plant ingredients (official site). · Shojin Gozen with Negoro-jiru soup; dashimaki and yuba sets.
places.gfd: Ask. Set meals include tempura and fried dishes, soy-seasoned simmered dishes and udon or soba (official menu); no gluten information.
places.vgd: The Shojin Gozen is marked vegetarian and vegan, made with plant ingredients and a kombu and shiitake dashi (official site, Japanese text: 「植物性食材と昆布・椎茸の出汁で仕立てた、ベジタリアン・ヴィーガン対応の精進御膳」). places.notes: [Yakitori · Marutamachi, salt-grilled skewers over binchotan] A 15-seat counter on Marutamachi where an owner with over ten years in yakitori grills local jidori, rare cuts and seasonal vegetables over Tosa binchotan, mostly with salt; finish with the grilled rice ball with fermented butter.
