places.cu: A large late-night seafood izakaya with Kyoto vegetables (Tabelog; 2022–2025 reviews) · chef's sashimi, grilled yellowtail collar, deep-fried conger eel, tekka maki, grilled Thai mackerel, grilled stingray fin (2022–2025) · yuba sashimi, maitake tempura, Kyoto nama-fu dengaku with miso, miso-marinated tofu, grilled mentaiko, fried chicken, chijimi (2023–2025) · courses of sashimi, ankake, tempura…
places.notes: [Seafood izakaya · Kawaramachi, open till 2 a.m.] A roomy second-floor seafood izakaya at the Kawaramachi station exit, open into the small hours: sashimi, grilled collar and Thai mackerel, Kyoto nama-fu dengaku and party courses with two hours of drinks from ¥4,500, in semi-private booths. ¥480 appetiser charge; smoking allowed per Tabelog. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Opened 29 May 2014 (Tabelog). Reviewers from 2022 to 2025 describe a spacious stylish room with semi-private seating, prompt staff who remembered a guest's booking by name (November 2024), and quick drinks service. · Sashimi; nama-fu dengaku.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: tempura, chijimi, fried chicken, nama-fu dengaku and soy-based dishes (2022–2025 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a seafood izakaya — sashimi, grilled fish, conger eel (2022–2025 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: Tue–Thu 17:00–1:30 (last orders food 0:30, drinks 1:00); Fri and nights before holidays 17:00–2:00; Sat 16:30–2:00; Sun and holidays 16:30–1:30; closed Monday (Tuesday when Monday is a holiday). Reservations taken. Appetiser charge ¥480 — Tabelog, Japanese original 「お通し480円」. 70 seats with…

places.n: WAGYU SUKIYAKI 祇園 (WAGYU SUKIYAKI Gion)
places.hood: Nishi-Ishigaki by the Kamo River, Shijo — 3 min walk from Hankyu Kawaramachi
places.cu: A new (July 2026) A5-wagyu sukiyaki restaurant above Kiyamachi (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · "A5 Rank Wagyu Sukiyaki Set", cooked in front of you, with seasonal vegetables, egg and rice (October 2026) · truffle egg over rice to finish (August 2026) · a bar and rooftop in the same venue (October 2026)
places.notes: [Sukiyaki · Kiyamachi-Shijo, a new A5-wagyu room] A sukiyaki restaurant that opened in July 2026 on the fourth floor of a Kiyamachi building by the Kamo River, serving A5 wagyu cooked at the table with egg and seasonal vegetables, and truffle egg over rice to finish; an English picture menu and a terrace for smoking. Only two reviews so far (August, October 2026). Closed Sunday and Monday.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Opened 15 July 2026 (Tabelog). Two 2026 reviewers describe A5 wagyu with beautiful marbling cooked in front of the guest, a quiet room in Kiyamachi, and a bar and rooftop in the same venue. It shares the RAKUAS Kiyamachi building (斎藤町123) with 隠れ酒場ともしび3rd (2F) and 京鴨 鴨蔵. · A5 wagyu sukiyaki.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: wagyu dipped in sauce and egg (October 2026); sukiyaki sauce is normally soy-based.
places.vgd: Not vegan: A5 wagyu sukiyaki with raw egg (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: Tue–Sat 11:45–14:15 and 17:00–22:00; closed Sunday and Monday. Reservations taken (private hire by phone). 33 seats: 10 at tables, 8 at the counter, plus a 14-seat terrace where dining is not allowed (smoking is allowed there). English picture menu; children, babies and strollers welcome. …

places.n: 隠れ酒場ともしび3rd 海鮮と炭火鶏焼 (Kakure Sakaba Tomoshibi 3rd)
places.hood: Nishi-Ishigaki, Shijo-Kawaramachi — 1 min walk from Hankyu Kawaramachi
places.cu: A lively seafood-and-charcoal-chicken izakaya, the third of the ともしび shops (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews) · sashimi platter of three ¥990; seafood yukhoe ¥680; smoked mackerel ¥680; yokowa tuna tataki; grilled nodoguro; butter-steamed clams ¥880; abalone with butter (2025–2026) · charcoal-grilled chicken, neck, tsukune ¥350, "Tomoshibi chicken" tulip wings ¥550, cartilage karaage ¥580 (2025–2026) ·…
places.notes: [Izakaya · Kiyamachi-Shijo, ¥100 highball happy hour] A busy second-floor izakaya by Hankyu Kawaramachi, opened in 2025: sashimi, charcoal-grilled chicken and cheap snacks, a ¥100-highball happy hour until 19:00, cheerful young staff, free extra dishes and smoking allowed. One diner waited so long that a tsukune order was cancelled (February 2026). No service charge.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Opened 3 March 2025 (Tabelog). The same name runs four shops in the Kyoto crawl — 隠れ酒場 ともしび (Karasuma-Takoyakushi), 肴と海鮮 ともしびセカンド, this 3rd and お酒とまるまる ともしびzero — none yet in this app. Reviewers in 2025–2026 describe energetic young staff who remember regulars, complimentary small dishes, and tablet ordering. It shares the RAKUAS Kiyamachi building with WAGYU SUKIYAKI 祇園 (4F). · Sashimi; charcoal-grilled chicken.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: karaage, tartar-sauce dishes, oden, soy-based grills (2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: seafood and charcoal-grilled chicken izakaya (Tabelog; reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: Sun–Thu and holidays 16:30–24:00 (last orders food 23:15, drinks 23:30); Fri, Sat and nights before holidays 16:30–1:00; closing days vary. Reservations taken. Happy hour until 19:00: highballs ¥100 and draft beer ¥250 with one dish from a set list (November 2025; February 2026; September …

places.n: 鉄板居酒屋 双葉 (Teppan Izakaya Futaba)
places.hood: Nishikiyamachi, north of Shijo — 5 min walk from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: A late-night creative teppan izakaya with natural wine (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews) · fresh-shrimp chili, the house favourite; "Futaba-yaki"; okonomiyaki; spicy Sichuan-style yakisoba; tonpei; grilled beef tendon with egg; mackerel toast; yukhoe sandwich (2025–2026) · appetiser of low-temperature beef tongue; beef carpaccio; gizzard confit; fried hoso and shrimp ajillo; kara-age; potato salad; pr…
places.notes: [Teppan izakaya · Nishikiyamachi, okonomiyaki and natural wine till 2 a.m.] A stylish, wine-minded teppan izakaya off Shijo-Kiyamachi where the owner pairs natural wines with fresh-shrimp chili, Futaba-yaki okonomiyaki, spicy yakisoba and beef-tendon teppan, open till 1–2 a.m. Diners note a 30-minute wait for the first dish and a cold counter (January 2026), strong flavours (November 2025) and a cramped room (April 2026). Smoking allowed. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Owner, not named in a source · Opened 30 April 2023 (Tabelog). Reviewers in 2025–2026 describe a modern Japanese room with an open-kitchen counter downstairs and tables upstairs, an owner who loves wine and explains each bottle, weekly changing specials, and a crowd that keeps arriving late at night. · Fresh-shrimp chili; Futaba-yaki.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: okonomiyaki, yakisoba, mackerel toast, karaage and sauces (2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: pork, beef, shrimp and egg teppan dishes (2025–2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: Tue–Fri 18:00–1:00; Sat and Sun 18:00–2:00; closed Monday and the day after a public holiday. Reservations advised — nearly always full late at night (March 2026); seat type may change. No cover charge — Tabelog, Japanese original 「無し」. 40 seats: an 8-seat counter at the open teppan, two t…

places.n: 京都氷屋 万年雪 (Kyoto Koriya Mannen Yuki)
places.hood: Umekoji Park / Kyoto Aquarium — 5 min from Umekoji-Kyotonishi Stn
places.cu: Year-round kakigori of pure ice frozen over three days, with homemade fruit syrups, condensed milk and white syrup (Tabelog): strawberry custard pie ¥1,750 (the most popular), matcha custard daifuku ¥1,750, freshly squeezed kiwi with almond jelly ¥1,600, kiwi milk, strawberry shortcake, strawberry tart, strawberry mascarpone; limited seasonal-fruit bowls; very large portions (2026 reviews)
places.notes: [Kakigori · Umekoji Park] A shaved-ice shop open all year, a minute from the Kyoto Aquarium bus stop: fluffy, very large bowls of three-day pure ice with fresh-fruit syrups — strawberry custard pie, kiwi with almond jelly, matcha custard daifuku — about ¥1,600–1,750 (mini sizes cheaper). Book online; no cards. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · Opened 15 April 2025 (Tabelog). · Pure ice shaved fluffy, enhanced by homemade syrups that concentrate fresh fruit (Tabelog). · Strawberry custard pie kakigori.
places.gfd: Ask. Shaved ice with fruit syrups, but many bowls are built with pie, tart, cake or daifuku elements (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: house condensed milk, custard, cream and mascarpone (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.hours: Mon, Tue and Thu–Sun 12:00–18:00; closed Wednesday; closing days may vary (Tabelog). Bookings through Air Reserve (airrsv.net/mannenyuki) (Tabelog); a September 2026 visitor found it easy to book. Order and pay at the entrance; cash or PayPay/Alipay, no cards or e-money (Tabelog; September 2026 rev…

menu.en: Freshly squeezed kiwi with almond jelly kakigori

places.cu: Old-style donuts, small but filling (2025–26 reviews): French cruller ¥190, kinako ¥190, coconut cake ¥230 (December 2025), chocolate cake ¥210, whipped French ¥230 (December 2025), apple fritter, sesame milk, rum raisin, a snowman donut at Christmas, lemon cake, an-donut, double chocolate, plain cake, twist, mini donuts; Shinshu apple juice
places.notes: [Donuts · Horikawa shopping street] The Horikawa branch of a Kitaoji donut shop, with a wood-lined room and a few seats: moist, old-fashioned donuts from about ¥190 — French crullers, a crisp apple fritter, kinako and lemon cake. Cash only; closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Staff (unnamed) · Branch of かもドーナツ, whose main shop is in Kitaoji (December 2025 review). A 2020 report on 4travel mentions its donuts at a bakery fair in the Fujii Daimaru basement. · Apple fritter; French cruller.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: wheat donuts (2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Ingredients not described; cake donuts and crullers usually contain egg and dairy (2025–26 reviews).
places.hours: Mon and Wed–Sun 9:30–20:30; closed Tuesday (Tabelog). No bookings; cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). 6 seats for eating in; non-smoking (Tabelog; December 2025 review). No parking (December 2025 review). In the Horikawa shopping street, in the 出水団地 block; the main shop is in Kitaoji (T…

places.hood: Nishinokyo, west of Nijo Stn — 5 min from JR Nijo Stn
places.cu: Charcoal yakitori of Okutanba chicken (June 2026 review; Tabelog matome): thigh, tsukune with tare, wings, heart, bonjiri, neck with wasabi, garlic gizzards; green onion, zucchini, baby corn in the husk and lotus root skewers; potato salad, avocado and cream cheese, yam kara-age, young-chicken kara-age, braised beef tendon, a dobin-steamed dish; shibazuke fried rice and a yakitori rice bowl to fi…
places.notes: [Charcoal yakitori · Nijo] A calm 11-seat yakitori counter near Nijo Station grilling Okutanba chicken over charcoal: crisp-juicy thigh, tsukune, garlic gizzards and seasonal vegetables by the single skewer, with shibazuke fried rice to finish. About ¥5,000–6,000. Book ahead; closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed) · Opened 30 September 2023 (Tabelog). · Chicken thigh; shibazuke fried rice.
places.gfd: Ask. Salt-grilled skewers are possible, but tare skewers, kara-age and fried rice are on the menu (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a chicken yakitori bar; some vegetable skewers (2026 reviews).

Bookings taken, often full on Saturdays; same-day phone bookings sometimes possible (Tabelog; March and May 2026 reviews). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and QR; no e-…

places.n: crème plus (クレーム プリュス)
places.hood: Senbon-dori north of Nijo Stn — 7 min from Nijo Stn
places.cu: Small pâtisserie and café known for its custard (2025–26 reviews): custard cream puff ¥350 (July 2026), crème brûlée torched in front of you when you buy it, baked cheesecake with a hint of salt, banana roll cake, pudding with brown sugar on the side, chestnut Mont Blanc ¥630 (July 2026), fraisier, lemon tart, espresso tiramisu, whole gâteau chocolat; matcha and hojicha lattes with cat latte art
places.notes: [Pâtisserie & café · Senbon-dori] A tiny cake shop with six seats north of Nijo Station, known for rich custard: cream puffs that sell out by evening (¥350), crème brûlée torched as you buy it, salty-rich baked cheesecake and banana roll cake, with lattes. About ¥1,000 or less. Closed Thursday.
places.chef: Pastry chef (unnamed) · Opened 7 March 2015 (Tabelog). A small team, per the Tabelog listing. · Custard cream puff; crème brûlée.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: cream puffs, tarts, roll cakes and cookies (2025–26 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: custard, cream, cheese and egg-rich pastries (2025–26 reviews).
places.hours: Mon–Wed and Fri–Sun 11:30–19:30 (café and drinks to 18:30); closed Thursday; temporary closures on Instagram (Tabelog). Bookings taken; the small team may not always answer the phone (Tabelog). Service charge: Tabelog's Japanese original says 「なし」 (none). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and…

places.hood: Higashinotoin-Shichijo, 3 min walk north of Kyoto Station
places.cu: Casual French bistro, the origin of the 大衆酒場フレンチマン bars (Tabelog) · signature cold pasta with sea urchin and salmon roe (Tabelog) · courses with all-you-can-drink ¥6,000 and ¥8,000: assorted appetisers, fish carpaccio, seasonal soup, fish, meat and dessert (April–October 2026) · weekend lunch course with a drink ¥4,400: five appetisers (pâté, frittata, carrot râpée, red cabbage), sea-bream carpac…
places.notes: [Bistro · Higashinotoin by Kyoto Station, casual French with free-flow] A lively second-floor bistro a few minutes from Kyoto Station — the original of the local French Man bar group — with no dress code and a counter facing the kitchen. Courses with all-you-can-drink run ¥6,000–8,000; à la carte stars include taro and blue-cheese gratin and a foie-gras porcini risotto. Busy and noisy at peak, and staff adapt dishes on request. Closed Monday; weekend lunch by reservation.
places.chef: Chef not named; operated by 有限会社らくちん (Kyoto; representative 渡辺 哲也) · Opened 13 July 2015 (Tabelog). Tabelog’s introduction calls it a bistro tucked into a corner of a building near Kyoto Station, French-centred but free of dress codes and table manners, and the origin of 大衆酒場フレンチマン. Per the company page: 有限会社らくちん, founded 2001, runs izakaya, yakiniku, yakitori, French and Thai concepts — 11 shops (8 direct, 3 franchised) — and opened its first 大衆酒場フレンチマン in Osaka in 2020. · The shop’s motto (Tabelog; company page): life is a way to pass the time — who will you spend it with, and doing what? · Cold pasta with sea urchin and salmon roe.
places.gfd: Ask. Bistro plates — pâté, carpaccio, gratins, risotto, pasta, roast meats — and courses; no gluten information is published, though staff swapped a course dish on request (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a meat- and seafood-led bistro (Tabelog; reviews).
places.hours: Dinner 17:00–23:00 (last food order 22:00, drinks 22:30) Tuesday–Sunday; lunch 11:30–14:00 on Saturday, Sunday and holidays, by reservation only; closed Monday (Tabelog). Call after 16:00 to book; tables limited to 3 hours when busy (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). 18 seats with a counte…

places.hood: Kawaramachi-Marutamachi, south-east of the Imperial Palace — 7 min walk from Jingu-Maruta…
places.cu: Spice curry built on off-spec vegetables that would otherwise be thrown away (official site) · butter-soy chicken curry, mild and the house standard; sesame tantan keema with soy meat, vegan and Sichuan-peppery; a monthly seasonal curry, e.g. Kochi ginger and spiced chicken bean keema (November 2026), sudachi and grilled salmon cream curry; mackerel miso and Kishu plum dashi curry (March 2025) (o…
places.notes: [Spice curry · Kawaramachi-Marutamachi, curry that rescues vegetables] A small, jazz-playing curry shop whose name comes from 日の目を見る, "to see the light of day": oversized or blemished vegetables that farms would discard ring every plate. Pick two or three curries — mild butter-soy chicken, a vegan sesame tantan keema, a monthly special — over turmeric rice, about ¥1,200–2,000. Open 11:00–22:00.
places.chef: Owner not named; a young owner (February 2025 review) · Per the official site: a spice-curry shop that cooks and sells vegetables of perfectly good quality that are discarded for being too big or slightly blemished — about 1.9 million tonnes a year in Japan — to make customers and growers happy; the name himeru (ひめる) shortens 日の目を見る, vegetables that would have been thrown away reaching the table. · Per the official site: to save vegetables that would be thrown away and make both customers and producers happy. · Butter-soy chicken curry.
places.gfd: Ask. Spice curries with turmeric rice and vegetable sides; one curry is butter-and-soy-sauce based; no gluten information is published (official site; reviews).
places.vgd: The sesame tantan keema curry is made vegan with soy meat (official site); the other curries use chicken, butter or fish, and cross-contact is not described.
places.hours: 11:00–22:00 (last order 21:00); the official site says closing days are irregular, Tabelog lists Tuesday as closed (official site; Tabelog). Bookings accepted online (official site). Order by smartphone QR code (December 2025–January 2026). Tabelog lists cards accepted; one January 2026 reviewer pa…

menu.en: Sesame tantan keema curry with soy meat (vegan)

places.n: おむらはうす 出町柳店 (Omura House Demachiyanagi)
places.hood: Demachiyanagi — 159 m from the station
places.cu: Creative Kyoto-style omurice, the first omurice specialist in Kyoto (official site) · three LL Sakura eggs per serving over rice cooked with 30% pressed barley, with sweet Awaji onions and celery (official site) · tororo-yuba omurice over hijiki rice with dashi sauce and wasabi, the most popular, ¥2,000; hayashi with melting cheese ¥1,600; chicken ¥1,300; curry, Japanese-style (wild vegetables, m…
places.notes: [Omurice · Demachiyanagi, Kyoto's original omurice specialist] A cosy, Beatles-playing omurice house by Demachiyanagi with long lunch queues. Each plate uses three eggs over barley rice; the favourite is silky tororo-yuba on hijiki rice with dashi and wasabi (¥2,000), alongside hayashi with cheese and a dozen more (¥1,300–2,000). No bookings; cards and QR. Closed Monday.
places.chef: Owner not named; a former itamae (official site) · Per the official site: Kyoto’s first omurice specialist, opened by an omurice-loving owner who found none to suit and drew on experience as an itamae; every sauce is handmade; three LL Sakura eggs per plate, barley rice and Awaji onions; sister shops are おむらはうす 金閣寺店 and おむら家 百万遍店. A May 2026 reviewer gives the opening year as 1994. · Per the official site: good ingredients make good food — care over rice and eggs, all sauces made by hand. · Tororo-yuba omurice.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: the rice is 30% pressed barley, and the shop says even the dressings contain wheat flour, so it may not be able to cater for a wheat allergy (official site).
places.vgd: Not vegan: omurice made with three eggs; butter is used in cooking (salad oil can be substituted); only the chicken rice and salads are egg-free (official site).
places.hours: 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:30) and 17:00–20:30 (last order 20:00); closed Monday, or Tuesday when Monday is a holiday (official site). Tabelog lists 11:00–14:30 and 17:00–20:00. No reservations — first come, first served; queues at lunch and at weekends (official site; several 2026 reviews). Cards,…

places.cu: Meat-led yoshoku set meals with vegetable sides, miso soup and rice (2026 reviews) · pork hamburg steak with almost no filler, firm like a large sausage, 150 g to 300 g, with ketchup or other sauces; beef hamburg (2026) · thick pork steak 250 g or 300 g with balsamic or garlic sauce; thick pork-loin cutlet cut, breaded and fried to order; bite-sized pork cutlets; fried prawns (2025–2026) · T-bone…
places.notes: [Yoshoku · Mototanaka near Kyoto University, a meat-lover's set-meal house] A converted house in the student quarter east of Mototanaka, serving generous, meat-first yoshoku: a pure-pork hamburg steak with almost no filler, firm as a big sausage; thick pork steaks with balsamic or garlic; slow-fried loin cutlets; even venison. Sets about ¥1,000–2,000, with sides, soup and rice. Expect a wait for fried dishes. Closed Sunday; Thursday lunch only.
places.chef: Owner not named · A neighbourhood yoshoku house in a residential street east of Mototanaka Station, with several reviewers on a 7th to 15th visit (2024–2026 reviews). · Filler-free pork hamburg steak; thick pork steak.
places.gfd: Ask. Breaded cutlets and fried prawns, sauced hamburg steaks and grilled pork, beef and venison steaks; no gluten information is published (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a meat-led yoshoku menu (Tabelog; reviews).
places.hours: Lunch 11:30–14:15 (Saturday from 11:00); dinner 17:30–21:00 Monday–Wednesday, Friday and Saturday; Thursday lunch only; closed Sunday; hours may change (Tabelog). Bookings accepted. Cards, e-money and PayPay (Tabelog). No service charge (Tabelog original text: なし). 20 seats: a 6-seat counter and ta…

places.n: 文の助茶屋 本店 (Fuminosuke Chaya Honten)
places.hood: Higashiyama, between Yasaka and Kiyomizu-dera — near Ninenzaka
places.cu: Old tea house of Japanese sweets, founded 1909 per 2026 reviews (1910 per a 2006 review) · warabi mochi of warabi starch and wasanbon with a hint of cinnamon and kinako, also to take away (2026 reviews) · anmitsu, matcha anmitsu with shiratama and matcha ice cream, mitarashi dango, tokoroten (2026 reviews) · zenzai: manpuku zenzai with chestnut and shiratama in winter, strawberry zenzai around Ne…
places.notes: [Japanese sweets · Higashiyama, on the way to Kiyomizu-dera] A long-established tea house in a renovated Kyoto house where you slip off your shoes for wobbly, cinnamon-scented warabi mochi, anmitsu, zenzai and summer kakigori, upstairs on tatami or by a little garden. Founded in the late Meiji era by a retired rakugo performer, per reviewers. Several 2026 reviewers note many tourists, including overseas visitors. Daytime only.
places.chef: Tea house staff (unnamed) · Per reviews: a tea house founded in 1909 (2026 reviews) — a 2006 reviewer gives 1910 and writes that it was started by a rakugo performer of the Katsura line after retiring from the stage, with amazake as the original specialty. Renovated before January 2026. Tabelog lists an online shop at ecstore.bunnosuke.jp and a JR Kyoto Isetan counter appears in our crawls. · Warabi mochi.
places.gfd: Ask. Warabi mochi of warabi starch and wasanbon sugar with kinako, zenzai, anmitsu and kakigori; mitarashi dango is glazed with a soy-based sauce; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Warabi mochi and zenzai look plant-based, but some sets come with matcha ice cream or soft serve; no ingredient information (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Daily 11:00–17:00; irregular closing days (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR (Tabelog). 28 seats; shoes off at the entrance; tables on the 1F, a tatami room upstairs and an engawa facing a small garden; non-smoking inside (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Kakigor…

places.n: 京都 たらこパスタ LABO (Kyoto Tarako Pasta LABO)
places.hood: Shijo Kawaramachi — 7F of Kawaramachi Garden, linked to Kawaramachi Stn
places.cu: Tarako pasta specialist with Hokkaido tarako and thick, chewy fresh pasta from Awaji, opened March 2026 as a sister of 京都北山洋食パセリカフェ (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · signature aburi tarako dashi spaghetti ¥1,485, topped with sesame, shibazuke and hijiki and finished with a pour of ago and kombu dashi (March and May 2026) · e.g. squid and tarako, root-vegetable kinpira, white miso and mushroom, citrus tar…
places.notes: [Pasta · Shijo Kawaramachi, tarako specialist] A small food-hall shop serving nothing but tarako pasta on chewy Awaji fresh noodles — try the aburi tarako dashi spaghetti, finished like ochazuke with a pour of dashi — plus a ¥1,380 lunch set. One April 2026 evening guest waited 40–50 minutes outside with half the seats empty for lack of staff; others found it average or a little pricey. Open all day.
places.chef: Kitchen and floor staff (unnamed) · Per the Kawaramachi Garden food hall page: a tarako pasta shop whose concept is creative tarako pasta and new ways to change its flavour (創作、味変と新しいたらこぱすたの楽しみ方). Opened 5 March 2026 (Tabelog). Reviewers in March–May 2026 call it a sister of 京都北山洋食パセリカフェ, which has a branch on the same floor. · Creative tarako pasta with flavour changes (food hall page). · Aburi tarako dashi spaghetti.
places.gfd: Not GF: fresh wheat pasta from Awaji in every dish (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: every pasta is made with tarako (cod roe), many with cream, cheese or dashi (2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Izakaya · Pontocho alley 15, since 1985] A tiny red-lantern izakaya down one of Pontocho's numbered alleys, run since 1985 and now by the second generation: home-style oden, dashimaki and yakitori with sansho, sake, and above all a chatty host and plenty of Pontocho stories. Opens at 16:15 for early drinks. Cash only; small appetizer charge.
places.chef: Owners (unnamed): a talkative host and a partner in the kitchen; second generation since July 2022 · Per Tabelog: an izakaya opened 2 March 1985; from July 2022 the second-generation proprietress has carried on the business. Reviewers describe a husband-and-wife team, the host chatting and the partner cooking (2012–2018, September 2025), and in November 2024 sister owners full of stories. · Oden; dashimaki.
places.gfd: Ask. Home-style izakaya food — oden, dashimaki, sashimi, yakitori with sansho, fried dishes, curry; no gluten information (2012–2025 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: oden in dashi, yakitori, sashimi and fried dishes (2012–2025 reviews).
places.hours: Monday–Wednesday and Friday–Sunday 16:15–22:00; Thursday 17:00–22:00; open on New Year's Eve (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Reviewers describe a warm master and many regulars (2024). · Omusoba; tonpei-yaki.

places.hood: Fuyacho south of Ayanokoji — 4 min walk from Kawaramachi Stn

Order and pay first; expect a queue at lunch. Staff lent ice packs and umbrellas to the summer line.

places.vgd: Ask. Burritos are packed with vegetables, beans and rice, and the menu lists every ingredient, but the classic has chicken; no vegan option confirmed (2026 reviews).

Hours vary — check Instagram. Closed Monday.

places.notes: [Yakiniku · Ayanokoji near Nishiki, good-value local grill] A spacious, clean yakiniku near the Shijo shops that locals rate for fair prices: salted tongue, outside skirt, kalbi and offal in half portions, yukhoe, the house oxtail soup and spicy bibim noodles to finish, with private rooms upstairs. 10% service in the private rooms. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Opened 18 March 2022 (Tabelog). places.cu: A small kappo counter in Gion since 1988, built on seasonal fish (Tabelog; 2017–2025 reviews) · omakase or à la carte; sashimi with bamboo shoots in spring, hamo in summer (otoshi and yakishimo, hamo nabe), matsutake in autumn, crab or fugu in winter (Tabelog; 2018–2025) · baby octopus, torigai, yellowtail shabu-shabu, ayu, ginkgo in soy, a large chawanmushi (2017–2025) · the suppon "maru-nabe" t…
places.notes: [Kappo · Gion south of Shijo, seasonal fish since 1988] A 15-seat kappo counter just south of Shijo, run since 1988 by a friendly owner-chef: seasonal sashimi, hamo in summer, matsutake in autumn, crab and fugu in winter, omakase or à la carte, finishing with a suppon maru-nabe. Fair prices for Gion, say reviewers. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: Owner-chef, not named in a source · Opened 20 September 1988 (Tabelog); per its Tabelog text, more than 34 years of kappo cooking that suggests the best way to enjoy each ingredient. Reviewers from 2017 to 2025 describe a friendly, experimenting chef who recommends sashimi without dipping sauce, care over tableware, and a cosy counter and tatami room. · From its Tabelog text: high-quality ingredients, served in the way that brings out their flavour. · Seasonal sashimi; suppon maru-nabe.

places.notes: [Bubble tea and crêpes · Kyoto Tower Sando food hall] A small stall in the food hall under Kyoto Tower, one of the few non-drinking stops down there: tapioca drinks with domestic pearls and homemade Assam milk tea or Kyoto matcha, plus chewy crêpes heaped with fruit and cream (about ¥700). Made to order, so allow a few minutes. Open daily 11:00–23:00.

places.notes: [Kakigori bar · Gojo-Omiya, savoury shaved ice] A chic townhouse bar near Gojo-Omiya shaving ice into unexpected savoury bowls — nikujaga over miso panna cotta, peach with cheese and grilled bacon, cream stew — alongside sweeter citrus-and-sansho or custard-strawberry ice, about ¥1,300–1,600, with cocktails. Reviewers (2025–2026) note it also offers lodging. Tabelog’s introduction: kakigori in a Kyoto townhouse — savoury ice, alcohol ice and seasonal fruit ice — with the day’s menu on Instagram. · Nikujaga kakigori.

places.notes: [Creative French · Higashinotoin near Shijo-Karasuma, a 1905 townhouse] Behind the SECOND HOUSE café, a long, quiet townhouse with a stone path, tatami, a storehouse room and a tea room, serving creative French courses with Japanese touches — sea bream with green-pea sauce, wagyu, pretty desserts — for about ¥4,000–6,500 at lunch, more at dinner. Shoes off; staff explain each dish. Closed Tuesday and the 2nd and 4th Wednesday.

Tabelog’s introduction: a 1905 Kyoto townhouse at Shijo-Karasuma blending Japanese and Western flavours at reasonable prices, courses at lunch and dinner. A September 2026 reviewer has come about five times in 20 years. · Per the operator’s site: handmade, warm cooking in relaxed spaces, every dish and shop made by hand. · Creative French courses in a townhouse.

places.chef: Owner not named · Per the official site: Kyoto’s first Thai-curry specialist, recognised in Thailand, with homemade curry pastes ground from fresh Thai herbs and made weekly to keep the aroma; it later opened the sister shop タイカレーラーメン専門店シャム (kyoto_thai_curry_ramen_siam in data); press in Amakara Techo, Mapple and Tabelog Best Restaurant 2009–2010. Reviewers (2025–2026) say it is Thai Select certified, and a September 2026 reviewer heard of a temporary closure to relocate in 2027. · Per the official site: an authentic taste that Thailand recognises — refreshing heat, mellow coconut milk, fruity sweetness and spice. · Green curry.

places.notes: [Nepalese curry · Ayanokoji near Kawaramachi, giant naan and a dog-friendly terrace] A bright Nepalese-run curry café a block from Kawaramachi: good-value lunch sets with chicken tikka, naan bigger than your plate from the tandoor, cheese naan, biryani and a vegetable curry, with five spice levels. Friendly staff are the most-praised thing here; some find the curries mild. Dogs welcome on the terrace. Cash only. Closed Monday.

Retty, Uber Eats and a Kyoto curry guide list it in Latin as "raicha Spice Cafe Restaurant"; Tabelog's English page renders the name "Righteous". Reviewers from 2021 to 2026 praise a Nepalese manager "fluent in Japanese" (May 2024), cheerful staff and tandoor-baked naan; a few found the curries milder than hoped (November 2022; September 2023). · Tandoor naan; spice curries.

Busy, with smoking allowed; service can lag at peak times, and the music is loud for some. ¥330 table charge. Open nightly to midnight.
places.chef: Not named in a source · Opened 1 May 2019 (Tabelog). Reviewers from 2024 to 2026 praise offal "without any unpleasant odor" (November 2024), a broth that is "not overly salty or heavy" (February 2025) and bright, quick staff (January 2025); criticism covers slow service in the year-end rush (December 2024), sukiyaki that was "somewhat average" (April 2025) and loud background music (February 2026). · Beef-offal motsu-nabe; Wagyu sukiyaki.

places.notes: [Kyoto kaiseki · Pontocho, Kamo River] A Pontocho kaiseki house of more than 120 years, now with its fourth-generation owner: tatami rooms over the Kamo River and a kawadoko deck in season, seasonal Kyoto courses, suppon hot pot and a riverside sukiyaki. About ¥10,000–15,000 at night. Closed Monday.

Hitosara describes it as a long-established ryotei whose specialty is suppon (soft-shell turtle), with kawadoko dining on the Kamo River. · Seasonal kaiseki of fine ingredients, with the river view (Tabelog). · Suppon nabe; seasonal kaiseki.

Quick and good value. Cash only; closed Monday.

places.notes: [Tempura · Kiyamachi-Sanjo counter] A small counter by the Kamo run by a couple, frying generous tendon to order: two big shrimp and vegetables with a soft egg, or the limited seafood bowl with an anago spilling over the rim. Light batter, free large rice and refills of miso soup and pickles, same price day and night. Closed Wednesday; no Thursday lunch.
places.chef: Chef and partner (couple, unnamed) · Per reviewers: a tempura counter of about eight seats on Kiyamachi run by a couple (September and October 2025), frying in oil blended by Yamanaka Aburaten, a Kyoto oil shop of nearly 200 years (August 2025), under a large painting by Daruma Shoten (May 2025). · Seafood tendon; special tendon.

places.hours: Monday, Tuesday and Friday–Sunday 11:30–14:30 and 17:00–20:30; Thursday 17:00–20:30; closed Wednesday (Tabelog). Same prices at lunch and dinner (August 2025). A sommelier picks wines (August 2026 review). · Creative Italian small plates with wine.

places.vgd: Not vegan: caviar, horse tartare, lamb tsukune, pork ragù pizza (2025–26 reviews).

places.n: 肉菓子 かぎりなき福 (KAGIRINAKIFUKU)

places.cu: "Meat confectionery": slightly sweet mochi daifuku filled with savoury meat — 牛しぐれ ¥600, 鶏てり ¥550, 豚しょうが ¥550, a set of three ¥1,700, six ¥3,400 (own store); earlier ¥550, ¥450 and ¥500 (2025 reviews); best warmed for about 20 seconds in a microwave (July 2025); a standing counter for shigure soba with beef (Tabelog)

places.vgd: Not vegan: beef, pork and chicken fillings (own store; 2025–26 reviews).

Takeaway, eat-in and delivery; frozen gift boxes by mail (Tabelog; own store; December 2025 review). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking; dogs welco…

places.n: 焼鳥 かなざわ 六角店 (Yakitori Kanazawa Rokkaku)

places.notes: [Yakitori · Rokkaku] A tiny 11-seat yakitori counter near Shinkyogoku grilling Kyoto red jidori over binchotan, mostly with salt; omakase sets of skewers, and rice bowls at midday. Third shop of a Yamashina yakitori. About ¥3,000–5,000.
places.chef: Opened 1 September 2016 as the third shop of 焼鳥かなざわ of Yamashina (Tabelog). A man grilling with two young staff (September 2021 review); a friendly owner (July 2022 review). · Morning-fresh Kyo Akajidori, raised about 150 days on pesticide-free feed, over Kishu binchotan (Tabelog). · Salt-grilled Kyo Akajidori.

places.vgd: Not vegan: chicken yakitori, wagyu and pork skewers (2019–2026 reviews).

places.notes: [Fugu · Kiyamachi by the Takase, since 1949] A third-generation fugu restaurant on the Takase river near Gojo bridge, with a counter for solo diners and private rooms: tessa sashimi with house daidai ponzu, kara-age, rare grilled fugu and tecchiri hot pot finished as zosui — the full course ¥11,000 — plus shirako in winter and hire-zake. No service charge.
places.chef: 上田 路実 (reading not sourced) · Owner (the invoice holder) · Tabelog’s shop text says the restaurant was founded in 1949 and has served fugu for three generations. Tabelog’s invoice number T8810003331402 is registered to an individual, 上田 路実 (NTA register). · Fugu is rested for over half a day after preparing to bring out its taste; reservations let the shop time its buying and preparation (Tabelog). · Grilled fugu; tecchiri.
places.gfd: Ask. Fugu sashimi with house ponzu, fugu kara-age, grilled fugu, hot pot and zosui; no gluten information (Tabelog).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a fugu restaurant — sashimi, fried, grilled and hot-pot fugu, shirako (Tabelog).
places.hours: 17:00–22:00 daily (L.O. food 21:00, drinks 21:30); closed on irregular days, and may close over New Year and in summer (Tabelog). places.chef: Head chef (unnamed) · Tabelog’s shop text describes a relaxed, homely place known for good, reasonably priced Kyoto food. An October 2025 regular, back after six years, was glad to see the same head chef. · Kyoto dishes that bring out the ingredients with plenty of dashi, served without pretension (Tabelog). · Kyoto courses with sake.
places.gfd: Ask. Kyoto courses built on rich dashi, with seasonal vegetables and fish; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: the cooking is built on dashi, with fish in the courses (Tabelog).

One course per person; closed Sunday.

A February 2026 diner saw the chef working solo without a break. · Edomae sushi omakase.

places.vgd: Not vegan: a sushi omakase of fish and seafood (Tabelog; February 2026).

À la carte at the counter, omakase courses in the tatami rooms upstairs. Coperto ¥880 plus 10% service; closed Sunday.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed), described as warm (August 2025) · Per Tabelog and the official site: a Western-style kappo based on Italian and French cooking, opened in May 2010 in a building that keeps the front of a former Miyagawacho teahouse. · Seasonal seafood, and domestic vegetables and meat wherever possible (Tabelog). · Italian–French dishes à la carte; pasta to finish.
places.gfd: Ask. À la carte seafood, meat and vegetables, with pasta to finish (official site; 2025–26 reviews); no gluten information. The chef adapts dishes to requests (August 2025; September 2026).
places.vgd: Ask. Seafood and meat lead, but seasonal vegetables are a focus and the chef cooks to request (official site; August 2025); no vegan information.

places.notes: [Sushi kappo · opposite Kyoto Ebisu Shrine] A long-running local sushi kappo on Yamato-oji, away from the tourist stretch, packed at lunch for a ¥2,500 set of small dishes, fresh tempura, nigiri and red miso soup. In the evening, a casual course around ¥4,300 or à la carte: hamo in season, miso dengaku, whale bacon, simmered whelk. Book ahead; closed Wednesday and Thursday.
places.chef: Per Tabelog and reviews: a sushi kappo on Yamato-oji south of Shijo, opposite Kyoto Ebisu Shrine, reviewed since 2008. · Hamo; sushi lunch sets.

places.vgd: Not vegan: sushi, hamo, whale bacon, dashi oden and red miso soup with clams (2025–26 reviews).

places.cu: Kyoto home-style dishes à la carte or as a course, with a strong sake list (2024–25 reviews) · baked tomato with cream cheese, grilled Kamo eggplant with miso, chilled ume mush, grilled tororo, chicken thigh with daikon sauce, salt-grilled flatfish, sashimi (September 2023) · ¥6,500 course with simmered vegetables and chawanmushi (February 2024) · braised beef tendon with red konnyaku, mentaiko o…
places.notes: [Kyoto home cooking and sake · Gion south] A long-loved house restaurant just off Hanamikoji with a counter and tatami rooms, serving gently seasoned Kyoto dishes — braised beef tendon, the signature grilled yam, sashimi platters, nama-fu dengaku, seasonal fish — with a deep sake list until 23:00. À la carte or courses; cash only; closed Tuesday.
places.chef: Per Tabelog and reviews: a Japanese restaurant in a house on the south side of Gion, reviewed since at least 2018; one January 2025 diner was returning after 15 years. · Grilled yam; sashimi platters; Kyoto home-style dishes with sake.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: tempura, nama-fu and tea soba appear on the menu (2025 reviews); dashi and soy throughout.
places.vgd: Not vegan: sashimi, beef tendon, mentaiko omelette and dashi-simmered dishes (2024–25 reviews).

places.cu: Kyoto kaiseki from a head chef with 30 years in Japanese cuisine: firefly-squid shabu-shabu in summer, fugu in winter, duck hot pot all year, hamo shabu-shabu and hamo kaiseki June to September; Hana course of 13 dishes ¥9,000, Moon course of 12 dishes ¥6,300; a vegetarian course (Tabelog) · ¥5,000 course with hamachi sashimi and tempura (August 2023) · hamo kaiseki: hamo hot pot with mizuna and …
places.notes: [Kyoto kaiseki · Bukkoji, since 2018] A quiet Kyoto-cuisine restaurant near Shijo-Karasuma with a counter and private rooms, popular for business lunches and groups: hamo kaiseki in summer, fugu in winter, duck hot pot year-round, and good-value lunch sets from soba to the ¥2,500 Miyabi. A vegetarian course on request. No service charge.
places.chef: Head chef (unnamed), 30 years in Japanese cuisine (Tabelog), Owner (unnamed), described as warm (October 2026) · Per Tabelog: a Kyoto-cuisine restaurant opened in March 2018 whose head chef has 30 years of experience in Japanese cooking, sourcing seasonal ingredients from across the country. · Seasonal kaiseki; hamo and duck hot pots.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: tempura in courses and lunch sets, and soba set meals at lunch (2023–25 reviews).

places.hours: Daily 11:00–14:00 (last order 13:30) and 17:00–22:00 (last order 21:30); closing days may vary (Tabelog). places.chef: Chef (husband), Front of house (wife) · Per Tabelog: a cosy, glass-fronted restaurant down a side street by a hair salon at Fuyacho-Sanjo, run by a husband-and-wife team and designed to welcome solo diners; opened 7 September 2011. · Dishes that bring out the best of the ingredients (Tabelog). · Kujo-negi and salsiccia pizza.

Reviewers note that the Marutamachi soba-boro maker has closed, leaving this house among the makers of the Kyoto classic (2025–2026). The company also runs the soba restaurant 晦庵 河道屋 (kawamichiya.co.jp). · Soba houru (buckwheat biscuits).

places.notes: [Dining bar · Shijo-Karasuma, a basement hideaway] A busy basement dining bar a few minutes from Shijo station: playful creative small plates — smoked snacks, Kyoto vegetables — a long drinks list, and late hours to 1 am. Counter, kotatsu tables; no table charge; smoking allowed.
places.chef: Not named · A dining bar reviewed since 2014 (Tabelog). Reviewers (2024–2026) describe a hidden basement spot that fills quickly, with a menu that has barely changed over the years. · Creative bar plates; smoked snacks.
places.gfd: Ask. Creative izakaya dishes, smoked snacks and set lunches with soy and miso; no gluten information is published (reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. Kyoto-vegetable dishes are on the menu, but most are with meat, fish or dashi (reviews).
places.hours: 18:00–01:00 (last food order 23:30, drinks 00:30) Monday–Saturday (Tabelog); Sunday is not stated. A weekday lunch was served in December 2024; lunch is not in Tabelog’s hours. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money; no service or table charge (Tabelog). 33 seats: an 8-seat counter, th…

places.hood: Gion, south of Shijo
places.cu: Seasonal Japanese cooking at an eight-seat counter, seasoned by subtraction to let ingredients speak (February 2026) · a small hot pot with hana-sansho; well-cooked meat (May 2025) · squid with canola flowers and sansho; sea bream and akagai sashimi; matsuba crab sashimi; nodoguro shabu-shabu (March 2026) · about ¥20,000–40,000 a head (2025–2026)
places.notes: [Kappo · Gion south of Shijo, eight-seat counter] An intimate eight-seat counter where a smiling, bow-tied chef lets top ingredients speak with minimal seasoning — matsuba crab sashimi, nodoguro shabu-shabu, a hot pot with hana-sansho. About ¥20,000–40,000; from 7 pm.
places.chef: Chef not named · Reviewers (2025–2026) describe a bow-tied chef with a ready smile, humble and charming, cooking live at the counter in a stylish, calm room. · Seasonal kappo.
places.gfd: Ask. Seasonal kappo with dashi and soy, sashimi and shabu-shabu; no gluten information is published (reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: courses of crab, fish and meat (reviews).
places.hours: 19:00–24:00; closing days vary (Tabelog). Cards and e-money accepted (Tabelog). An 8-seat counter; non-smoking, with a smoking area (Tabelog). On Gion-machi Minamigawa south of Shijo (Tabelog). About ¥20,000–40,000 a head (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

places.hood: Gion, north of Shijo
places.cu: Omakase sushi from two brothers trained in Tokyo, fish chosen at market each morning (May 2026) · special omakase with uni and caviar ¥15,000: appetizers, sashimi, seasonal dishes such as an uni “cocktail”, 8–10 nigiri and soup; crab can replace uni (May 2026) · sake pairing ¥4,500 by a sake sommelier; Kyoto sake and wine (April and May 2026)
places.notes: [Sushi · Gion north of Shijo, brothers’ omakase] A sleek ten-seat counter opened in November 2025 by two Tokyo-trained brothers who speak English and Spanish: a ¥15,000 omakase with uni and caviar, 8–10 nigiri, and a ¥4,500 sake pairing from a sake sommelier. Gluten-free requests accommodated, per a review — ask when booking.
places.chef: Two brothers, sushi chefs (not named) · Opened in November 2025 (Tabelog) by two brothers who trained at a well-known Tokyo sushi restaurant and speak English and Spanish; one is a sake sommelier (April and May 2026 reviews). · Sushi omakase with sake pairing.
places.gfd: Ask. An April 2026 reviewer says the brothers accommodate gluten-free requests; mention it when booking, as soy sauce and seasonings are not otherwise described (review B525889708).
places.vgd: Not vegan: a sushi omakase (reviews).
places.hours: 16:00–23:00 (last food order 21:00, drinks 22:00) Monday–Saturday, holidays, holiday eves and the day after a holiday (Tabelog); Sunday is not stated. Course only (April 2026). Cards (incl. UnionPay); no e-money (Tabelog). A 10-seat counter; non-smoking (Tabelog). Prime Building 2F, Gion-machi Kita…

places.hood: Nijo-dori east of Kawabata — 8 min from Keihan Sanjo
places.cu: The grocery café of the Italian restaurant cenci: buy its sauces, oils, cheeses and sweets, or eat risotto, lasagna and desserts at one shared table (Tabelog; 2022–2025 reviews) · lotus-root Bolognese risotto with a soup of the day (Jerusalem artichoke, corn) (2025–2026); herb-sausage, lotus-root and shiitake risotto (January 2025) · lasagna; Gobal basil sausage with mashed potato and takana must…
places.notes: [Grocery café · Kawabata-Nijo, cenci's shop and table] The bright grocery shop of the acclaimed Italian restaurant cenci: browse its pantry goods, then sit at the one big table for a generous risotto, lasagna or cacao chiffon with coffee or natural wine. An avocado sandwich has been labelled vegan. About ¥1,500–3,000. Closed Mon and Tue.
places.chef: A shop run by the Italian restaurant cenci (kyoto_cenci_shogoin in this guide), selling the ingredients, sauces and sweets used there; a December 2025 reviewer calls it cenci's second shop. A November 2023 visitor from Tokyo was served by the wife of cenci's chef Sakamoto, who opened on a closed day for her. A December 2022 reviewer credits the cacao chiffon to cenci's pâtissier Nakatsuka. · cenci's risottos, sauces and cacao sweets.
places.gfd: Ask. No gluten information. Risottos are rice-based, but the menu also has lasagna, sandwiches, chiffon and lemon cakes and granola (2023–2025 reviews).
places.vgd: Ask. An April 2024 reviewer had an avocado sandwich labelled vegan; most other dishes use cheese, cream, eggs, sausage or meat sauce.
places.hours: Tabelog: Wed–Sun 11:00–19:00 (food L.O. 17:00); closed Monday and Tuesday. No reservations. Mainly a grocery shop selling ingredients, sauces, frozen risottos and sweets from the Italian restaurant cenci, with eat-in at one table for about 6–7 (2023–2024 reviews). Cards and e-money. places.hood: Gojo-Rakuen, near the Ume-yu bathhouse — 7 min from Kiyomizu-Gojo
places.cu: A new late-night neighbourhood Chinese diner (opened 17 March 2026) from the owner of the café "Kissa Jani", in a renovated old house (Tabelog; 2026 reviews) · nira soba ¥950: noodles buried in chopped garlic chives with egg yolk and chashu, on Teikoku flat noodles (March–November 2026) · special chuka soba ¥1,000 in clear chicken broth (March 2026) · gyoza with homemade chili oil; shrimp-paste a…
places.notes: [Neighbourhood Chinese · Gojo-Rakuen, a late-night machi-chuka] A buzzy, nostalgic-style Chinese diner in an old house near the Ume-yu bathhouse, open to midnight: heaps-of-chives nira soba, gyoza with house chili oil, tomato-egg stir-fry and chili-shrimp fried rice, many in small portions. One drink each required. About ¥2,000–3,500. Some dishes run salty. Closed Sunday.
places.chef: Owner (unnamed; also runs Kissa Jani) · Opened 17 March 2026 (March 2026 review). A May 2026 reviewer writes that the owner of the popular Gojo café "Kissa Jani" opened it in a renovated old house, recreating an old-style neighbourhood Chinese diner, and that older regulars from the nearby bathhouse drop in for gyoza and beer. A November 2026 diner counted a staff of four. · Nira soba; gyoza; late-night Chinese plates.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles (nira soba, chuka soba, tantanmen), gyoza, spring rolls, fried bread and soy-based sauces (2026 reviews).
places.vgd: Not vegan: chicken-and-pork broths, chashu, gyoza, shrimp and pork dishes; even the fried eggplant comes from a meat-heavy kitchen (2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: Mon–Sat and public holidays 15:00–24:00 (L.O. food 23:00, drinks 24:00); closed Sunday; hours may change. October 2026 reviewers came at lunch for a newly added lunch set (ramen and a mini chashu bowl), so check Instagram for lunch days. Charge: 「無し、ただしワンドリンク必須（＝フードのみの利用不可）」 (no charge, bu…

places.hood: Off Matsubara-dori east of Shinmachi — 440 m from Gojo
places.cu: A handmade-soba izakaya down an alley off Matsubara-dori: thin, firm ni-hachi soba and, at night, charcoal yakitori with sake and soba shochu (Tabelog; 2022–2026 reviews) · zaru soba ¥1,080 with green onion and real wasabi (December 2025); grated-daikon soba ¥1,100 (September 2022) · duck and leek soba with a warm dipping broth; tempura rice bowl (December 2025) · chicken nanban soba; soba with c…
places.notes: [Soba izakaya · Matsubara-Shinmachi, handmade soba and yakitori] A lantern-lit alley doorway leads to a roomy, regular-filled soba house: start with a drink and charcoal yakitori, then finish with crisp ni-hachi zaru soba (¥1,080) or duck soba. About ¥3,000–5,000 at night. Evenings only; closed Sundays. Can be slow when busy.
places.chef: Reviewers describe a shop full of regulars and kind staff — one lent a guest an umbrella in the rain (May 2022) — with soba made on site in a visible soba-making room (December 2025). One March 2026 diner waited over 30 minutes for food; others find it a little pricey but worth it. · Handmade ni-hachi soba; charcoal yakitori.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: the soba is ni-hachi — 80% buckwheat, 20% wheat flour (December 2024, December 2025) — plus tempura bowls and soy-based dipping sauce.
places.vgd: Not vegan: soba in broth or with dipping sauce, chicken nanban soba, duck soba, oyakodon and charcoal yakitori (2022–2026 reviews); no vegan information.
places.hours: Tabelog: Mon–Sat 17:30–22:00 (L.O. 21:30), open on public holidays; closed Sunday, the 3rd Monday and the 5th Saturday of the month; closes early when the soba sells out; occasional temporary closures. 2022 reviewers ate weekday lunch here, but current Tabelog hours are evenings only. Reservations …

places.hood: Yanagibanba-Nijo — 6 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae
places.cu: A teppanyaki restaurant in a converted house cooking Miyazaki beef in front of you, with courses ending in temari sushi or garlic rice and a much-loved French toast (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews) · lunch course ¥3,500: appetizer tataki, onion soup, ankake, chicken-thigh steak, temari sushi, French toast and tea (February 2025) · lunch with 60–80 g of Miyazaki beef from about ¥4,000 (November 2024) …
places.notes: [Teppanyaki · Yanagibanba-Nijo, Miyazaki beef in a townhouse] A calm house-turned-teppan bar where the chef grills Miyazaki beef and seasonal fish at the counter, finishing with temari sushi or garlic rice and a famous French toast. Lunch courses from ¥3,500, dinner about ¥10,000. Free message plates for celebrations. Closed Wednesday.
places.chef: Reviewers describe a hidden teppan restaurant in a private house, with a 1st-floor counter and 2nd-floor tables (November 2024), chefs who explain each dish (February 2025) and regulars who return every year for birthdays. One April 2025 diner found the temari sushi bland and hoped the service would match the food. · Miyazaki beef teppanyaki; French toast.
places.gfd: Not gluten-free: teppan courses end with French toast, and include soups, a seafood foil bake and Japanese-style ankake (2024–2026 reviews); no gluten information.
places.vgd: Not vegan: Miyazaki beef and jidori chicken teppanyaki courses with sea bream, seafood and roast beef (2024–2026 reviews).
places.hours: Tabelog: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 11:30–15:00 (L.O. food 14:00) and 17:30–22:00 (L.O. food 21:00); closed Wednesday. Reservations taken; message plates for celebrations free on request (March 2026). Lunch courses about ¥3,500–4,000+; dinner courses around ¥10,000. 24 seats: counter on the 1st floor, table…
